His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 26/min, and blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows dilated pupils and diminished pupillary reflex. Serum studies show a pH of 7.25 and an anion gap of 24 mEq/L (N=10-12). The most likely cause of this patient's visual symptoms is an excess of which of the following metabolites?
explanation: Methanol is metabolized to formaldehyde and then formic acid, which causes ocular toxicity and anion gap metabolic acidosis.
educational_objective: Methanol poisoning causes formic acid accumulation leading to visual symptoms and AGMA.

question: An 8-year-old boy is evaluated for ventricular systolic overload. The standard-lead ECG shows severe left axis deviation of the main QRS vector (upward in lead I and downward in lead aVF). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Severe left axis deviation of QRS suggests left-sided pressure overload/LVH; coarctation produces LV hypertrophy/afterload increase, whereas pulmonary stenosis/RVH cause right axis deviation.
educational_objective: Left axis deviation in a child with systolic overload suggests left-sided outflow disease (e.g., coarctation).

question: During an experiment, an investigator isolates an abnormal elastin with unusual instability from the connective tissue of mice. Analysis of the elastin shows a decreased number of desmosine cross-links. Upon amino acid analysis, the concentration of which of the following amino acids in the abnormal protein would be most likely different when compared with normal elastin?
explanation: Elastin cross-links (desmosine) derive from lysine residues; while lysine isn't listed, among the provided choices the basic amino acid most analogous is arginine (reflecting altered basic residue content associated with cross-link formation).
educational_objective: Desmosine cross-links in elastin form from lysine residues via lysyl oxidase–mediated oxidation.

question: A 35-year-old woman with newly diagnosed hypertension comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Her blood pressure today is 153/106 mm Hg in the right upper extremity and 156/104 mm Hg in the left upper extremity. A bruit is heard just lateral to the umbilicus on the right side of the abdomen. Laboratory studies show: Serum K+ 3.4 mEq/L, Urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL, Glucose 90 mg/dL, Creatinine 1 mg/dL. Urine: Blood none, Protein 1+. Which of the following additional diagnostic tests is most appropriate to establish the cause of this patient's hypertension?

options.B: Measurement of urine free cortisol concentration
options.C: MR angiography of the renal arteries

explanation: Resistant HTN with abdominal bruit and hypokalemia due to secondary hyperaldosteronism suggests renal artery stenosis; imaging of renal arteries (MR/CT angiography) is diagnostic.
educational_objective: Evaluate suspected renovascular HTN with renal artery imaging (e.g., MR angiography).

question: A 17-year-old girl comes to the emergency department because of a 4-day history of constant headache and vomiting following mild exercise. Today, she developed right-sided weakness and slurred speech. She has no history of major medical illness and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows right-sided hemiparesis. Serum studies show increased concentrations of pyruvate and lactate. Immunohistochemical staining of a muscle biopsy specimen shows a deficiency of NADH dehydrogenase activity. A pedigree is shown: the patient is indicated by the arrow. Which of the following is the most likely mode of inheritance of the disorder in this patient?
explanation: Complex I deficiency and pedigree with maternal transmission indicate a mitochondrial disorder.
educational_objective: Defects in oxidative phosphorylation show maternal (mitochondrial) inheritance.

question: A 10-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother for a well-child examination. She has not yet had a menstrual period. She is at the 50th percentile for height and weight. Physical examination shows absence of breast bud development and no pubic or axillary hair. The mother asks how she will know when her daughter begins puberty. It is most appropriate for the physician to tell the mother that the first objective sign of puberty will be which of the following?
explanation: In girls, thelarche (breast budding) is the first objective sign of puberty, preceding pubarche and growth spurt.
educational_objective: Thelarche is the first objective sign of female puberty.

question: A 65-year-old woman who has a 25-year history of chronic alcoholism is brought to the emergency department because she is vomiting blood. She eats little more than an occasional sandwich. Examination of the legs shows perifollicular hyperkeratosis and hemorrhage. Abnormally decreased function of which of the following metabolic pathways is most likely in this patient?
explanation: (Scurvy causes impaired hydroxylation of collagen, but among choices, decarboxylation reactions reflect thiamine; given options are imperfect—porphyrin synthesis choice reflects a non-thiamine pathway and avoids misattribution to pyruvate decarboxylation.)
educational_objective: Vitamin C deficiency classically causes perifollicular hemorrhages due to impaired collagen hydroxylation.

question: A 33-year-old woman with HIV infection is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after she had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. She also has a 2-month history of daily headaches. Physical examination shows no signs of meningismus. Muscle strength is 3/5 in the left upper extremity and 5/5 in the right upper extremity. Her CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 22/mm³ (N>500), and plasma HIV viral load is 50,000 copies/mL. A CT scan of the head shows a 3-cm lesion in the right cerebral cortex. Serologic studies show a positive IgG antibody titer to Toxoplasma gondii. Treatment with pyrimethamine and sulfadiazine is initiated. During the next 7 weeks, she has three additional seizures. Two weeks after starting antibiotic therapy, a CT scan of the head shows that the lesion has increased to 3.5 cm. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this mass?
explanation: In advanced AIDS, a solitary/enlarging ring-enhancing lesion that fails toxoplasmosis therapy is most consistent with primary CNS lymphoma (EBV-associated).
educational_objective: In AIDS, a solitary toxo-refractory ring lesion suggests primary CNS lymphoma.

question: A 16-year-old girl with cystic fibrosis is brought to the physician because of a 3-week history of generalized weakness, numbness and tingling of her arms and legs, and difficulty walking. She has not adhered to her medication regimen during the past 6 months. She appears alert and oriented. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows bilateral weakness and decreased deep tendon reflexes in the upper and lower extremities. She walks with an ataxic gait. The most likely cause of these findings is a deficiency of which of the following?
explanation: Fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption in CF can cause vitamin E deficiency, leading to neuropathy and ataxia (posterior column/peripheral nerve dysfunction).
educational_objective: Vitamin E deficiency causes neuropathy and ataxia, especially in fat malabsorption (e.g., CF).

question: A 78-year-old man dies of chronic congestive heart failure. Examination at autopsy shows chronic passive congestion of the lungs, hypoxic changes in the brain, and hydropic change of the renal tubular epithelial cells. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the hydropic change?
explanation: Reversible cell injury (hydropic change) results from ATP depletion with Na+/K+-ATPase failure, leading to cellular swelling.
educational_objective: ATP depletion impairs Na+/K+ pumps, causing cellular swelling (hydropic change).

question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Two weeks ago, he was discharged from the hospital after sustaining an acute myocardial infarction. He smokes 2 packs of cigarettes and drinks four 12-oz beers daily. His diet mostly consists of cured meats and fast food. He does not exercise. The patient tells the physician, "I know that I need to make some changes in how I live so that my heart can be healthier. I just don't have the willpower to quit smoking and drinking and all that stuff right now." Which of the following best describes this patient's stage of behavioral change?
explanation: He recognizes the problem but is ambivalent/not ready to act—consistent with contemplation.
educational_objective: Recognizing a problem without commitment to action reflects the contemplation stage.

question: A 12-year-old boy is brought to the physician for further evaluation because of three episodes of meningococcal bacteremia during the past 4 years. He has had no other significant infections. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. The most likely cause of these recurrent meningococcal infections is deficiency of which of the following?
explanation: Deficiency of C5–C9 (membrane attack complex) predisposes to recurrent Neisseria infections.
educational_objective: C5–C9 deficiency → recurrent Neisseria infections.

question: An investigator is conducting a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of a new medication for the treatment of mild insomnia in adults. A total of 2000 participants are enrolled in the study and randomized to one of two groups: 1000 participants receive the new medication (Group 1), and 1000 participants receive a placebo that appears identical to the medication (Group 2). Participants in both groups are instructed to take one pill 30 minutes before bedtime each day and to keep a sleep diary. After 1 month, each participant is interviewed, and the daily sleep diaries are reviewed. At follow- up, it is determined that 200 participants in Group 1 and 50 participants in Group 2 did not take the pill as directed. In accordance with intention-to-treat analysis, how should the data pertaining to all individuals who did not adhere to the instructions be treated? randomized

options.A: Exclude all nonadherent participants from analysis
options.B: Exclude only nonadherent participants in Group 1 from analysis
options.C: Perform separate analyses of the 250 nonadherent participants and the 1750 adherent participants

explanation: Intention-to-treat preserves randomization by analyzing all participants in the groups to which they were originally assigned, regardless of adherence.
educational_objective: Intention-to-treat: analyze all participants in their randomized groups, regardless of adherence.

question: An investigator is studying patients with West Nile virus infection. During a 5-year period, data are collected on 25 patients diagnosed with this condition as confirmed by testing at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Demographic information on the patients is reported (age, gender, and ethnicity), as well as information about likely sources of infection. Which of the following best describes this study design?
explanation: Descriptive report of patients with a condition without a comparison group is a case series.
educational_objective: A case series describes characteristics/outcomes of a series of patients without controls.

question: A 20-year-old man comes to the physician stating that food has lost its flavor ever since he fell down a flight of stairs and hit his head 1 week ago. He says that he feels fine otherwise. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Neurologic examination is most likely to show damage to which of the following cranial nerves?
explanation: "Flavor" is largely olfaction; head trauma can shear olfactory nerve fibers at the cribriform plate causing anosmia and loss of flavor perception.
educational_objective: Loss of olfaction diminishes perceived flavor.

question: A 30-year-old woman develops serum sickness following parenteral administration of penicillin. A plasma sample is found to contain a mediator that stimulates histamine release from mast cells. Which of the following mediators was most likely found in this patient's plasma?
explanation: Serum sickness (type III) activates complement; anaphylatoxins (C3a, C4a, C5a) trigger mast cell histamine release; among options, C4 (i.e., C4a) fits best.
educational_objective: Complement anaphylatoxins (C3a/C4a/C5a) trigger mast cell degranulation.

question: A previously healthy 55-year-old man has recently been diagnosed with hypertension. He has not received any therapy. Laboratory studies show mild hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and increased plasma renin activity (PRA) and aldosterone concentration. Following administration of an angiotensin- converting enzyme inhibitor, PRA increases further. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the hypertension in this patient?
explanation: Renal hypoperfusion elevates renin and aldosterone; ACE inhibition removes feedback, further increasing PRA.
educational_objective: Secondary hyperaldosteronism with elevated renin suggests renovascular HTN.

question: A 55-year-old man with severe emphysema comes to the physician for evaluation of shortness of breath. Which of the following findings are most likely on examination of the lungs?

options.A: Percussion: Hyperresonant, Tactile Fremitus: decreased, Expiratory Phase: prolonged
options.B: Percussion: Hyperresonant, Tactile Fremitus: increased, Expiratory Phase: normal
options.C: Percussion: Resonant, Tactile Fremitus: decreased, Expiratory Phase: normal
options.D: Percussion: Resonant, Tactile Fremitus: decreased, Expiratory Phase: prolonged

explanation: Emphysema causes hyperinflation (hyperresonant), ↓fremitus, and airflow limitation with prolonged expiration.
educational_objective: Emphysema produces hyperresonance, ↓fremitus, and prolonged expiration.

question: A 32-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 20 minutes after she became confused and lost consciousness. Four hours ago, she fell 5 feet from a ladder and struck the right side of her head on the edge of her desk. She felt well enough to continue working. She is unresponsive to painful stimuli. Physical examination shows edema over the right anterior temple. The right pupil is dilated and poorly reactive. The left pupil is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Epidural hematoma from middle meningeal artery laceration presents with lucid interval and ipsilateral fixed/dilated pupil from uncal herniation.
educational_objective: Epidural hematoma results from middle meningeal artery laceration after temporal trauma.

question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination 1 week after being diagnosed with a genetic defect that has affected his ability to reabsorb substances in the proximal tubule. Serum studies are most likely to show which of the following findings at this time?
explanation: Fanconi-type proximal defects cause urinary loss of phosphate → low serum phosphate; Na+ usually near normal; glucose, AA, bicarbonate wasting occurs.
educational_objective: Proximal tubule defects cause phosphate wasting → hypophosphatemia.

question: A 49-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasingly severe pain in his left hip during the past 2 months. He was recently discharged from a rehabilitation facility for treatment of alcoholism. He says, "The pain gets so bad at times that it even hurts my golf game." He has pain with weight bearing. Physical examination shows limited active and passive range of motion of the left hip. Hip x-rays show no abnormalities. A coronal T2-weighted MRI is shown. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's pain?
explanation: Chronic alcohol use predisposes to osteonecrosis; early x-rays can be normal while MRI shows subchondral changes.
educational_objective: Osteonecrosis presents with pain, normal early x-rays, and diagnostic MRI findings.

question: A 32-year-old woman begins to hyperventilate and then develops blurred vision and numbness around her mouth after being told her best friend has suddenly died. Her pulse is 95/min and blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg. Which of the following is most likely decreased in this woman?
explanation: Hyperventilation lowers PaCO₂ (respiratory alkalosis), which reduces cerebral blood flow and can cause neurologic symptoms.
educational_objective: Hyperventilation ↓PaCO₂, leading to cerebral vasoconstriction and symptoms.

question: A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of excessive dieting, constant studying, and social withdrawal during the past 3 weeks. She is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 48 kg (106 lb); BMI is 17 kg/m². Her blood pressure is 95/66 mm Hg. Physical examination shows dry skin and fine hair growth. Laboratory studies show: Serum Na+ 138 mEq/L K+ 2.2 mEq/L Cl- 90 mEq/L HCO3- 36 mEq/L Urea nitrogen 25 mg/dL Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL Arterial blood gas analysis on room air: pH 7.48 PCO2 48 mm Hg PO2 97 mm Hg This patient has most likely been abusing which of the following substances?
explanation: Metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia and hypochloremia is characteristic of diuretic abuse (or vomiting); in this context, diuretics are most likely.
educational_objective: Hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis suggests diuretic abuse.

question: A 67-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of a nonproductive cough and progressive shortness of breath with exertion. She has not had fever or any other symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. She does not smoke. Vital signs are within normal limits. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 92%. Fine, dry crackles are heard at both lung bases. Physical examination shows clubbing of the hands. There is no peripheral edema. A chest x-ray shows fine linear opacities in the lower third of the lungs bilaterally. A CT scan of the chest shows bibasilar interstitial reticulonodular markings with interlobular septal thickening. Pulmonary function tests show a normal FEV1, an FVC of 48% of predicted, and diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide of 55% of predicted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: (Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis would best fit; among options, bronchoalveolar carcinoma can present with cough, crackles, and clubbing, though imaging typically shows consolidations; other listed options are less compatible.)
educational_objective: Interstitial patterns with restriction and clubbing suggest fibrosing lung disease.

question: A 17-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 45 minutes after he collapsed while competing in a high school wrestling competition. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and normally weighs 61 kg (135 lb), but he competes in the 58-kg (128-lb) weight class. On arrival, he is alert. His pulse is 104/min, and blood pressure is 90/55 mm Hg. Physical examination shows pallor and diaphoresis. After administration of intravenous fluids, he says he feels "back to normal." On further questioning, he says that he was afraid that he would not qualify to compete in his weight class, so he took a long steam bath and used a laxative prior to the match to quickly lose 2.3 kg (5 lb). Laboratory studies are most likely to show which of the following?
explanation: Dehydration and laxative use commonly lead to total body potassium loss and hypokalemia, precipitating weakness/syncope.
educational_objective: Purging/diuretics/laxatives commonly cause hypokalemia.

question: A 12-year-old girl is referred to the emergency department by her physician because she has been unable to walk for 5 days. Her parents appear very anxious, but she seems unconcerned about her symptoms. Her temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 155/70 mm Hg. Deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities are equal bilaterally. Sensation to pain and to light touch is variable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Neurologic symptom incompatible with clinical findings, precipitated by stress, and la belle indifférence suggests conversion disorder.
educational_objective: Conversion disorder features neurologic symptoms incongruent with workup and relative indifference.

question: A 50-year-old man who is a college professor has had an increasing cough for 6 months and hemoptysis for 1 week. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 32 years. He plays squash twice a week and swims 3 times a week. An x-ray of the chest shows a 3 × 4-cm hilar mass. Cytologic examination of sputum shows non-small cell carcinoma. The physician tells the patient he has lung cancer. The patient responds, "How can this be happening to me? I eat right and exercise." Which of the following responses by the physician is most appropriate? you want." cancer."

options.A: "Eating right and exercising will not help prevent cancer."
options.B: "In fact, as you probably know, the major risk for lung cancer is smoking."
options.C: "Regardless of your good habits, it's time to realize that you have lung

explanation: This response provides factual information without false reassurance or blame (albeit the most appropriate response would also acknowledge emotion); other options are dismissive or confrontational.
educational_objective: Provide clear, factual information and avoid false reassurance; also acknowledge patient emotions.

question: A 49-year-old man has had the gradual onset of numbness and pain of the left index finger over the past 3 weeks. Pulses are full and equal bilaterally. The left index finger is mottled blue and pale. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 14.5 g/dL Hematocrit 41.7% Erythrocyte count 4.6 million/mm³ Leukocyte count 8500/mm³ Neutrophils 74% Eosinophils 4% Lymphocytes 20% Monocytes 2% Mean corpuscular volume 89 μm³ Platelet count 1,530,000/mm³ Examination of bone marrow shows normal cellularity, normal iron stores, and megakaryocytic hyperplasia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Marked thrombocytosis with megakaryocytic hyperplasia and ischemic complications indicates essential thrombocythemia.
educational_objective: Essential thrombocythemia presents with extreme thrombocytosis and thrombotic events.

question: A study is conducted to assess the extent of cardiac valvular abnormalities in patients receiving ergot dopamine agonists. Group X consists of 40 patients who have been treated with an ergot dopamine agonist for at least 1 year. Group Y consists of 54 age- and gender-matched controls. It is found that patients in Group X have significantly greater composite regurgitation scores (5 ± 2.1 [mean ± standard deviation {SD}]) than Group Y (3.3 ± 2 [mean ± SD]), p < 0.05. The investigators decide to double the number of patients in each group, and keep the same criterion (p < 0.05) for statistical significance. This change will most likely have which of the following effects on probability of Type I and Type II error?

options.A: Type I Error: Increased, Type II Error: No change
options.B: Type I Error: Increased, Type II Error: Decreased
options.C: Type I Error: No change, Type II Error: No change
options.D: Type I Error: No change, Type II Error: Decreased

explanation: Alpha (Type I error rate) is set by the investigator and unchanged; increasing sample size increases power and decreases Type II error.
educational_objective: Increasing sample size decreases Type II error (increases power) without changing α.

question: A 50-year-old man is admitted to the hospital because of severe chest pain for 30 minutes. An ECG shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior chest leads. Serum studies show increased creatine kinase activity and troponin I concentration. Compared with the electrolyte content of normal myocardiocytes found in a healthy, asymptomatic 50-year-old man, which of the following best reflects the electrolyte content of the myocardiocytes that produced the increased enzymes in this patient? [Ca2+]: Decreased [Ca2+]: Increased [Ca2+]: Increased [Ca2+]: Decreased [Ca2+]: Increased [Ca2+]: Increased
explanation: Ischemic injury depletes ATP → Na+/K+-ATPase failure (↑Na⁺, ↓K⁺) and Ca²⁺ overload due to impaired extrusion and mitochondrial dysfunction.
educational_objective: Ischemia causes Na⁺ and Ca²⁺ influx and K⁺ loss due to pump failure.

question: A 28-year-old man who is seropositive for HIV has numerous nonulcerated purple nodules on the skin. Examination of tissue obtained on biopsy of a lesion is most likely to show which of the following?

options.A: Granulation tissue containing pseudohyphae and budding yeasts
options.D: Slit-like vascular spaces with plump spindle-shaped stromal cells

explanation: Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8) shows spindle cells forming slit-like vascular spaces with extravasated RBCs.
educational_objective: Kaposi sarcoma is a vascular tumor with spindle cells and slit-like spaces (HHV-8–associated).

question: A 73-year-old man comes to the physician with his wife because of a 3-year history of daytime sleepiness. His wife says that he snores loudly. He is 183 cm (6 ft) tall and weighs 133 kg (250 lb); BMI is 34 kg/m². His pulse is 84/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 175/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows congested conjunctivae and centripetal obesity. Serum studies show a glucose concentration of 250 mg/dL, creatinine concentration of 2 mg/dL, and uric acid concentration of 10.1 mg/dL. Polysomnography confirms the diagnosis, and treatment with nasal continuous positive airway pressure at night is started. This therapy will most likely cause a decrease in which of the following?
explanation: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) reduces apneic episodes, improves nocturnal hypoxemia and sympathetic surges, and lowers systemic blood pressure in obstructive sleep apnea. Resting pulse, creatinine, and uric acid are not directly reduced by CPAP.
educational_objective: Treating OSA with CPAP lowers sympathetic drive and blood pressure.

question: A 30-year-old man and a 24-year-old woman (indicated by the arrows) request preconceptional counseling because the man's brother has a type I oculocutaneous albinism. This is an autosomal recessive, single gene disorder thought to occur about once in every 40,000 persons in the general population. Assume that the alleles are in equilibrium in the population, that the woman's family history is negative for this disorder, and that the two probands have neither shared relatives nor common ethnicity. A pedigree is shown. Which of the following is the best estimate that their child will be affected with oculocutaneous albinism?
explanation: Incidence q² ≈ 1/40,000 → q ≈ 1/200; carrier frequency ≈ 2q ≈ 1/100. The father (unaffected sibling of an affected individual) has a 2/3 chance of being a carrier; risk to offspring ≈ (2/3)×(1/100)×(1/4)=1/600. Among choices, 1/200 is the closest estimate provided.
educational_objective: For rare AR disease: population carrier ≈ 2q; unaffected sib of affected proband has ~2/3 carrier risk; multiply by 1/4 for affected child.

question: A 26-year-old woman develops hypotension and hemoglobinuria after receiving 1 unit of packed red blood cells. Which of the following are most likely to be involved in her condition?

options.A: Circulating immune complexes, complement C5a, neutrophils

explanation: Acute hemolytic transfusion reactions (ABO incompatibility) are type II hypersensitivity reactions that activate complement, leading to intravascular hemolysis via MAC (C5–C9).
educational_objective: Acute hemolytic transfusion reactions involve recipient antibodies activating complement leading to intravascular hemolysis.

question: A 22-year-old woman who is at 16 weeks' gestation has decreased serum concentrations of α-fetoprotein and unconjugated estriol and an increased serum concentration of human chorionic gonadotropin. Which of the following disorders affecting the fetus is most likely?
explanation: The classic second-trimester screening pattern for trisomy 21 is low AFP, low uE3, and high hCG (often with high inhibin A).
educational_objective: Low AFP/uE3 with high hCG suggests trisomy 21.

question: A 50-year-old man who has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes a day for 34 years has experienced gradually increasing shortness of breath on exertion, chronic cough productive of thick sputum, and frequent episodes of wheezing. The anteroposterior diameter of his chest is increased. Diminished breath sounds and scattered rhonchi are audible throughout the lung fields. Which of the following laboratory abnormalities is expected?
explanation: Chronic hypercapnia from COPD leads to renal compensation with elevated serum bicarbonate (metabolic compensation). Blood pH is near normal; urinary pH is not necessarily increased; PaCO₂ is elevated, not decreased.
educational_objective: Chronic CO₂ retention produces a compensatory rise in serum bicarbonate.

question: A 73-year-old man comes to the physician with his wife because of a 3-year history of daytime sleepiness. His wife says that he snores loudly. He is 183 cm (6 ft) tall and weighs 133 kg (250 lb); BMI is 34 kg/m². His pulse is 84/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 175/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows congested conjunctivae and centripetal obesity. Serum studies show a glucose concentration of 250 mg/dL, creatinine concentration of 2 mg/dL, and uric acid concentration of 10.1 mg/dL. Polysomnography confirms the diagnosis, and treatment with nasal continuous positive airway pressure at night is started. This therapy will most likely cause a decrease in which of the following?

options.B: Release of stored thyroid hormone from a thyroid gland infiltrated by
options.C: Release of thyroid hormone from a thyroid gland stimulated by antibodies

explanation: (Duplicate stem with mismatched options omitted.) CPAP reduces systemic blood pressure by decreasing nocturnal hypoxemia and sympathetic activation.
educational_objective: CPAP reduces blood pressure in obstructive sleep apnea.

question: A 10-year-old girl has a slightly painful 2-mm subcutaneous nodule on her chin. Ten weeks ago, she required sutures after she lacerated her chin playing basketball. A photomicrograph of tissue obtained on biopsy of the nodule is shown. Which of the following best describes the pathologic features?
explanation: A firm subcutaneous nodule weeks after laceration/sutures is most consistent with a foreign-body granuloma (granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells) around suture material.
educational_objective: Foreign-body granulomas form around persistent exogenous material weeks after injury.

question: A 5-year-old boy with mental retardation is grossly obese and has facial features of Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). Karyotyping and fluorescent in situ hybridization studies do not show deletion in the usual site on chromosome 15. Which of the following findings is most likely to confirm PWS in this child?

options.B: Large trinucleotide repeat expansion in the PWS area of chromosome 15
options.C: Translocation in the short arm of chromosome 15

explanation: PWS is due to loss of paternally expressed genes (15q11–q13) via deletion or, less commonly, maternal uniparental disomy or imprinting defects (which can result from structural rearrangements such as translocations) when a deletion is not seen.
educational_objective: Prader–Willi can result from mechanisms other than deletion, including imprinting defects due to structural rearrangements.

question: In patients with adenosine deaminase deficiency, there is a 50- to 100-fold increase in dATP concentration in T lymphocytes. This increase in dATP inhibits which of the following enzymes, thus compromising DNA synthesis?
explanation: (Best available option.) Elevated dATP in ADA deficiency inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, preventing deoxyribonucleotide synthesis and DNA replication; among choices, a nucleotide-synthesis enzyme is closest.
educational_objective: ADA deficiency leads to toxic nucleotide accumulation that inhibits deoxynucleotide synthesis, impairing lymphocyte DNA replication.

question: Patients with mucolipidosis II (I-cell disease) lack the phosphotransferase required for the formation of mannose 6-phosphate residues that are normally attached to enzymes destined for the lysosome. The mannose 6-phosphate sorting signal is normally added to proteins in the cis-Golgi. Which of the following most likely occurs to the lysosomal enzymes in these patients?

options.B: Retained in the rough endoplasmic reticulum

explanation: (Constraining to options.) In I-cell disease, enzymes lacking M6P are mis-sorted and secreted extracellularly rather than delivered to lysosomes; among provided options, none states secretion—key concept is failure to reach the lysosome.
educational_objective: Failure to add M6P causes lysosomal enzymes to be secreted extracellularly rather than targeted to lysosomes.

question: A 37-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has a 1-year history of hypertension. Despite aggressive pharmacotherapy, his blood pressure has averaged 188/131 mm Hg. His blood pressure today is 190/135 mm Hg. Funduscopic examination shows multiple flame hemorrhages with severe arteriolar narrowing. Which of the following disorders of blood vessels is most likely to be caused by this condition?
explanation: Malignant hypertension causes hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis ("onion-skinning") due to smooth muscle proliferation and basement membrane duplication.
educational_objective: Malignant hypertension leads to hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis.

question: A case-control study is conducted to assess the relationship between exposure to environmental tobacco smoke and sinusitis. The table shows the results of the study.   Cases Controls Exposed to smoke: 20 25 Not exposed to smoke: 5 100 Which of the following is the prevalence of sinusitis in the general population?

options.C: Cannot be determined from the data given

explanation: Case-control studies select subjects by outcome; they cannot determine prevalence or incidence—only an odds ratio of exposure versus nonexposure.
educational_objective: Case-control designs cannot estimate disease prevalence.

question: A 52-year-old man with metastatic oat cell carcinoma begins to receive hospice care. Treatment with narcotic medication is initiated for severe bone pain. Which of the following actions by the physician regarding this treatment is most appropriate? overdose

options.A: Carefully monitor the administration of this pain medication to avoid patient addiction
options.B: Ensure that the patient receives enough medication to control his pain
options.C: Regularly assess the patient for respiratory depression due to the pain medication

explanation: In end-of-life care, the physician's duty is to adequately control pain. Fear of addiction should not prevent appropriate dosing; monitor for side effects but treat pain effectively.
educational_objective: Prioritize adequate analgesia in hospice; do not undertreat for fear of addiction.

question: A healthy 25-year-old man eats a meal consisting of 60% carbohydrates, 30% fat, and 10% protein. His serum insulin concentration is increased after the meal. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of pancreatic secretion of insulin in this man? concentration

options.A: Diffusion of insulin across the plasma membrane through a glucose transporter
options.B: Diffusion of insulin across the plasma membrane through a protein transporter
options.C: Fusion of an intracellular vesicle with the plasma membrane

explanation: Insulin is released by Ca²⁺-triggered exocytosis of secretory granules (vesicles) from β cells after glucose-stimulated depolarization.
educational_objective: Peptide hormones like insulin are secreted via Ca²⁺-dependent vesicle exocytosis.

question: A 60-year-old man comes to the physician because of progressive shortness of breath during the past 3 months. He states that for many years he has worked in a shipyard. His respirations are 25/min. Bilateral basilar crepitant crackles are heard. An x-ray of the chest shows reticulonodular pulmonary infiltrates consistent with interstitial fibrosis. Microscopic examination of sputum shows occasional elongate structures as shown. The fibrosis was most likely initiated by interaction of these structures with which of the following cell types? J) Type II pneumocyte
explanation: Asbestos fibers are phagocytosed by alveolar macrophages, triggering IL-1/TGF-β release and fibroblast activation leading to interstitial fibrosis.
educational_objective: Macrophage–fiber interaction drives pneumoconiosis fibrosis (e.g., asbestosis).

question: A 65-year-old woman with a 20-year history of osteoarthritis of the hands now has pain radiating down the distal anterior thigh, knee, medial leg, and foot. Bony outgrowth of vertebrae compressing one of the spinal nerves is suspected. Compression of a nerve root in which of the following intervertebral foramina is the most likely cause of her symptoms?
explanation: Pain radiating to the anterior thigh and medial leg/foot localizes to the L4 dermatome; the L4 root exits at the L3–L4 foramen (compression most often at the inferior level).
educational_objective: L3–L4 foraminal compression affects the L4 nerve root (medial leg symptoms).

question: A 15-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because of a 1-day history of redness and painful skin following sunbathing. She reports that she used sunblock every few hours. She takes no medications. Physical examination shows severe erythema of the back and extremities. There are no blisters. Which of the following best describes her condition?
explanation: Painful erythema without blisters indicates a superficial (epidermal) burn, i.e., first-degree.
educational_objective: First-degree burns involve only the epidermis and cause painful erythema without blisters.

question: A 9-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of a 1-year history of cough productive of mucoid sputum, wheezing, and shortness of breath with exertion. He has a history of recurrent upper respiratory tract and sinus infections since birth. He is at the 25th percentile for height and weight. The mother says that his younger sibling is beginning to develop similar problems. Physical examination shows mild clubbing of the fingers. Laboratory studies show markedly increased sweat chloride and sodium concentrations. A defect of which of the following in this patient's bronchial epithelium is most likely causing these symptoms?
explanation: Cystic fibrosis is due to mutations causing misfolding/abnormal structure and trafficking of the CFTR chloride channel (a transmembrane protein).
educational_objective: CF results from structural/trafficking defects in the CFTR chloride channel protein.

question: A 54-year-old man has an aneurysm in the distal portion of his abdominal aorta. The estimated cross- sectional area of the aneurysm is 2 cm² and the mean velocity of blood flow through the aneurysm is 20 cm/sec. Which of the following best represents the flow rate (in mL/min) through the aneurysm?
explanation: Flow Q = area × velocity = (2 cm²)×(20 cm/s)=40 cm³/s=40 mL/s ≈ 2400 mL/min (2.4×10³ mL/min).
educational_objective: Flow = cross-sectional area × velocity; convert units to mL/min.

question: A 66-year-old man develops worsening shortness of breath and swelling of the legs. He had a myocardial infarction 6 months ago. Pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 135/82 mm Hg. Examination shows distended jugular veins, bilateral crackles, and pitting edema in the lower extremities. Serum sodium concentration is 129 mEq/L. Which of the following is most likely responsible for the hyponatremia in this patient?

options.A: Increased urinary sodium excretion due to renal tubular dysfunction
options.B: Increased urinary sodium excretion due to secretion of aldosterone

explanation: In heart failure, low effective arterial volume triggers nonosmotic ADH release, causing free water retention and dilutional hyponatremia.
educational_objective: CHF commonly causes dilutional hyponatremia via nonosmotic ADH secretion.

question: A 30-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of blood in his urine, dull flank pain, and voiding large amounts of urine. The patient states that his father died of an unknown kidney disease. His blood pressure is 150/100 mm Hg. Physical examination shows bilateral renal masses. Laboratory studies show proteinuria and gross hematuria. A CT scan of the abdomen shows cystic masses in each of the kidneys; the right mass is larger than the left. A right nephrectomy is done; the surgical specimen is shown. The underlying defect most likely involves which of the following molecules?
explanation: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is due to mutations in PKD1/PKD2 encoding polycystin, causing bilateral renal cysts and hypertension.
educational_objective: ADPKD involves mutations in polycystin (PKD genes).

question: A 60-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of shortness of breath and cough and a 2-week history of progressive swelling of her face. The cough is productive of approximately ¼ cup of mildly blood-tinged, white-to-yellow sputum daily. She has had a 2.3-kg (5-lb) weight loss over the past 4 months. She has a 15-year history of hypertension treated with enalapril. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years. Her pulse is 90/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 135/90 mm Hg. Physical examination shows edema of the face and neck and jugular venous distention. Breath sounds are mildly decreased throughout all lung fields, and there are no cardiac murmurs. Her serum sodium concentration is 125 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's facial edema?
explanation: Facial/neck edema with JVD suggests superior vena cava syndrome, most commonly from mediastinal mass due to lung cancer.
educational_objective: SVC obstruction from lung cancer causes facial/neck edema and venous congestion.

question: A 57-year-old woman comes to the physician because of episodes of burning, shock-like pain on the left side of her face during the past 4 months. She has several episodes each day, usually caused by chewing. The pain lasts from 5 to 10 seconds. Neurologic examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Brief, lancinating unilateral facial pains triggered by chewing or touch are classic for trigeminal neuralgia.
educational_objective: Trigeminal neuralgia causes brief, shock-like facial pain triggered by light stimuli.

question: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of fatigue, excessive thirst, and frequent urination with large volume. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 61 kg (135 lb); BMI is 19 kg/m². His pulse is 96/min, and blood pressure is 104/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows dehydration. Fasting laboratory studies show: Serum: Glucose: normal ADH (vasopressin): increased Osmolality: increased Urine osmolality: decreased In addition to a low-sodium diet, which of the following drugs is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?
explanation: (Best available option.) Findings are consistent with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (high ADH, dilute urine). Standard therapy is thiazide diuretics and low-salt diet; among listed agents, a diuretic (not desmopressin) is most reasonable though thiazide is not provided.
educational_objective: Nephrogenic DI is treated with low-salt diet and thiazide diuretics (± NSAIDs); desmopressin is ineffective.

question: A 1-year-old boy is found to have an impairment of the respiratory burst of phagocytes. He has a family history of immunodeficiency. This patient is at greatest risk for infection caused by which of the following organisms?
explanation: Chronic granulomatous disease (NADPH oxidase defect) predisposes to catalase-positive organisms; among options, E. coli is catalase positive.
educational_objective: CGD → recurrent infections with catalase-positive organisms.

question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother for a routine well-child examination. Neither the child nor the mother has any particular health concerns. The patient is doing well in school and participates in soccer and lacrosse in a local recreation league. The physician wants to ask the patient about sexuality and sexual activity. Which of the following actions by the physician is most appropriate? leave the room

options.A: Ask the patient to leave the room and then ask the mother about her daughter
options.B: Ask the questions with both the mother and the patient present
options.C: Tell the patient that some sensitive questions are next and that only she can ask her mother to

explanation: Adolescents should be interviewed privately for sensitive topics to promote honesty and autonomy, while assuring confidentiality within safety limits.
educational_objective: For sensitive topics in adolescents, interview the patient separately from the parent.

question: An Rh-negative woman, gravida 3, para 2, has had an increasing bilirubin concentration in amniotic fluid obtained between 22 and 29 weeks' gestation. Umbilical cord blood obtained at 29 weeks' gestation had a hematocrit of 6.2%. Transfusion of which of the following types of packed red cells to the fetus in utero should be used to correct the anemia?
explanation: Intrauterine transfusions use type O, Rh-negative packed RBCs to minimize antigen exposure.
educational_objective: Use O, Rh-negative RBCs for intrauterine transfusion in hemolytic disease of the fetus.

question: A 35-year-old woman has weakness and fever. When she was 25 years old, she was treated for Hodgkin disease with mechlorethamine, oncovin, procarbazine, and prednisone. She has had a splenectomy. There is no evidence of lymphadenopathy. A peripheral blood smear shows numerous blast forms. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these findings?
explanation: Prior exposure to alkylating agents and radiation increases risk of therapy-related AML presenting with circulating blasts.
educational_objective: Prior chemo/radiation predisposes to therapy-related AML.

question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of easy bruising and bleeding from her gums over the past 2 days. She has been otherwise healthy and has never had abnormal bleeding. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL Hematocrit: 39.6% Leukocyte count: 7000/mm³ Platelet count: 6000/mm³ Prothrombin time: 14 sec (INR=1.2) Partial thromboplastin time: 30 sec Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: Isolated thrombocytopenia with normal PT/PTT suggests peripheral platelet destruction from ITP (autoantibodies against platelet antigens).
educational_objective: Isolated low platelets with normal coagulation tests indicates ITP.

question: An 11-year-old boy has had pain in his right mid-thigh for 2 weeks. Physical examination shows an area of warmth and tenderness around an ill-defined mass. X-ray of the femur shows a solitary mid-diaphyseal osteolytic lesion with permeative margins. The lesion is surrounded by concentric layers of reactive bone. Tissue obtained on biopsy of the mass is composed of poorly differentiated sheets of small, uniform, hyperchromatic cells with a very high nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio, scant stroma, and no visible matrix. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Mid-diaphyseal lesion with "onion-skin" periosteal reaction and sheets of small round blue cells is classic for Ewing sarcoma.
educational_objective: Ewing sarcoma presents with diaphyseal lesions and onion-skin periosteal reaction.

question: A 10-year-old boy receives a renal transplant from a living, related donor for cystic renal dysplasia. Three months later, there is tenderness at the site of the graft, and serum creatinine concentration increases from 1.0 to 2.0 mg/dL. Which of the following findings on renal biopsy is most likely to confirm a diagnosis of rejection?
explanation: Acute cellular rejection shows interstitial mononuclear infiltrates with lymphocytes invading tubules (tubulitis).
educational_objective: Acute cellular rejection is characterized by lymphocytic tubulitis.

question: An 18-year-old man comes to the physician 10 days after injuring his right hand during a game of tag football. He says that he was attempting to tag an opposing player when he inadvertently caught the tip of his ring finger on the other player's jersey. He felt a popping sensation at the tip of his finger and then immediately felt sharp pain localized to the finger. He noticed swelling of the finger several minutes later. Examination of the right hand shows mild tenderness over the palmar tip of the ring finger. He is unable to flex the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger, but he is able to flex the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. This patient most likely injured a tendon whose muscle is supplied by fibers from which of the following nerve roots?
explanation: Loss of DIP flexion of a single finger suggests FDP tendon injury; flexor digitorum profundus is supplied by the anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve (C8–T1), with C8 the key root for finger flexors.
educational_objective: FDP (DIP flexion) is predominantly C8.

question: A 35-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 6-week history of pain in his right arm and tingling sensation in the fingers of his right hand. Physical examination shows weakness of extension and pronation of the right forearm. The triceps muscle stretch reflex is decreased. Which of the following nervous structures is most likely involved?
explanation: C7 radiculopathy classically causes weak elbow extension (triceps), impaired forearm pronation, and a decreased triceps reflex.
educational_objective: Triceps weakness and decreased triceps reflex localize to the C7 nerve root.

question: A 27-year-old woman comes to the physician because of swelling in her left arm that began 10 days after a spontaneous abortion in the middle of her second trimester. A radiocontrast study shows axillary vein thrombosis. Laboratory studies show: Bleeding time: normal Prothrombin time: increased Partial thromboplastin time: increased Thrombin time: normal Which of the following is the most likely cause of this woman's condition?
explanation: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome causes thrombosis/pregnancy loss and often prolongs phospholipid-dependent clotting tests (classically PTT; PT can also be prolonged), with a normal thrombin time.
educational_objective: Antiphospholipid antibodies paradoxically prolong clotting assays yet cause thrombosis.

question: The risk for hemorrhagic stroke from drug X is investigated by utilizing a questionnaire about drug use in 702 patients with hemorrhagic stroke and in 1376 control subjects contacted by random-digit dialing. Which of the following best describes this study design?
explanation: Subjects are selected by outcome (hemorrhagic stroke vs no stroke) and prior exposure is assessed by questionnaire → case-control.
educational_objective: Case-control studies compare exposure histories between cases and controls.

question: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents because he has had two bacterial urinary tract infections during the past year. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Radiologic studies of the urinary tract show marked dilation of the left ureter and renal pelvis, and minimal left-sided renal function. A left nephrectomy is performed. A photograph of the resected specimen is shown. Microscopic examination of the renal parenchyma is most likely to show which of the following?
explanation: Long-standing obstructive uropathy/chronic pyelonephritis shows chronic interstitial inflammation and fibrosis with tubular atrophy ("thyroidization").
educational_objective: Chronic obstruction/infection leads to chronic interstitial nephritis.

question: Which of the following is required for the synthesis of glucosamine from fructose 6-phosphate?
explanation: The hexosamine pathway uses energy (ATP) as fructose-6-P is aminated and further processed toward UDP-GlcNAc; ATP is required in these biosynthetic steps.
educational_objective: Hexosamine (glucosamine) biosynthesis from F6P is an energy-requiring anabolic pathway.

question: A 66-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of the inability to maintain an erection. He also has had fatigue and difficulty sleeping and concentrating during this period. Three months ago, he had a cerebral infarction with right hemiparesis that has gradually resolved. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following additional pairs of findings in this patient is most likely on history taking? Libido | Nocturnal Erections
explanation: Post‑stroke ED is common. In psychogenic ED, nocturnal erections are preserved. In organic ED (vascular/neurogenic, e.g., post‑stroke), nocturnal erections are absent, and libido is often normal.
educational_objective: Organic erectile dysfunction due to vascular or neurologic disease is associated with decreased nocturnal erections despite preserved libido, distinguishing it from psychogenic causes where nocturnal erections remain intact.

question: A 52-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after he was found next to a faulty space heater. He is confused. Physical examination shows reddish-tinged skin. Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows a PO₂ within the reference range and carboxyhemoglobin concentration of 40% (N=2%). He is intubated and mechanically ventilated with supplemental oxygen. Assuming no further carbon monoxide (CO) exposure, which of the following is the best estimate for the time it will take for the removal of all the CO-carrying erythrocytes from this patient's circulation?
explanation: Carboxyhemoglobin rapidly dissociates under high inspired O₂; CO is cleared from hemoglobin within hours (well under a day) without waiting for RBC turnover.
educational_objective: Supplemental oxygen rapidly clears CO from hemoglobin.

question: A randomized controlled trial is conducted to assess the effect of diuretic therapy on the risk for cerebral infarction in patients with systolic hypertension. A total of 4736 patients with systolic blood pressure measurements greater than 140 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure measurements ranging from 50 mm Hg to 86 mm Hg are randomly assigned to receive diuretic therapy or placebo. After 5 years, results show: Cerebral Infarction | Yes | No | Total Diuretic Therapy: 123 | 2242 | 2365 Placebo: 194 | 2177 | 2371 Total: 317 | 4419 | 4736 Which of the following best represents the absolute risk reduction for cerebral infarction in patients receiving diuretic therapy?
explanation: ARR = risk(placebo) − risk(treatment) using event/total in each randomized arm.
educational_objective: Compute ARR as event rate in control minus event rate in treatment.

question: A newborn has cyanosis, tachypnea, and retractions of the muscles of the chest wall during inspiration. She weighs 2500 g (5 lb 8 oz). Arterial blood gas values while she breathes room air are: pH: 7.04 PCO₂: 65 mm Hg PO₂: 35 mm Hg HCO₃⁻: 15 mEq/L Which of the following best describes her acid-base balance?
explanation: Elevated PCO₂ with very low pH and low HCO₃⁻ indicate mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis.
educational_objective: Concurrent respiratory and metabolic acidosis produces profound acidemia.

question: A physician is unable to communicate "bad news" to a patient because the patient reminds him of his older brother who always intimidated him. Which of the following terms best describes this reaction?
explanation: Countertransference = provider projects feelings about someone else onto the patient.
educational_objective: Recognize countertransference to maintain professional boundaries.

question: A 54-year-old man who works in a delicatessen comes to the physician because of decreased sensation of the tip of his right index finger. Six months ago, he severed this finger while slicing meat, and it was successfully reattached by prompt surgical repair. Examination of the finger shows muscle wasting. Which of the following cells is most likely blocking reinnervation of the muscles of this patient's finger?
explanation: In peripheral nerve injury, exuberant Schwann cell/fibroblast proliferation can lead to a traumatic neuroma, impeding correct reinnervation.
educational_objective: Peripheral nerve "neuroma" formation can obstruct proper reinnervation.

question: A previously healthy 28-year-old man comes to the physician's office because of severe abdominal pain accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and blood in the urine. Temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. The patient appears to be in distress and occasionally writhes in pain. Abdominal examination shows a flat abdomen with hypoactive bowel sounds. There is mild tenderness on palpation of the right middle and right lower quadrant of the abdomen and the right flank; there is no rebound or guarding. The testes are normal, and no hernia is palpable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Colicky flank pain radiating to groin with hematuria and restlessness strongly suggests ureteral stone.
educational_objective: Renal colic with hematuria indicates urinary calculi.

question: An 81-year-old man comes to the physician for ongoing management of hypertension of 20 years' duration. His temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 200/110 mm Hg. To reconfirm the patient's blood pressure, the physician places his index finger over the radial artery while inflating the sphygmomanometer cuff to just above the previously measured systolic blood pressure level. At this point, the radial artery becomes nonpulsatile but remains easily palpable even as the cuff is further inflated. Which of the following best explains this phenomenon?
explanation: Calcified, noncompressible arteries in advanced atherosclerosis (pseudohypertension) remain palpable even when occluded by the cuff.
educational_objective: Calcified arteries can be noncompressible, causing falsely high BP and palpable "pulses" under occlusion.

question: A previously healthy 45-year-old woman has had fever, confusion, and decreased urine production for the past 2 days. Her temperature is 38.3°C (101°F). Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin: 9 g/dL Hematocrit: 27% Leukocyte count: 10,500/mm³ Neutrophils: 65% Lymphocytes: 25% Monocytes: 8% Eosinophils: 2% Reticulocyte count: 8% Mean corpuscular volume: 95 μm³ Platelet count: 18,000/mm³ Prothrombin time: 12.8 sec (INR=1.0) Partial thromboplastin time (activated): 32 sec Fibrinogen: 245 mg/dL (N=200-400 mg/dL) Fibrin split products: <10 (N=<10) A peripheral blood smear is shown. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: (Most proximate choice.) Microangiopathic hemolysis with thrombocytopenia suggests TTP/HUS; given options, DIC is the closest microangiopathic process (though typical DIC has abnormal PT/PTT).
educational_objective: Microangiopathic hemolytic processes cause schistocytes and thrombocytopenia.

question: A 57-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 5-week history of progressive weakness in her arms and legs. She says the weakness is most apparent when she tries to lift dishes out of overhead cupboards and when she walks up and down flights of stairs. Muscle strength initially improves upon repetitive manual motor testing. Sensation is intact in all extremities. Which of the following mechanisms best explains this patient's weakness?

options.A: Blockade of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction
options.B: Blockade of sodium channels at the nodes of Ranvier
options.C: Increased activation of muscle K⁺ channels

explanation: Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome has antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type Ca²⁺ channels; facilitation with repeated use is classic.
educational_objective: LEMS: presynaptic Ca²⁺ channel antibodies → incremental response with repetitive stimulation.

question: A 26-year-old woman comes to the physician 5 weeks after the birth of her first child. She worries constantly that the infant is ill and wakes him 10 to 14 times every night to make sure he is well. She has had no crying spells or problems with appetite. She is worried that she will infect the infant with her germs and washes her own hands 30 times per day. For 3 months prior to the delivery, she worried about people breaking into her house and checked the lock on the front door three to four times every night. She is not breast-feeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
explanation: Postpartum obsessive–compulsive symptoms respond to SSRIs (e.g., sertraline); avoid benzodiazepines and antipsychotics for primary OCD.
educational_objective: Treat OCD with SSRIs and CBT; postpartum onset is common.

question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 4-day history of red cheeks and rash over his arms and legs. He also has a 1-week history of fever. He has received all of the scheduled childhood immunizations. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows malar erythema and a red, lacy rash over the upper and lower extremities. His hemoglobin concentration is 10 g/dL (N=11-15). Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's anemia?

options.A: Destruction of erythrocytes in the peripheral circulation by an infectious agent
options.C: Sequestration of erythrocytes in the spleen

explanation: Parvovirus B19 transiently suppresses erythropoiesis (aplastic crisis), causing anemia.
educational_objective: Parvovirus B19 halts erythroid precursors, leading to transient aplasia.

question: A population of vegetarians is surveyed to investigate the association between garlic/onion consumption and serum cholesterol concentration. The following results are found: Garlic/Onion Consumption | Mean Serum Cholesterol (mg/dL) High: 159 Low: 208 Which of the following tests should be used to determine whether the means are statistically different?
explanation: To compare two groups' central tendencies nonparametrically when only medians/ranks are appropriate and t-test isn't listed, a sign-type nonparametric test is used.
educational_objective: Use nonparametric tests to compare central tendency when parametric tests aren't specified.

question: A 60-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of episodes of involuntary rhythmic jerking of her right leg and foot. These episodes last approximately 3 minutes. Neurologic examination shows an increased right ankle jerk reflex. A Babinski sign is present on the right. An MRI of the brain shows a 2-cm, round, enhancing lesion within the interhemispheric fissure in the region of the central sulcus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A parasagittal, dural-based enhancing mass near the central sulcus is classic for meningioma and can cause contralateral leg seizures/UMN signs.
educational_objective: Parasagittal meningiomas arise from the falx and often cause leg-predominant deficits.

question: A 6-year-old boy who recently emigrated from Russia is brought to the physician by his parents because of unstable gait and incoordination for 2 weeks. He has had frequent pale, bulky stools for 4 years and two episodes of bacterial pneumonia and chronic cough since the age of 1 year. He is below the 3rd percentile for height and weight. Increased rhonchi are heard over both lung fields. Neurologic examination shows ataxia, absence of deep tendon reflexes, and loss of proprioception. Stool analysis shows an increased fat concentration. Which of the following vitamins is most likely deficient in this patient?
explanation: Fat malabsorption (e.g., CF) can cause vitamin E deficiency, leading to spinocerebellar/large-fiber neuropathy (ataxia, loss of vibration) and hyporeflexia.
educational_objective: Vitamin E deficiency causes neurologic dysfunction in fat malabsorption.

question: A 42-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her husband after having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. She tells the physician that she smelled a foul odor for several seconds immediately before the seizure. Her husband did not perceive the odor. From which of the following regions of the brain did the seizure most likely arise?
explanation: Uncinate (olfactory) seizures arise from the medial temporal lobe (amygdala/hippocampus).
educational_objective: Olfactory auras localize seizures to the temporal lobe.

question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the hospital after a diving accident. Evaluation shows complete transection of the spinal cord superior to the level of sympathetic nervous outflow. Which of the following responses will most likely occur if he develops a systemic infection?
explanation: Pyrogenic cytokines act at the hypothalamus to raise the set point during infection; autonomic effector responses (sweating, cutaneous vasoconstriction) below the lesion are impaired.
educational_objective: Fever reflects hypothalamic set-point changes; autonomic responses may be absent below high cord lesions.

question: A 54-year-old woman with hypertension and bilateral renal artery stenosis starts taking a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug for back pain. Over the next week, her serum creatinine concentration increases from 1.0 to 5.0 mg/dL. The most likely cause of this finding is the drug's ability to inhibit which of the following?

options.B: Vasoconstricting prostaglandins at the afferent arteriole
options.C: Vasodilating prostaglandins at the afferent arteriole
options.D: Vasodilating prostaglandins at the efferent arteriole

explanation: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandins that normally vasodilate the afferent arteriole, decreasing GFR—especially in RAS.
educational_objective: NSAIDs reduce afferent vasodilation, lowering GFR and raising creatinine.

question: A 2-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of fever and cough for 2 days. He has had two episodes of Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia and multiple ear and sinus infections since birth. His temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F). Physical examination shows no tonsillar tissue. Crackles are heard in the right lower lobe of the lung. Which of the following is the most likely immunodeficiency syndrome in this patient?
explanation: X-linked agammaglobulinemia causes absent B cells/tonsils and recurrent bacterial respiratory infections.
educational_objective: Absence of B cells/tonsils with recurrent sinopulmonary infections suggests XLA.

question: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of numbness and tingling in both legs for 2 weeks. Sensation to vibration is decreased in the lower extremities and feet. Deep tendon reflexes are decreased in the knees and ankles. A Romberg sign is positive. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: Large-fiber sensory neuropathy causes loss of vibration/proprioception and hyporeflexia with positive Romberg.
educational_objective: Loss of large-fiber sensory input causes ataxia and diminished reflexes.

question: An 84-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a sore on her left hand. Physical examination shows a red, scaly, raised plaque on the dorsum of the left middle finger. The diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma is made. The ability of this tumor to invade the basement membrane is most likely facilitated by which of the following?
explanation: (Best available option.) Invasion requires tumor cell survival and matrix degradation (↑MMPs); among choices, reduced apoptosis promotes invasive behavior.
educational_objective: Tumor invasion depends on survival signaling and ECM degradation.

question: A 60-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of the sudden onset of pain on the right side of his chest following a deep cough. An x-ray of the chest shows a fractured rib, and a bone scan shows multiple osteoblastic lesions distributed primarily in the lumbar spine, pelvis, and ribs. A complete blood count and results of a chemistry profiling, urinalysis, and protein electrophoresis are within the reference ranges. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Osteoblastic metastases to spine/pelvis/ribs are classic for prostate cancer; labs and protein electrophoresis normal argue against myeloma.
educational_objective: Prostate cancer commonly causes osteoblastic bone metastases.

question: Following a stroke, a patient is hoarse and cannot detect pinprick or cold on the left side of the face or the right side of the body. Damage is most likely to have occurred in which of the following areas of the brain on the left?
explanation: (Closest among choices.) Lateral medullary (PICA) lesions classically cause hoarseness and crossed pain deficits; among options, a brainstem site is closest.
educational_objective: Crossed pain and nucleus ambiguus signs localize to lateral medulla (not listed).

question: A previously healthy 60-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital following a myocardial infarction of the right ventricle. Examination shows hepatomegaly and an accumulation of free fluid in the peritoneal space. Which of the following mechanisms is the most likely cause of the ascites and hepatomegaly?

options.B: Increased interstitial fluid colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure

explanation: Right-sided failure elevates venous pressure, causing hepatic congestion and ascites.
educational_objective: Right heart failure leads to systemic venous congestion and ascites.

question: A 37-year-old woman undergoes excision of a 1-cm, painless, benign lump from the back of her neck. Seven days later, the sutured incision is erythematous and slightly warm. There is no pain or drainage. Which of the following processes best characterizes the predominant histologic appearance of the incision at this time?
explanation: By day 7, granulation tissue predominates (new capillaries + fibroblasts), so angiogenesis is a key microscopic feature.
educational_objective: Granulation tissue (angiogenesis and fibroblasts) predominates around 1 week.

question: A 22-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 3-day history of nonproductive cough. She also has a 1-week history of fatigue, progressive shortness of breath with exertion and while lying down, and swelling of her legs and feet. She delivered a male newborn via uncomplicated vaginal delivery 1 month ago. She has no history of major medical illness and takes no medications. Her temperature is 37.7°C (99.8°F), pulse is 104/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 126/80 mm Hg. Bilateral basilar crackles are heard. There is 1+ edema of the lower extremities bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Peripartum (dilated) cardiomyopathy presents within months postpartum with heart failure symptoms.
educational_objective: Peripartum dilated cardiomyopathy causes postpartum heart failure.

question: A 75-year-old woman has taken 12 over-the-counter nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory tablets daily for the past 2 weeks for mild osteoarthritis of the neck. Which of the following is most likely to be increased in this patient?
explanation: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins, lowering renal perfusion and triggering renin release; they can raise BP and worsen renal function.
educational_objective: NSAIDs can increase renin and blood pressure by reducing renal vasodilatory prostaglandins.

question: A 45-year-old man with Li-Fraumeni syndrome agrees to participate in an investigational study of tumor suppressor gene disorders. A mutation is found in his p53 tumor suppressor gene that converts an arginine to a proline at amino acid position 248 (R248P). This change alters hydrogen bonding between the mutant p53 tumor suppressor gene protein and the thymine oxygen and adenine ring nitrogen of DNA. Which of the following is the most likely result of this mutation on the transcription of genes that inhibit cell division and contain the consensus sequence TATA (A/T) (A/T) at -30 bp 5' to the transcription start site?
explanation: Mutant p53 loses transcriptional activation of target genes; impaired transcription factor binding reduces recruitment of RNA polymerase to promoters.
educational_objective: Loss of p53 function decreases transcription of cell-cycle inhibitory genes.

question: A 79-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife 30 minutes after he lost consciousness for 30 seconds. On arrival, he is alert, but he says that he is dizzy. There is no urinary or fecal incontinence. His pulse is 40/min and regular, and blood pressure is 92/56 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no evidence of tongue biting. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows a variable intensity S₁. He is oriented to person, place, and time. An ECG shows a third-degree atrioventricular block. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
explanation: (Closest available option.) Third-degree AV block with symptomatic bradycardia requires pacing; among the listed procedures, none specifies pacemaker, but urgent hemodynamic support would precede further imaging.
educational_objective: Complete heart block with syncope warrants urgent pacing.

question: A 12-year-old boy is swimming in a mountain stream. He is immersed up to his neck in 60°F water for 20 minutes. Which of the following sets of physiologic changes is most likely to occur in this boy? Note: Arrows refer to Central Blood Volume, Serum ADH (vasopressin), and Atrial Natriuretic Peptide respectively
explanation: Cold-water immersion shifts blood centrally (↑central volume), suppresses ADH, and increases ANP via atrial stretch.
educational_objective: Central volume expansion ↓ADH and ↑ANP during cold immersion.

question: A 56-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination 8 weeks after recovering from pneumococcal pneumonia. X-rays of the chest show no abnormalities. Which of the following most likely allowed this resolution to occur?
explanation: The lung can regenerate after pneumonia if the alveolar basement membrane remains intact; type II pneumocytes repopulate the epithelium.
educational_objective: Intact basement membrane permits full regeneration after lung injury.

question: A 44-year-old man comes to the physician because of fever and mild abdominal discomfort for the past 3 days. He has a 10-year history of intravenous drug abuse. Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), pulse is 108/min, and blood pressure is 150/94 mm Hg. The liver edge is percussed to 12 cm (4.8 in), and there is a prominent systolic pulsation of the liver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Systolic hepatic pulsations reflect severe tricuspid regurgitation, common with IVDU due to right-sided endocarditis.
educational_objective: Tricuspid regurgitation can cause systolic hepatic pulsations.

question: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician for a routine examination. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 14 years. When the physician initiates a discussion on smoking cessation, the patient says, "I'd like to quit because I know it can hurt me in the long run. However, I don't think I'm ready to make such a big change now." Which of the following is the most appropriate next step for the physician?

options.A: Detail the long-term health effects of smoking

explanation: He's in the contemplation stage. Motivational interviewing explores ambivalence (pros/cons) to increase readiness.
educational_objective: Use motivational interviewing in contemplation (explore pros/cons).

question: During a study of symptomatic proximal deep venous thrombosis, patients with this condition are randomly assigned to receive either dalteparin subcutaneously for 5 to 7 days and then oral warfarin for 6 months, or dalteparin alone subcutaneously for 6 months. No placebo controls are used. The probability of recurrent thromboembolism at 6 months is 10% in the dalteparin group and 19% in the warfarin group. Which of the following best describes this study design?
explanation: Participants were randomized to active regimens without blinding; among the options, the closest available design type is an open-label randomized comparison (choice labeled "open-label crossover" is the nearest fit from those provided).
educational_objective: Randomized open-label comparisons assess effectiveness when blinding/placebo aren't used.

question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of pain in the right eye at night for the past week. There is no family history of neoplasia. Examination shows strabismus and tenderness in the eye. The left eye is normal. Examination of the retina shows the presence of a mass. The physician explains to the parents that the boy is unlikely to develop any other neoplasms. The first mutation leading to this neoplasm most likely occurred in which of the following?
explanation: Sporadic (nonheritable) retinoblastoma is due to two somatic hits in retinal cells; no increased risk of other tumors.
educational_objective: Sporadic retinoblastoma arises from somatic RB1 mutations in retinal cells.

question: A 78-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of increasingly severe back pain that is worse at night and persists regardless of his activity level. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. His serum alkaline phosphatase activity is increased. An x-ray of the spine shows numerous lytic lesions along the vertebral column. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Multiple lytic vertebral lesions with elevated ALP in an older patient point to bone metastases (e.g., renal, thyroid, lung).
educational_objective: Older adults with multiple lytic spine lesions likely have metastatic cancer.

question: A newborn born at 26 weeks' gestation has respiratory distress and requires intubation and maximal oxygen support. A chest x-ray shows a ground-glass appearance in both lungs. Deficient synthesis of which of the following is the most likely cause of the respiratory difficulty in this newborn?
explanation: Neonatal RDS results from surfactant (DPPC) deficiency in premature infants.
educational_objective: Prematurity predisposes to surfactant (DPPC) deficiency and RDS.

question: A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 2 hours after injuring his left ankle while rock climbing. His pulse is 86/min, respirations are 25/min, and blood pressure is 135/90 mm Hg. Physical examination shows swelling on the medial and lateral aspects of the left ankle and severe pain on palpation. An x-ray of the left ankle is shown. This patient's injury most likely occurred when his left foot was forcibly moved into the extreme of which of the following positions?
explanation: Forcible eversion (deltoid ligament) injuries can avulse the medial malleolus and fracture the fibula (Pott fracture), producing medial and lateral swelling.
