educational_objective: Eversion injuries can cause bimalleolar injury with medial/lateral swelling.

question: A previously healthy 6-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of a 1-week history of an itchy rash in his armpits, both hands and feet, and groin. The itching is most intense at night and keeps him awake. His vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the skin shows multiple erythematous papules, some with burrows and many of which are excoriated, similar to the ones shown in the photograph. Which of the following questions to the mother will be most helpful in establishing the diagnosis?

options.A: "Does anyone else in the family have an itchy rash like this?"
options.C: "Have you changed soaps or detergents lately?"

explanation: Scabies is highly contagious with severe nocturnal pruritus and burrows in web spaces/waistline; household spread supports the diagnosis.
educational_objective: Scabies causes nocturnal pruritus and spreads to close contacts.

question: A patient in the early stages of hemorrhagic shock is most likely to have which of the following?

options.A: Flushing due to cutaneous vasodilation that occurs secondary to sweating
options.B: Increased renal blood flow due to sympathetic activation
options.C: Weak pulse due to decreased stroke volume

explanation: Hypovolemia lowers stroke volume and pulse pressure, producing a weak, thready pulse; sympathetic tone increases ventilation and TPR.
educational_objective: Early hemorrhagic shock shows low SV and weak, thready pulse.

question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician's office for excision of an invasive squamous cell carcinoma on the lower lip. The physician has explained the reasons for the procedure, the technique to be used, the possible complications of the procedure, and the identity of the physician who will be performing the procedure. Which of the following additional information is required for informed consent?
explanation: Informed consent requires discussion of diagnosis, proposed treatment, risks/benefits, and reasonable alternatives (including no treatment).
educational_objective: Always discuss reasonable alternatives when obtaining informed consent.

question: A 35-year-old man comes to the physician because of an itchy rash on his hands, waist, and feet for 2 days. He says that his wife and three teenage children are beginning to develop the same symptoms. He says, "We live near a wooded area and love to hike in the woods." Physical examination shows 2-mm erythematous papules in the finger webs, wrists, umbilicus, genital area, and toes. Scrapings of the lesions show mites and eggs. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step by the physician?

options.A: Instruct the patient to use diethyltoluamide (DEET) bug spray while hiking
options.B: Instruct the patient to wear a long-sleeved shirt and pants while hiking
options.C: Prescribe permethrin for the patient and his family

explanation: Scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) requires topical permethrin for the patient and close contacts simultaneously to eradicate infestation.
educational_objective: Treat scabies with permethrin for all close contacts as well as the patient.

question: A 45-year-old man with end-stage renal failure is brought to the emergency department by his mother because of his feelings of depression and apathy for 2 weeks. He has been receiving dialysis three times weekly for 5 years, but he has missed the last three sessions because, "I've been too depressed to do anything since my wife left me 3 weeks ago." Bilateral crackles are heard on auscultation of the chest. Mental status examination shows confusion. Serum studies are most likely to show a decrease in which of the following concentrations?
explanation: Missed dialysis leads to uremia with metabolic acidosis (↓HCO₃⁻) and increased BUN, creatinine, K⁺, and Mg²⁺.
educational_objective: Uremia from missed dialysis causes metabolic acidosis (↓HCO₃⁻).

question: A 50-year-old man comes to the physician for follow-up treatment of progressive, disabling osteoarthritis during the past 6 years. The physician has just learned of a promising experimental treatment for this condition. The company that produces the new drug is offering physicians $1000 for each case referred for treatment. The physician believes that the patient is a good candidate for this drug. Which of the following best describes whether the physician should tell this patient that she will receive $1000 for the referral?

options.A: No, because the patient may ask for the money
options.B: No, especially if the protocol clearly spells out that the patient is not to know
options.C: Yes; the patient may wish to consider the money's influence on the physician's recommendation

explanation: Physicians must disclose financial conflicts of interest that could bias recommendations, allowing patients to make fully informed decisions.
educational_objective: Disclose financial conflicts of interest to patients.

question: A study is conducted to assess the prevalence of hypertension in Caucasian people compared with African American people. A total of 500 Caucasian participants (Group X) and 500 African American participants (Group Y) between the ages of 25 and 40 years are enrolled. Blood pressure readings are taken from each participant three times over a period of 4 months. The prevalence of hypertension in Group X is 10%, and the prevalence in Group Y is 16%. Which of the following statistical tests is most appropriate to determine if this difference is statistically significant?
explanation: The chi-square test compares proportions (categorical outcomes) between groups (e.g., prevalence of hypertension).
educational_objective: Use chi-square to compare categorical proportions between groups.

question: A 30-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being stabbed in the abdomen during a robbery. His pulse is 130/min, and respirations are 28/min. His mean arterial pressure is 50 mm Hg, and pulse pressure is 5 mm Hg to 10 mm Hg. A diagnosis of rupture of the aorta is made. Which of the following is expected to occur as a compensatory response to this rupture?

options.A: Decreased serum urea nitrogen:plasma creatinine ratio
options.C: Increased carotid sinus nerve firing rate

explanation: Massive blood loss triggers sympathetic activation and RAAS → ↑renin/angiotensin II/aldosterone; carotid sinus firing decreases; ADH increases; TPR increases; BUN:Cr ratio increases (prerenal).
educational_objective: Hemorrhage increases RAAS and ADH to restore perfusion.

question: A 23-year-old woman develops multiple red, papulovesicular lesions following exposure to poison ivy. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism underlying the development of these lesions?

options.A: Binding of antigen to IgE on the surface of mast cells, leading to mast cell degranulation
options.B: Deposition of antigen-antibody complexes within postcapillary venules, leading to activation of
options.C: Processing of antigen by Langerhans cells, leading to activation of CD4+ T cells

explanation: Poison ivy dermatitis is a type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity mediated by antigen-presenting cells (Langerhans cells) activating T cells.
educational_objective: Poison ivy causes a T cell–mediated (type IV) contact dermatitis.

question: An 18-year-old woman develops sepsis after an abortion. Within 24 hours she becomes dyspneic, oliguric, and develops petechiae, ecchymoses, and bleeding from venipuncture sites. Which of the following is the laboratory finding most consistent with this disease process?
explanation: DIC features consumption of clotting factors/platelets (↓fibrinogen, ↓platelets), ↑PT/PTT, and ↑D-dimers.
educational_objective: DIC consumes fibrinogen and platelets and prolongs PT/PTT.

question: A 21-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after the acute onset of left-sided chest pain and shortness of breath. The symptoms began while he was playing basketball with friends. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 63 kg (138 lb); BMI is 20 kg/m². His pulse is 120/min, respirations are 30/min, and blood pressure is 124/86 mm Hg. Breath sounds are decreased on the left. There is hyperresonance to percussion of the left hemithorax. A chest x-ray shows a sharp line adjacent to a radiolucent region without lung markings on the left side. Which of the following is the strongest predisposing risk factor for this patient's condition?
explanation: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs most often in tall, thin young men due to apical bleb rupture.
educational_objective: Tall, thin male body habitus predisposes to spontaneous pneumothorax.

question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after the sudden onset of shortness of breath. She has a 9-year history of episodes of soft tissue swelling, particularly involving her face and extremities, but without urticaria or erythema. Some of these episodes have been accompanied by acute abdominal pain with diarrhea. She has no history of severe or frequent infections. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 81/min, respirations are 20/min and labored with marked stridor, and blood pressure is 95/65 mm Hg. Physical examination shows marked facial edema. Treatment with danazol and stanozolol resolves her symptoms. The most likely cause of her condition is a deficiency of which of the following substances?
explanation: Hereditary angioedema due to C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency causes recurrent nonurticarial swelling and abdominal pain; attenuated androgens (danazol) can help prophylaxis.
educational_objective: C1 inhibitor deficiency causes hereditary angioedema.

question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has hypertensive nephropathy and chronic renal insufficiency. Current medications include clonidine and calcium acetate. His blood pressure is 145/92 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show a serum creatinine concentration of 3.5 mg/dL and serum calcium concentration of 7.8 mg/dL. Which of the following additional sets of serum concentrations is most likely in this patient?

options.A: Increased inorganic phosphorus, decreased parathyroid hormone, increased calcitriol
options.B: Increased inorganic phosphorus, decreased parathyroid hormone, decreased calcitriol
options.C: Decreased inorganic phosphorus, increased parathyroid hormone, decreased calcitriol

explanation: CKD causes hyperphosphatemia, low calcitriol (↓1α-hydroxylase), hypocalcemia, and secondary hyperparathyroidism.
educational_objective: CKD leads to ↑PO₄³⁻, ↓calcitriol, and secondary ↑PTH.

question: A 3-month-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother for a well-child examination. Her mother says that the infant can lift her head when lying prone. The patient is eating well and recently started sleeping about 6 uninterrupted hours through the night. The mother adds that the baby does not yet smile in response to human faces and has not started to coo or gurgle with attention. The patient is at the 25th percentile for length and weight and 10th percentile for head circumference. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Which of the following best describes this infant's development?

options.A: Motor normal, social normal, verbal and cognitive delayed
options.B: Motor normal, social delayed, verbal and cognitive normal
options.C: Motor delayed, social normal, verbal and cognitive normal
options.D: Motor delayed, social normal, verbal and cognitive delayed

explanation: At ~2–3 months, lifting head prone is expected (motor normal); infants should have a social smile and begin cooing—both are delayed here.
educational_objective: By 2 months infants should smile responsively and coo; failure suggests delay.

question: A 29-year-old woman has an inflammatory disease involving her joints, kidneys, serosal surfaces, anterior chamber of the eye, and choroid plexus. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of this disorder?

options.C: Release of vasoactive compounds from IgE-stimulated basophils
options.D: Systemic release of interleukin-1 (IL-1) and tumor necrosis factor

explanation: (Best available option.) Systemic autoimmune inflammatory disorders (e.g., SLE) feature widespread cytokine-mediated inflammation; classic mechanism is immune complex deposition with complement activation (not listed).
educational_objective: Systemic autoimmune inflammation involves cytokine-driven tissue injury.

question: A 72-year-old man with multiple myeloma agrees to participate in an investigational chemotherapy clinical trial. Prior to enrollment in the study, peripheral blood B and T lymphocytes are isolated and undergo Southern blot analysis of lymphoid cell-specific genes. Using a single B-lymphocyte J-region probe, analysis of the B-lymphocyte DNA shows a 1.5-kb band. Analysis of the T-lymphocyte DNA using the same J-region probe shows a 6-kb band. The 6-kb band most likely signifies which of the following?
explanation: In T cells, Ig genes remain in the germline (unrearranged) configuration, giving a different-sized band than rearranged B-cell Ig genes on Southern blot.
educational_objective: Ig genes are unrearranged in T cells (germline configuration).

question: A 38-year-old man with Down syndrome is brought to the physician by his nephew for a follow-up examination. He had lived with his parents until their death 2 years ago, but he now lives with his sister and her children. He receives Social Security insurance benefits from his deceased father's account, and this is currently the family's only income. He has missed his last four scheduled visits. He is unkempt and malodorous, and he appears anxious and hypervigilant. He startles when his nephew speaks, and he shrinks away when the physician reaches to pat his shoulder. The patient used to be pleasant and relaxed. He has had a 6.4-kg (14-lb) weight loss since his last appointment 3 months ago. When the physician asks to interview the patient alone, the nephew refuses to leave the room. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial action by the physician?

options.A: Ask the patient's nephew if he often loses his temper around the patient
options.C: Meet with the patient's family and advise them on how to care for someone with Down syndrome

explanation: Signs suggest possible abuse/neglect; inability to interview privately and safety concerns warrant immediate report to APS to ensure the patient's safety.
educational_objective: Report suspected abuse/neglect of vulnerable adults to protective services.

question: A 22-year-old man comes to the physician because of infertility. The photomicrograph shows tissue obtained on biopsy of the scrotal testes. Which of the following is the most likely genetic abnormality?
explanation: Klinefelter syndrome causes seminiferous tubule hyalinization and azoospermia → infertility.
educational_objective: Klinefelter (47,XXY) leads to testicular atrophy and infertility.

question: A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because he says he feels as if he is "frozen in ice." Examination shows muscle rigidity. Toxicology screen shows evidence of exposure to MPTP (N- methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine). Which of the following neuronal cell bodies are primarily affected?

options.B: Dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra
options.C: Serotonergic neurons in the locus ceruleus

explanation: MPTP causes parkinsonism by destroying nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons (substantia nigra pars compacta).
educational_objective: MPTP selectively injures substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons.

question: A 26-year-old nulligravid woman comes to the physician because she has been unable to conceive for the past year. She also has had pain during sexual intercourse. Menses occur at irregular 2- to 3-month intervals. Her last menstrual period was 8 months ago. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Serum studies show decreased concentrations of estrogen, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and luteinizing hormone (LH). Dysfunction of which of the following is the most likely cause of her infertility and dyspareunia?
explanation: Low GnRH → low FSH/LH → low estrogen (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism) causing anovulatory infertility and vaginal dryness with dyspareunia.
educational_objective: Hypothalamic dysfunction causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (↓FSH/LH/E₂).

question: A 65-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has a 15-year history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, resulting in multiple peripheral neuropathies. Neurologic examination shows wasting of the interosseous muscles of the left hand and inability to abduct the fingers of this hand; plantar flexion of the right foot is absent. The function of which of the following pairs of nerves is most likely impaired in this patient?
explanation: Ulnar nerve → interossei (finger abduction). Tibial nerve → plantar flexion.
educational_objective: Ulnar nerve controls interossei; tibial nerve plantarflexes the foot.

question: A 72-year-old man is given ketorolac for pain control after an abdominal operation. He has a 20-year history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is at greatest risk for which of the following drug-induced adverse effects?
explanation: NSAIDs (including ketorolac) inhibit renal prostaglandins, risking acute kidney injury, especially in patients with CKD risk factors (HTN, DM).
educational_objective: NSAIDs can precipitate AKI via afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction.

question: A 40-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of dryness of her mouth and itching and burning of her eyes. Physical examination shows inflammation of both corneas and sclerae, enlarged salivary glands, and a paucity of saliva. Serum antinuclear antibody assay is positive. She is told that she is at risk for developing a lymphoma. Which of the following is the most likely mode of inheritance?
explanation: Sjögren syndrome is an autoimmune condition with complex (multifactorial) inheritance and environmental contributions; it carries a risk of MALT lymphoma.
educational_objective: Many autoimmune diseases (e.g., Sjögren) are multifactorial.

question: An 18-month-old boy is admitted to the hospital because of generalized tonic-clonic seizures. He has a history of mild developmental delay. There is no family history of seizure disorder or major medical illnesses. He is at the 25th percentile for length, the 25th percentile for weight, and the 25th percentile for head circumference. Physical examination shows six hypopigmented macules scattered on the torso and a raised, flesh-colored lesion on the back. An MRI of the brain shows multiple lesions in the cerebral cortex. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Ash-leaf hypopigmented macules, cortical tubers, and seizures suggest tuberous sclerosis.
educational_objective: Hypopigmented macules and cortical tubers indicate tuberous sclerosis.

question: A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician 3 days after discovering a painless mass in her left breast during self-examination. She has not had any weight loss or other recent symptoms. Mammography 18 months ago showed no abnormalities. Menopause occurred at the age of 50 years. She takes no medications. She has no family history of breast cancer. Physical examination shows a 2-cm, firm, nontender mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. There is no axillary lymphadenopathy or nipple discharge. Mammography shows an extremely radiodense mass with irregular margins; it contains clustered irregular microcalcifications. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Irregular, spiculated, radiodense mass with clustered microcalcifications is characteristic of invasive breast carcinoma.
educational_objective: Suspicious mammographic features (spiculated margins, microcalcifications) suggest carcinoma.

question: A 65-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of shortness of breath. He has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. There is no history of heart disease. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide, ramipril, and metformin. He does not smoke. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 28/min, and blood pressure is 152/92 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 90%. Cardiac examination shows an S3. A grade 2/6 systolic murmur is heard over the lower left sternal border radiating to the axilla. The point of maximal impulse is diffuse and most prominent in the axillary line. Which of the following findings is most likely on pulmonary auscultation?
explanation: New S3, MR, and displaced diffuse PMI indicate decompensated left-sided heart failure → pulmonary edema with inspiratory crackles.
educational_objective: Left-sided HF causes pulmonary edema and crackles on exam.

question: A 38-year-old man is admitted to the hospital after sustaining multiple injuries in a farm implement accident. The day after admission, his plasma fibrinogen concentration is increased. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this finding?
explanation: Fibrinogen is a positive acute-phase reactant synthesized in the liver under the influence of IL-6. It rises during inflammation or tissue injury to promote coagulation and repair. Anaphylaxis causes hypotension and bronchospasm but not fibrinogen increase. DIC decreases fibrinogen due to consumption. Histamine triple response is a localized vascular reaction, not systemic fibrinogen elevation.
educational_objective: Acute-phase reactants (eg, fibrinogen, CRP, ferritin) are increased during systemic inflammation, driven by IL-6 from the liver.

question: A 31-year-old woman in the second trimester of pregnancy is brought to the emergency department because of vaginal bleeding. Blood pressure is 140/95 mm Hg. Ultrasound examination shows a conceptus with patches of tissue containing vesicular structures but no apparent embryo. The tissue is surgically removed and genetic analysis shows a 69,XXY karyotype. The presence of which of the following would indicate that an embryo had been formed within this conceptus?
explanation: A triploid (69,XXY) partial mole has both maternal and paternal genetic material, which allows embryonic development. The presence of hematopoietic stem cells indicates embryogenesis occurred. Cytotrophoblasts and trophoblastic lacunae derive from trophoblast, not embryonic tissue. Primary stem villi are placental precursors, not evidence of embryo proper.
educational_objective: Partial moles can contain embryonic tissue; detection of hematopoietic stem cells confirms embryogenesis.

question: A 53-year-old woman with a long history of fibromuscular dysplasia involving the left renal artery develops hypertension. Her left kidney is 7.4 cm (N = 10 cm). She is being evaluated for a revascularization procedure; a left kidney biopsy is performed. Which of the following histologic findings is most likely? arterioles

options.A: Diffuse infiltrate of neutrophils within tubules and interstitium

explanation: Renal artery stenosis causes ischemic nephropathy. Biopsy shows tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis from chronic hypoperfusion. Fibrinoid necrosis is seen in malignant hypertension/vasculitis. Neutrophilic infiltrates = acute pyelonephritis. Mesangial hypercellularity = glomerulonephritis.
educational_objective: Chronic renal hypoperfusion from renal artery stenosis leads to ischemic nephropathy with tubular atrophy.

question: A 73-year-old woman dies 7 years after the onset of progressive memory loss and depression. She had severe intellectual deterioration at the time of death. A coronal section of the brain at autopsy is shown. Histologic sections showed numerous neuritic plaques in the cerebral cortex and numerous neurofibrillary tangles in cortical neurons. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the ventricular enlargement?
explanation: Loss of cortical volume in Alzheimer disease causes ventricular dilation (ex vacuo). Communicating hydrocephalus is due to CSF absorption failure. Noncommunicating is from obstruction (eg, aqueductal stenosis). Oversecretion of CSF is rare (choroid plexus papilloma).
educational_objective: Ventricular enlargement in Alzheimer disease results from neuronal loss (hydrocephalus ex vacuo).

question: A 24-year-old man who is comatose is admitted to the hospital because of a drug overdose and pneumonia. On admission, he is intubated and mechanically ventilated. While receiving a tidal volume of 500 mL, the patient's end-expiratory pressure is +5 cm H₂O, and his end-inspiratory airway pressure is +25 cm H₂O. An esophageal balloon is inserted, and an end-inspiratory pleural pressure of +20 cm H₂O is measured. Which of the following best represents this patient's respiratory system compliance?
explanation: Compliance = ΔV/ΔP. Tidal volume = 500 mL, ΔP = plateau pressure − pleural pressure = (25 − 20) = 5 cm H₂O. Compliance = 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mL/cm H₂O. Other options underestimate compliance.
educational_objective: Respiratory system compliance = tidal volume ÷ (plateau pressure − pleural pressure).

question: A 38-year-old single woman with a history of chronic headaches comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She has three sons with sickle cell disease, for which they have required frequent hospitalizations. She tells the physician that she used to feel angry and abandoned by her family, as they have provided little to no support in helping her with her sons. She states that she recently started taking kickboxing lessons, and now she feels happier and more relaxed. She adds that her headaches also have improved. This patient is most likely using which of the following types of coping mechanisms?
explanation: Redirecting emotions from one target to another (anger → kickboxing). Projection = attributing one's feelings to others. Rationalization = justifying behavior. Suppression = conscious withholding of thoughts.
educational_objective: Displacement is redirecting emotions toward a neutral activity or object.

question: A 6-month-old boy has recently been diagnosed with developmental delay. He has had difficulty feeding and recurrent vomiting since early infancy. He was found to have hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy during a routine examination at age 3 months. Examination of a biopsy specimen of bone marrow shows numerous foam cells. A defect in which of the following metabolic pathways is the most likely cause of this disorder?
explanation: Niemann-Pick disease due to sphingomyelinase deficiency causes lipid-laden foam cells. Other pathways (chylomicron transport, VLDL synthesis) do not produce foam cells.
educational_objective: Lysosomal storage disorders cause foam cells from impaired lipid degradation.

question: A 65-year-old woman has the recent appearance of a lesion at the site of a peripheral scar on the lung. The scar developed at the site of a pulmonary infarct 20 years ago. It was not present on her last x-ray 2 years ago. She has not smoked cigarettes for the past 20 years. A lobectomy is done. Which of the following is the most likely type of malignancy?
explanation: Peripheral lung tumors, especially in scars (old infarcts, TB), are usually adenocarcinomas. Squamous cell carcinoma typically central. Lymphoma/metastasis less likely here.
educational_objective: Adenocarcinoma is the most common lung cancer in nonsmokers and arises in scars.

question: A 65-year-old woman develops deep venous thrombosis of the right lower extremity 10 days after she underwent a right hip replacement. She has been receiving subcutaneous anticoagulant therapy since the procedure. Her platelet count is now 73,000/mm² compared with 300,000/mm² 10 days ago. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: HIT = IgG against platelet factor 4–heparin complexes → thrombosis + thrombocytopenia. Other causes (AML, HSP, TTP) do not match timing with heparin therapy.
educational_objective: HIT is an immune-mediated adverse effect of heparin therapy.

question: A 47-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis is brought to the physician because of a 2-day history of bilateral lower extremity numbness. Muscle strength is 5/5 in the upper extremities. There is spastic paraparesis of the lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are brisk in the lower extremities, and there is sustained clonus at the ankles. Babinski sign is present bilaterally. Proprioception and sensation to vibration are diminished in the toes. Sensation to pinprick and temperature are normal. When asked to stand with her eyes closed and arms extended outward, the patient is unable to maintain balance. This patient's symptoms of abnormal sensation are most likely caused by damage to which of the following tracts?
explanation: MS demyelinates dorsal columns. Fasciculus gracilis carries vibration/proprioception from legs. Fasciculus cuneatus = arms. Spinocerebellar tracts = unconscious proprioception.
educational_objective: MS can damage dorsal columns, impairing vibration/proprioception.

question: A 32-year-old woman comes to the emergency department after taking 40 1-mg tablets of alprazolam. She says that her boyfriend threatened to leave her, and she feels "empty." She drinks several six-packs of beer weekly and uses cocaine daily. She has outbursts of rage whether or not she is intoxicated. Which of the following is the most likely personality disorder?
explanation: Features: unstable relationships, impulsivity, emptiness, rage, suicidality. Antisocial = disregard for others. Dependent = clingy, submissive.
educational_objective: Borderline PD presents with instability, impulsivity, and self-harm behaviors.

question: A 62-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after her husband found her on the bedroom floor, awake but unable to move her arms or legs. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Her current medications are insulin, clonidine, and simvastatin. Her blood pressure is 173/95 mm Hg. Horizontal eye movements are impaired bilaterally; vertical eye movements are intact. Her speech is dysarthric. Examination of the extremities shows quadriplegia. An MRI of the brain is most likely to show a lesion at which of the following locations?
explanation: Classic locked-in syndrome from ventral pons infarction → quadriplegia, anarthria, but intact consciousness/vertical eye movement.
educational_objective: Basilar artery stroke → pontine infarction causes locked-in syndrome.

question: A 16-month-old boy is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has had recurrent bacterial infections since the age of 6 months. Findings on a complete blood count, including leukocyte differential, are within the reference ranges. Further testing of the patient's leukocytes shows normal oxidative burst. His serum immunoglobulin concentrations are uniformly decreased. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?

options.C: Impaired intracellular bactericidal activities in neutrophils

explanation: X-linked agammaglobulinemia: no B cells, no germinal centers, recurrent infections. Normal neutrophil oxidative burst.
educational_objective: Bruton's agammaglobulinemia = absent B cells, low Ig, absent germinal centers.

question: A 56-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of increasing weakness of her arms and legs. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. Physical examination shows pronounced weakness of the hip girdle muscles and lesser weakness of the shoulder girdle muscles, both of which improve with repetitive testing. A chest x-ray shows a hilar lung mass. Electromyography is compatible with a malfunction of the neuromuscular junction. Impairment of which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

options.A: Binding of acetylcholine on the postsynaptic membrane
options.B: Direct depolarization of muscle fibers by Ca²⁺

explanation: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome: antibodies block presynaptic Ca²⁺ channels → ↓ACh release. Improves with activity. Associated with small cell lung cancer.
educational_objective: Lambert-Eaton = paraneoplastic, presynaptic Ca²⁺ channel blockade.

question: Which of the following sets of serum findings is most likely in a 50-year-old man with recently diagnosed chronic renal failure?
explanation: CRF → ↓vitamin D activation, hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism.
educational_objective: Chronic renal failure → hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism.

question: Electrical stimulation of the stellate ganglion is most likely to result in an increase in which of the following?

options.C: Vasodilation in the skin of the upper extremity

explanation: Stellate ganglion = sympathetic to heart → ↑HR. Sympathetic does not cause bronchoconstriction, esophageal secretion, or skin vasodilation.
educational_objective: Stellate ganglion (sympathetic) increases heart rate.

question: Which of the following properties of integral membrane proteins results in their becoming anchored within the membrane? phospholipid tails membrane phospholipid tails head group

options.A: Extensive hydrogen bonding of the amino acid side chains of the protein and the membrane
options.B: Extensive hydrophobic interactions between the amino acid side chains of the protein and the
options.C: Formation of β-pleated sheet structures to maximize protein interactions with the phospholipid

explanation: Membrane-spanning regions are hydrophobic α-helices interacting with lipid tails. Disulfide bonds, H-bonds, β-sheets are not main anchoring mechanism.
educational_objective: Integral membrane proteins are anchored by hydrophobic α-helices interacting with lipid bilayer.

question: A 75-year-old man with prostate cancer has metastases to the spine near L-2. Which of the following is the most likely route of metastatic spread?

options.A: Lymphatic drainage to the iliac nodes
options.B: Lymphatic drainage to the sacral nodes
options.C: Prostatic venous plexus to the vertebral venous plexus

explanation: Prostate venous plexus communicates with vertebral venous plexus → direct spread to spine. Lymphatic drainage is to internal iliac/sacral nodes, not vertebrae.
educational_objective: Prostate cancer commonly spreads to spine via vertebral venous plexus.

question: A 2-year-old girl is brought to the physician because she is "cross-eyed." Physical examination shows moderate strabismus. If not treated, she will most likely have deficits in depth perception due to lack of appropriate competitive interactions in the visual cortex. Calcium entry through which of the following receptors mediates the outcome of this competitive process?
explanation: Ocular dominance columns require NMDA receptor–mediated Ca²⁺ influx for synaptic plasticity. GABA, glycine, 5-HT, metabotropic glutamate are not involved in this process.
educational_objective: NMDA receptor–mediated Ca²⁺ influx drives ocular dominance plasticity.

question: A 62-year-old woman is brought to the physician because her left foot has become cool and discolored, and she has begun to have difficulty walking. Her symptoms began 4 hours ago with several acute episodes of palpitations followed by tingling and numbness of the left foot several hours later. She was not too concerned until the current symptoms occurred. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

options.A: Embolus to the femoral artery with left leg ischemia
options.B: Peripheral neuropathy caused by lumbar nerve root compression
options.C: Small cerebral infarction due to regional ischemia

explanation: Sudden limb pallor, coldness, pain, paresthesia after atrial fibrillation → arterial embolism. Neuropathy/tumor/cerebral infarct don't explain acute limb ischemia.
educational_objective: Acute limb ischemia often due to embolus from atrial fibrillation to peripheral arteries.

question: A 42-year-old man with a history of recurrent pyelonephritis comes to the office because of a 2-day history of left flank pain, fever, and chills. His temperature is 38.8°C (101.8°F). He appears anxious and is in moderate distress. Physical examination shows left costovertebral angle tenderness exacerbated by percussion. His urine is cloudy and has a pH of 7.3. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a large renal calculus. Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy is done for fragmentation and removal. A photograph of a resected calculus from a patient with a similar condition is shown. Based on these findings, this patient most likely has a calculus composed of which of the following substances?
explanation: Recurrent infections with urease-producing bacteria → alkaline urine and struvite stones (magnesium ammonium phosphate). Radiopaque staghorn calculi.
educational_objective: Struvite stones form in alkaline urine after recurrent UTIs (urease-producing bacteria).

question: A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of progressive shortness of breath. He recently retired after 30 years as a construction worker. He does not smoke. Bilateral basilar, fine, end- inspiratory crackles are heard over the lung fields. A chest x-ray shows diffuse, bilateral parenchymal opacities with a reticular pattern and bilateral diaphragmatic pleural plaques. Microscopic examination of a sputum sample shows no atypical cells. Pulmonary function testing is likely to show which of the following set of results in this patient?

options.A: FEV₁/FVC Decreased, FVC Decreased, Diffusing Capacity Normal
options.B: FEV₁/FVC Decreased, FVC Normal, Diffusing Capacity Normal
options.C: FEV₁/FVC Normal, FVC Decreased, Diffusing Capacity Normal
options.D: FEV₁/FVC Normal, FVC Normal, Diffusing Capacity Normal

explanation: Restrictive pattern: ↓FVC, normal/increased FEV₁/FVC, ↓DLCO (fibrosis).
educational_objective: Asbestosis causes restrictive lung disease with ↓FVC and ↓DLCO.

question: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination 1 week after being diagnosed with severe hypertension. Her blood pressure is 180/120 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a renal artery aneurysm. A renal angiogram obtained from a femoral approach is shown. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: FMD: string-of-beads renal artery, common cause of secondary hypertension in young women. Not atherosclerosis or PKD.
educational_objective: Fibromuscular dysplasia causes renal artery stenosis/aneurysm in young women.

question: Cyclophosphamide and some other chemotherapeutic agents kill mitotic cells. Which of the following cellular compartments is most rapidly depleted during cyclophosphamide therapy?
explanation: Alkylating agents suppress bone marrow, rapidly dividing granulocytes first. Hepatocytes/endothelium are spared.
educational_objective: Chemotherapy kills rapidly dividing cells → granulocytopenia.

question: An antiserum is elicited by immunization with protein X, and the anti-X antibodies are adsorbed to microtiter wells. The graph shows the amount of radiolabeled protein X bound by the antiserum in the presence of varying concentrations of protein Y. With respect to the anti-X serum, which of the following interpretations of the epitopes expressed by proteins X and Y is correct? the epitopes expressed by protein X of the epitopes expressed by protein Y

options.A: Proteins X and Y have no epitopes in common
options.B: Protein X expresses all of the epitopes expressed by protein Y, but protein Y does not express all of

explanation: If binding of protein X is blocked by protein Y, they share epitopes.
educational_objective: Competitive inhibition of antibody binding shows shared epitopes.

question: A 46-year-old woman has a 1-day history of high-grade fever, productive cough, and pleuritic chest pain. Laboratory studies show: Leukocyte count 39,000/mm³, Neutrophils 10%, Bands 10%, Lymphocytes 12%, Monocytes 3%, Metamyelocytes 3%, Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase 300 U/L (N=20-100). Which of the following findings most reliably distinguishes a leukemoid reaction from chronic myelogenous leukemia in this patient?

options.A: Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase activity greater than 250 U/L
options.C: More than 60% mature neutrophils on the peripheral smear

explanation: Leukemoid reaction = high LAP, vs CML = low LAP. Both may have ↑WBC, left shift.
educational_objective: Leukemoid reaction distinguished from CML by ↑LAP score.

question: A cohort study is conducted to examine the association between cigarette smoking and lung cancer in a sample of 4000 people. One thousand participants smoke cigarettes, and 3000 participants do not smoke. After 10 years of follow-up, there are 30 cases of lung cancer among the smokers and 30 cases of lung cancer among the nonsmokers. According to these results, how many lung cancer cases attributable to smoking would be expected to occur in a group of 10,000 smokers over the same period of time?
explanation: Incidence smokers = 30/1000, nonsmokers = 10/1000 → attributable risk = 20/1000. In 10,000 smokers → 200 cases attributable.
educational_objective: Attributable risk = incidence in exposed − incidence in unexposed.

question: An 18-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of progressive muscle weakness, poor exercise tolerance, and shortness of breath with exertion. She also has had difficulty following moving objects with her eyes, especially when she is tired. Her pulse is 110/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 105/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows bilateral ptosis. Muscle strength is 3/5 to 4/5 in all extremities. Examination of a muscle biopsy specimen shows abnormal accumulations of mitochondria in the subsarcolemmal regions. Which of the following additional sets of findings is most likely in this patient?

options.A: Maximum Oxygen Consumption (VO₂max) ↓, Venous Blood Lactate ↑, Energy Production by Glycolysis ↓
options.B: Maximum Oxygen Consumption (VO₂max) ↓, Venous Blood Lactate ↑, Energy Production by Glycolysis ↑
options.C: Maximum Oxygen Consumption (VO₂max) ↓, Venous Blood Lactate ↑, Energy Production by Glycolysis ↑
options.D: Maximum Oxygen Consumption (VO₂max) ↓, Venous Blood Lactate ↑, Energy Production by Glycolysis ↓

explanation: Defective oxidative phosphorylation → low VO₂max, reliance on glycolysis, lactate buildup.
educational_objective: Mitochondrial myopathies → ↓aerobic capacity, ↑anaerobic glycolysis, ↑lactate.

question: A 45-year-old man comes to the office for a health maintenance examination. He had smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years until he quit 3 years ago. Physical examination shows a painless white patch on the lateral border of the tongue. A photomicrograph of a biopsy specimen of the lesion is shown. Which of the following changes is most likely to occur next if this patient's lesion is left untreated?
explanation: Leukoplakia → premalignant squamous dysplasia → invasive carcinoma. Viral regression unlikely.
educational_objective: Oral leukoplakia can progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

question: A female newborn develops respiratory distress. Her respirations are 60/min. There was poor prenatal care. Physical examination shows intercostal retractions. A chest x-ray shows multiple rib fractures. Skeletal x-rays show multiple fractures of the long bones at various stages of healing; the skull bones have a wormian appearance. There is no family history of recurrent fractures. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Type I collagen defect → brittle bones, fractures, blue sclerae. Not Ehlers-Danlos, Marfan, rickets.
educational_objective: Osteogenesis imperfecta → multiple fractures, bone fragility, blue sclera.

question: A 22-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after a friend found him unconscious on the floor. A drug overdose is suspected. His pulse is 120/min, respirations are 4/min with apparent low tidal volumes, and blood pressure is 120/100 mm Hg. Physical examination shows mild cyanosis. He is intubated and mechanically ventilated with positive pressure ventilation (rate = 12/min; Vt = 7 mL/kg) using 10 cm H₂O positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP). Which of the following sets of findings best describes the effects of the mechanical ventilation with PEEP on this patient's alveolar (PA) and intrapleural (Pip) pressures? Positive Negative Positive Negative

options.A: Peak Inspiratory PA Positive, End-Tidal PA Zero, Peak Inspiratory Pip Positive, End-Tidal Pip
options.B: Peak Inspiratory PA Zero, End-Tidal PA Zero, Peak Inspiratory Pip Zero, End-Tidal Pip Negative
options.C: Peak Inspiratory PA Negative, End-Tidal PA Positive, Peak Inspiratory Pip Positive, End-Tidal Pip
options.D: Peak Inspiratory PA Negative, End-Tidal PA Zero, Peak Inspiratory Pip Negative, End-Tidal Pip

explanation: Mechanical ventilation → always positive alveolar pressures, pleural pressure positive at inspiration.
educational_objective: PEEP keeps alveolar pressure positive at end-expiration.

question: A 3-month-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of a 2-month history of an enlarging red spot on her abdomen. She appears well developed and well nourished. She is at the 65th percentile for length and 70th percentile for weight. A photograph of the lesion is shown. Microscopic examination of the lesion is most likely to show which of the following?
explanation: Infantile hemangioma: benign proliferation of capillaries, blanches, grows then regresses. Not AVM/lymphangioma.
educational_objective: Infantile hemangiomas = benign capillary proliferation in infants.

question: Which of the following best explains impaired action potentials in the affected axons in patients with demyelinating diseases?
explanation: Loss of myelin ↑capacitance, ↓membrane resistance, impairs saltatory conduction.
educational_objective: Demyelination increases capacitance, reducing conduction velocity.

question: A 70-year-old man with severe congestive heart failure has had progressive orthopnea for the past 4 weeks. He has not been taking his medications. During this time, his urine output has progressively decreased to 300 mL/day. Which of the following sets of laboratory findings is most likely? 1.010 1.025 1.005 1.025 1.010

options.A: Serum Urea Nitrogen (BUN) 20 mg/dL, Creatinine 2 mg/dL, Urine Na⁺ 40 mEq/L, Specific Gravity
options.B: Serum Urea Nitrogen (BUN) 30 mg/dL, Creatinine 2 mg/dL, Urine Na⁺ 30 mEq/L, Specific Gravity
options.C: Serum Urea Nitrogen (BUN) 50 mg/dL, Creatinine 4 mg/dL, Urine Na⁺ 10 mEq/L, Specific Gravity

explanation: Prerenal azotemia: high BUN:Cr (>20:1), low urine Na (<20), concentrated urine.
educational_objective: Prerenal azotemia = ↑BUN:Cr, concentrated urine, low urine Na.

question: A 44-year-old man with invasive pancreatic cancer is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-week history of severe right-sided back and abdominal pain. The patient states that he has had a 6.8-kg (15-lb) weight loss during the past month. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. An operation is scheduled to relieve the pain. The most likely target of pain relief is which of the following labeled sites in the photograph of a myelin-stained cross section of the spinal cord shown?
explanation: Pain from pancreas transmitted via celiac plexus.
educational_objective: Pancreatic cancer pain relieved by celiac plexus block.

question: A 46-year-old man is found unresponsive in his yard by a neighbor. Paramedics arrive and begin resuscitation. Twenty-five minutes later, he regains a stable cardiac rhythm. He is brought to the emergency department, and mechanical ventilation is initiated. His temperature is 36.4°C (97.5°F), pulse is 76/min, respirations are 14/min (with spontaneous respiratory efforts), and blood pressure is 98/60 mm Hg. He remains unresponsive. After the patient is admitted to the hospital, his neighbor says, "He always said he wouldn't want to be kept on life support if there was no hope of recovery. His wife died 5 years ago, and I've been cooking for him and helping him with errands since then." The patient has no children or close relatives. The physician believes that the patient has sustained significant anoxic brain injury and his prognosis is poor. It is most appropriate for the physician to state to the neighbor which of the following at this time? directive." this time." decisions for him." decisions for him." point."

options.A: "Since the patient has already been put on life support, he will have to remain on life support at
options.B: "Thank you for telling me this. Your friend's previous statements to you can be helpful in making
options.C: "Unfortunately, your friend is brain-dead, so there is no need to make life support decisions at this

explanation: Surrogate decision-making guided by substituted judgment when no formal directive exists.
educational_objective: In absence of family, close friend's report of wishes can guide care.

question: A 60-year-old man has had easy fatigability, loss of appetite, and significant weight loss over the past 3 months. Routine blood studies show a marked increase in serum calcium concentration. Radiographic examination does not show bone metastases. This patient is most likely to have cancer of which of the following organs?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma → ↑PTHrP → hypercalcemia without bone lesions.
educational_objective: Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy most often due to squamous cell carcinoma of lung.

question: A prospective study is done to assess the relative efficacy of two different antihypertensive medications, both of which were shown to be efficacious in placebo-controlled trials. In the study, patients with hypertension were randomly assigned to receive one of two antihypertensive medications. At the conclusion of the study, some participants reported inconsistent adherence to their medication regimen, while others reported discontinuing their study medication altogether before the primary outcome (blood pressure measurement after 30 days) was obtained. A few of these patients who discontinued their study medication were prescribed the other group's study medication by their primary care physician and were taking it at the time of the primary outcome measurement. In their primary analysis, which of the following methods should the investigators use to analyze data from these patients who were not adherent to the medication regimen?

options.A: Exclude the outcome for only those who reported stopping the medication altogether
options.B: Include the outcome for each participant in the group to which he or she was randomized

explanation: To preserve randomization, patients analyzed by assigned group regardless of adherence.
educational_objective: Intention-to-treat preserves validity of randomized trials.

question: A 63-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of progressive shortness of breath with exertion. Her pulse is 80/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 125/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. A chest x-ray shows a mass pressing against the outside of the trachea just above the carina. Pulmonary function testing is most likely to show which of the following sets of results in this patient?

options.A: FVC Normal, FEV₁/FVC Normal, Peak Expiratory Flow Rate ↓, Peak Inspiratory Flow Rate Normal
options.B: FVC Normal, FEV₁/FVC Normal, Peak Expiratory Flow Rate ↓, Peak Inspiratory Flow Rate ↓
options.C: FVC ↓, FEV₁/FVC Normal, Peak Expiratory Flow Rate Normal, Peak Inspiratory Flow Rate Normal
options.D: FVC ↓, FEV₁/FVC ↓, Peak Expiratory Flow Rate Normal, Peak Inspiratory Flow Rate ↓

explanation: Variable extrathoracic obstruction → inspiratory flow limitation. Expiratory flow preserved.
educational_objective: Extrathoracic airway obstruction flattens inspiratory loop.

question: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious in the desert. Twenty-four hours ago, he had been hiking and lost consciousness after falling and striking his head on a rock. His pulse is 124/min and blood pressure is 80/40 mm Hg. He is mildly confused. Physical examination shows multiple ecchymoses on the upper and lower extremities and a large contusion on the left forehead. Which of the following best explains the hypotension?
explanation: Trauma with hemorrhage → tachycardia, hypotension, cool skin.
educational_objective: Hemorrhage causes hypovolemic shock.

question: A 21-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after sustaining knife wounds to the abdomen in a gang-related fight. He is in shock. He undergoes immediate operative repair of a perforation of the small intestine and a bleeding puncture wound to the liver. Recovery is uneventful and the patient is discharged. Six months later, he is admitted to the hospital for treatment of an intestinal obstruction caused by peritoneal adhesions. During the corrective abdominal operation, it is observed that one site of his previous injury has regenerated without any evidence of fibrous scarring. Which of the following sites is most likely being described?
explanation: Hepatocytes regenerate completely without fibrosis if basement membrane intact.
educational_objective: Liver can regenerate without scarring.

question: An 18-month-old girl is brought to the physician because of failure to thrive and frequent wet diapers. She is at the 3rd percentile for length and weight. Physical examination shows dehydration, decreased muscle tone, and bowing of the legs. Slit lamp examination shows crystals in the corneas. Serum studies show hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, and a nonanion gap metabolic acidosis. Urine studies show a pH of 5, glucosuria, phosphaturia, and generalized aminoaciduria. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the metabolic acidosis in this patient?

options.A: Decreased carbonic anhydrase activity in the proximal tubule
options.B: Decreased hydrogen ion secretion in the distal tubule
options.C: Decreased sodium bicarbonate reabsorption in the distal tubule
options.D: Decreased sodium bicarbonate reabsorption in the proximal tubule

explanation: Proximal RTA with phosphaturia, aminoaciduria, glucosuria.
educational_objective: Fanconi syndrome causes proximal tubule dysfunction and acidosis.

question: A 40-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of episodes of an abnormal tingling or pins-and-needles sensation that starts in his left hand and then spreads to his left arm and face. The episodes last approximately 1 minute. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. The most likely cause of these symptoms is a lesion in which of the following gyri of the cerebral cortex?
explanation: Sensory homunculus = postcentral gyrus (parietal lobe).
educational_objective: Focal sensory seizures localize to postcentral gyrus.

question: A 42-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 1-year history of an enlarging, painless mass on her right wrist. Examination of the right wrist shows the findings in the photograph. The mass is firm and nontender and transilluminates with the application of a pen light. Without treatment, which of the following is most likely to occur in this patient?
explanation: Ganglion cyst is benign, may compress nerves → paresthesia. No malignant potential.
educational_objective: Ganglion cysts may cause local nerve compression but are benign.

question: An otherwise healthy 26-year-old scuba diver has difficulty breathing immediately after ascending from a 30-minute dive to a depth of 15 m. Which of the following physical signs is most consistent with the x-ray of the chest shown?

options.A: Cardiac impulse displaced to the left
options.B: Hyperresonance over most of the left side of the chest
options.C: Increased tactile fremitus over the left lower lobe

explanation: Pneumothorax = unilateral hyperresonance, ↓breath sounds.
educational_objective: Pneumothorax causes unilateral hyperresonance.

question: In a study of the use of ultrasonography for the early detection of prostate cancer, 35 of 50 men with prostate cancer have abnormal test results, and 20 of 100 men without prostate cancer have abnormal test results. Which of the following best represents the specificity of this test?
explanation: Specificity = TN ÷ (TN+FP) = 80/100 = 80%. Option closest is 87.5%.
educational_objective: Specificity measures proportion of true negatives correctly identified.

question: A man accidentally touches the surface of a hot stove; 20 minutes later, a blister develops at the site. Biochemical analysis of the blister fluid at this time is most likely to show the presence of which of the following? NBME 23 Questions - Formatted
explanation: Thermal injury triggers mast cell degranulation and an acute inflammatory response within minutes; histamine is released early and will be present in blister fluid at 20 minutes. IgE, IFN-γ, and IL-2 reflect adaptive immune activity and would not be present this early.
educational_objective: Immediate-phase inflammation after injury is mediated by mast cells and histamine.

question: A female neonate is delivered at 36 weeks' gestation by cesarean section. Physical examination shows macrocephaly and shortening of the proximal segments of all limbs. A diagnosis of achondroplasia is made. DNA sequencing shows a G→A mutation in the fibroblast growth factor 3 receptor gene on chromosome 4. The biosynthesis of this protein requires a functional signal recognition particle receptor. This receptor is most likely found in which of the following cellular locations?
explanation: Proteins destined for secretion/membranes are targeted to the ER by the SRP/SRP receptor on the ER membrane (classically the rough ER; answer choice "ER" best matches as "smooth ER" among options).
educational_objective: SRP/SRP receptor directs ribosome–nascent peptide complexes to the ER membrane for cotranslational translocation.

question: A 74-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of progressive shortness of breath with exertion; her symptoms are not exacerbated by lying down. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 56 years. She is seated with her hands placed on her knees, using accessory muscles of respiration. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 17/min. Physical examination shows no jugular venous distention. Chest examination shows an increased anteroposterior diameter. Breath sounds are decreased, and heart sounds are distant on auscultation of the chest. There is no peripheral edema. In addition to albuterol, which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient?
explanation: COPD (emphysema phenotype) benefits primarily from bronchodilators (short/long-acting β₂-agonists and antimuscarinics). When antimuscarinics are not offered among choices, a mucolytic (acetylcysteine) can aid sputum clearance; cromolyn/montelukast are asthma-oriented and amantadine is antiviral.
educational_objective: COPD management centers on bronchodilation; mucolytics can help symptoms when other first-line options aren't available.

question: An 85-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her daughter because of a 3-year history of progressive forgetfulness. Mental status examination shows moderate difficulty learning and recalling new verbal and nonverbal material. She also has mild difficulty with naming and calculations. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy to improve her symptoms?
explanation: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (e.g., donepezil) provide symptomatic benefit in Alzheimer disease. CoQ10, zinc, and riluzole are not indicated for dementia (riluzole is for ALS).
educational_objective: AChE inhibitors improve cognition in Alzheimer disease.

question: Investigators conduct a prospective, community-based study to assess the effectiveness of an intervention to promote early language acquisition among children during the first 3 years of life. Delivered over 6 months across five day-care centers, the intervention consisted of providing monthly classes to a cohort of mothers, beginning when each child was 2 years of age. Each child's language skills were assessed independently at the ages of 2 and 3 years; scores were normalized for age. Which of the following sets of characteristics of this study best supports a causal relationship between the intervention and child language scores?

options.D: Strength of association, temporal relationship, dose-response gradient

explanation: Bradford Hill criteria for causality emphasize temporality, strength of association, and dose-response relationship. "Sensitivity/specificity" are diagnostic test parameters, not causality criteria.
educational_objective: Causal inference in observational studies relies on temporality, strength, and dose–response.

question: A 36-year-old nulligravid woman and her 40-year-old husband come to the physician for genetic counseling prior to conception. They have no family history of genetic syndromes. They have been reading on the Internet about certain inherited diseases and ask about their risk for being carriers of an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder that occurs in 1 in 10,000 individuals. Which of the following best represents the carrier frequency of this condition?
explanation: For an AR disease, q² = 1/10,000 → q = 1/100 → carrier frequency ≈ 2q = 1/50.
educational_objective: Carrier frequency for rare AR diseases ≈ 2√(prevalence).

question: A 45-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo a lymph node biopsy under local anesthesia. A surgical resident asks a third-year medical student to get signed consent from the patient before the procedure is performed. Which of the following actions by the student is most appropriate?

options.A: Get signed consent from the patient
options.B: Get signed consent from the patient with another medical student acting as a witness

explanation: Informed consent must be obtained by the clinician performing the procedure; students should observe/assist but not obtain consent independently.
educational_objective: The proceduralist (or supervising physician) must obtain informed consent.

question: A 17-year-old girl with type 1 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She has had multiple admissions to the hospital during the past 5 months for diabetic ketoacidosis. She appears well. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin A₁c of 11.5%. She tells the physician that she does not take her insulin regularly because she either forgets to or is too busy. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step by the physician?

options.A: Discuss the patient's noncompliance with her parents
options.B: Educate the patient about the long-term complications of untreated diabetes
options.C: Refer the patient to a psychologist

explanation: Use patient-centered, nonjudgmental engagement (reflective listening) first to build rapport and explore barriers before education or referrals.
educational_objective: Start with empathy and motivational interviewing to address adherence.

question: A 60-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the office because of a 6-week history of right shoulder pain. The pain occurs when she attempts to raise her arm and when lying on her right side. She has not had weakness, tingling, or numbness. Physical examination shows tenderness to palpation in the region of the right deltoid muscle just lateral to the acromioclavicular joint. While sitting upright, she is able to abduct her arm to nearly 90 degrees, but additional abduction is prevented by pain. Muscle strength is 5/5 in the right upper extremity, sensation is intact, and there is no impingement sign. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Pain with abduction beyond ~90°, tenderness lateral to the acromion, normal strength, and lying-on-side pain suggest subacromial (subdeltoid) bursitis.
educational_objective: Subacromial bursitis causes painful arc of abduction with preserved strength.

question: A 2-week-old female newborn of Mexican descent is brought to the physician by her mother for a well- child examination. The mother reports that the baby has been doing well, except that she often cries inconsolably for about an hour after feeding with formula. The mother says, "I am sure that she has got the evil eye!" The mother has been passing an egg over the baby's body, then cracking the egg into a glass of water and placing the glass underneath the baby's bed. However, there has been no change in the baby's behavior. The newborn is at the 50th percentile for length and weight and 35th percentile for head circumference. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical and abdominal examinations show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate statement by the physician? try?" who is?" harming the baby."

options.A: "I think your baby has gas, not the evil eye. Why don't we try giving her medication?"
options.B: "I'm not very knowledgeable about your folk beliefs. Would you like me to refer you to a doctor
options.C: "Why don't you continue with what you're doing, and let's try changing her to a different formula."

explanation: Respect harmless cultural practices while offering medical management (likely colic/gas). This maintains trust and adherence.
educational_objective: Cultural sensitivity: integrate benign folk practices with standard care.

question: A 65-year-old man develops a progressive ataxia with gait unsteadiness. There is an intention tremor on the right side. The most likely cause is damage to which of the following areas of the brain?
explanation: Cerebellar lesions cause ipsilateral limb ataxia/intention tremor; hemisphere lesions affect extremities.
educational_objective: Limb ataxia/intention tremor localize to the ipsilateral cerebellar hemisphere.

question: A 76-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her son who is concerned that she has become more forgetful during the past few months; he thinks she should be placed in a long-term care facility. She says she feels well, thinks that her son is overly concerned, and clearly does not want to leave her apartment. She has no medical problems and appears cheerful. Which of the following findings is most crucial in determining her decision-making capacity?

options.B: She expresses clear and consistent values
options.C: She has memory of childhood events

explanation: Decision-making capacity hinges on understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and expressing a stable choice aligned with values.
educational_objective: Capacity requires the ability to understand, reason, and express consistent choices/values.

question: A 61-year-old woman comes to the physician for a health maintenance examination. She says that she has been feeling well. A split S₁ is heard over the left sternal border. Which of the following best explains the first component of this sound?
explanation: S₁ is closure of AV valves (M1 then T1). Splitting of S1 reflects asynchronous M1/T1; the first component is M1.
educational_objective: S₁ = M1 then T1; mitral closure occurs just before tricuspid closure.

question: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of a 2-day history of an itchy red rash on his right arm and trunk after a hike in the woods. His mother says the rash began on his arm 1 day after the trip, but it has now spread to his trunk. Physical examination shows 2-cm patches of raised, red, elongated blisters that ooze clear fluid on the upper extremities and trunk. The blisters are in a linear distribution with patches of erythema. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this patient's reaction?

options.B: Late phase reaction of a type I hypersensitivity
options.C: Synthesis of high-affinity IgG by B lymphocytes

explanation: (Best available option mismatch) Poison ivy is a type IV T-cell–mediated contact dermatitis; among offered choices, none states T-cell mediation. The provided options for type I/III are incorrect for this scenario; select the remaining (acknowledging that the true mechanism is T-cell mediated).
educational_objective: Allergic contact dermatitis is a delayed (type IV) hypersensitivity mediated by sensitized T cells.

question: A study was conducted to investigate the mean age at onset in one type of muscular dystrophy. Based on a mental evaluation, patients were divided into two groups: normal intelligence and subnormal intelligence. If age at onset has a normal (gaussian) distribution, the percentage of children with normal intelligence who will have onset of the disease at less than 9 years of age is closest to which of the following?
explanation: In a Gaussian distribution, ~16% of observations lie below −1 SD.
educational_objective: In normal distributions, ≈16% lie below −1 SD of the mean.

question: A 24-year-old man has a grade 3/6 systolic murmur. Cardiac catheterization shows: Right atrium pressure 5 mm Hg, O₂ saturation 70%; Right ventricle pressure 30/5 mm Hg, O₂ saturation 75%; Pulmonary artery pressure 30/20 mm Hg, O₂ saturation 75%; Left atrium pressure 10 mm Hg, O₂ saturation 98%; Left ventricle pressure 180/10 mm Hg, O₂ saturation 98%; Aorta pressure 110/70 mm Hg, O₂ saturation 98%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A step-up in O₂ saturation from RA to RV indicates a left-to-right shunt at the ventricular level (VSD) with a holosystolic murmur.
educational_objective: RV O₂ step-up points to VSD.

question: A 32-year-old man has a diastolic blood pressure that consistently ranges between 100 and 110 mm Hg. He is otherwise healthy and is not taking any medications. Serum concentrations of potassium, glucose, creatinine, cholesterol, and uric acid are within the reference range. Urine contains only trace amounts of protein and no albumin. He is unlikely to develop peripheral tissue edema because of regulatory adjustments in which of the following?
explanation: The lymphatic system can increase flow to remove excess interstitial fluid and prevent edema formation.
educational_objective: Increased lymphatic drainage buffers edema formation.

question: Electrophysiology of the heart is studied in an anesthetized experimental animal. Initially, an ECG shows no abnormalities. Which of the following procedures is most likely to produce the ECG abnormality shown?

options.C: Destruction of part of the right atrium

explanation: SA node ablation produces junctional escape rhythms with absent/abnormal P waves; without the figure, SA node ablation best matches common NBME patterns.
educational_objective: SA node destruction yields junctional rhythms with altered P waves.

question: A 16-year-old girl with bulimia nervosa is brought to the physician by her mother because of a 4-month history of nonbloody diarrhea. Her mother is concerned that she is abusing laxatives to maintain a low body weight. The patient is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 52 kg (115 lb); BMI is 19 kg/m². Her temperature is 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse is 120/min, respirations are 30/min, and blood pressure is 69/61 mm Hg. Which of the following sets of serum electrolyte concentrations is most likely in this patient?

options.A: Potassium: Increased, Chloride: Decreased, Bicarbonate: Decreased
options.B: Potassium: Unchanged, Chloride: Increased, Bicarbonate: Decreased
options.C: Potassium: Decreased, Chloride: Normal, Bicarbonate: Increased

explanation: Laxative abuse causes non-anion gap metabolic acidosis (↓HCO₃⁻) and hyperchloremia; hypokalemia is common but not provided as an exact option—this is the closest match among choices.
educational_objective: Diarrhea → hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis (↓HCO₃⁻, ↑Cl⁻).

question: A 43-year-old woman comes to the physician because she has fainted on three separate occasions during the past 5 months. After the most recent episode 2 weeks ago, she noticed weakness of her face and right arm, which resolved over the next 2 days. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiac examination shows a mild grade 2/6 diastolic murmur over the apex that becomes more pronounced when the patient rises from a prone position. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's syncope?
explanation: (Item appears to lack "atrial myxoma," the classic answer.) A position-dependent diastolic murmur classically suggests atrial myxoma; among options, none fits perfectly—acknowledging mismatch.
educational_objective: Atrial myxoma can cause position-dependent obstruction with syncope (if available among options).

question: A 65-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of intermittent substernal chest discomfort over the past 24 hours. Which of the following eicosanoids is most likely contributing to his symptoms?
explanation: Platelet-derived TXA₂ promotes vasoconstriction and platelet aggregation implicated in coronary thrombosis/ischemia.
educational_objective: TXA₂ mediates platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction in ACS.

question: A study is planned to assess differences in hypertension control between patients in the USA and those in Western Europe. The study population includes 21,053 patients with hypertension receiving care from 291 cardiologists and 1284 primary care physicians in five Western European countries and the USA. The main outcome measure is hypertension control defined as a most recent blood pressure reading less than 140/90 mm Hg. Which of the following best describes this study design?
explanation: A single time-point assessment of disease status across populations is cross-sectional.
educational_objective: Cross-sectional studies measure prevalence/exposure and outcome at one time.

question: A 32-year-old man who lives at sea level travels to a mountainous region for a 2-month hiking vacation. On arrival at the mountainous area, he develops shortness of breath with exertion. At the end of his first 2 weeks of vacation, his exercise tolerance has increased. If this patient's bone marrow were examined at this time, it would most likely show increased numbers of which of the following cells?
explanation: (Best available option) High altitude increases EPO → erythroid proliferation; among choices, megakaryocytes are the only marrow lineage cell listed (though erythroid precursors would be expected).
educational_objective: Hypoxia stimulates marrow hematopoiesis via EPO (erythroid lineage).

question: A 12-year-old girl is admitted to the hospital for treatment following a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. She has mild mental retardation and scoliosis. She underwent surgical repair for partial dislocation of the lenses in both eyes 3 years ago. Her plasma cystathionine concentration is decreased. A CT scan of the head shows a small infarction in the right cerebral hemisphere. Which of the following serum amino acid concentrations is most likely increased in this patient?
explanation: (Answer set mismatch) Homocystinuria (↓cystathionine β-synthase) increases homocysteine and methionine; among listed amino acids, none matches—choosing phenylalanine acknowledges options' mismatch.
educational_objective: Homocystinuria causes ↑homocysteine/methionine with thromboembolism and lens dislocation.

question: A 60-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of headache and dizziness. His blood pressure is 160/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows moderate splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 20.5 g/dL, Hematocrit 55%, Erythrocyte count 7 million/mm³, Mean corpuscular volume 78 μm³, Leukocyte count 18,000/mm³, Segmented neutrophils 15%, Eosinophils 5%, Basophils 5%, Monocytes 5%, Lymphocytes 10%, Red cell distribution width 20% (N=13%-15%), Arterial O₂ saturation normal. Which of the following analytes is most likely to be decreased in this patient?
explanation: PV has increased RBC mass with low EPO (autonomous JAK2-mutant proliferation); LAP and uric acid are typically elevated; platelets often high.
educational_objective: Polycythemia vera features low EPO due to autonomous erythropoiesis.

question: A 6-month-old male infant is brought to the physician because of a 2-month history of failure to thrive and intractable diarrhea that is worse after he feeds. Physical examination shows eczematous dermatitis and mild lymphadenopathy. His heelstick blood glucose concentration is 260 mg/dL (N=60-100). Genetic testing shows a mutation in the gene encoding the transcriptional protein, FOXP3. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a decrease in which of the following T-lymphocyte populations?
explanation: FOXP3 is essential for Treg development/function; deficiency → autoimmunity, enteropathy, DM.
educational_objective: FOXP3 defects impair Tregs, causing immune dysregulation (IPEX).

question: Genetic analyses of cells obtained on amniocentesis confirm that a fetus has a familial loss-of-function genetic mutation that leads to impairment of G-protein-coupled receptor-mediated signal transduction. This defect would most directly impair transcription of genes whose expression is regulated by which of the following hormones?
explanation: GPCR signaling (e.g., β-adrenergic → cAMP/PKA/CREB) regulates transcription; steroid/thyroid hormones signal via intracellular/nuclear receptors instead.
educational_objective: GPCR defects impair catecholamine second-messenger–mediated gene regulation.

question: The parents of a 1-year-old boy with a bilateral cleft palate come to the physician for counseling prior to conception. Both parents have a family history of cleft palate. They ask about the risk of recurrence in future offspring. Which of the following best describes the pattern of inheritance of this disorder?
explanation: Cleft palate demonstrates multifactorial inheritance with polygenic and environmental contributions.
educational_objective: Many congenital anomalies (e.g., cleft palate) are multifactorial.

question: A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he sustained blunt trauma to the abdomen in a motor vehicle collision. Abdominal examination shows mild tenderness but no distention. During the next 3 hours, he develops progressive abdominal tenderness and swelling. His blood pressure decreases to 90/60 mm Hg. Appropriate fluid therapy is initiated, and operative repair of a ruptured spleen is scheduled. During the operation, several episodes of hypotension occur, but the bleeding is controlled. During the next 24 hours, he develops azotemia. He is fully volume-restored, but his urine volume remains less than 20 mL/h. Urine studies are most likely to show which of the following findings in this patient at this time?

options.C: Urine osmolality greater than 1000 mOsmol/kg H₂O

explanation: Ischemic acute tubular necrosis after hypotension causes intrinsic AKI: FENa > 2%, muddy brown casts, low urine osmolality.
educational_objective: ATN shows FENa > 2% with granular casts after ischemia.

question: A 44-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of severe headache. She is 157 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 86 kg (190 lb); BMI is 35 kg/m².
