Physical examination shows lethargy and a clear nasal discharge. Laboratory studies show: Serum: Ammonia increased, Citrulline decreased, Glutamine increased, Urine orotic acid increased. This patient most likely has a deficiency of which of the following enzyme activities?
explanation: Correct: OTC deficiency → hyperammonemia with low citrulline, high glutamine, and elevated urinary orotic acid (carbamoyl phosphate diverted to pyrimidines). Incorrect: Arginase deficiency has elevated arginine; ASS/ASL deficiencies have high citrulline/arginiosuccinate patterns, not orotic acid excess with low citrulline.
educational_objective: OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia with low citrulline and ↑orotic acid in urine.

question: An 80-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by police 30 minutes after she was found wandering in the street, confused and disoriented. She says that she has no medical conditions and takes no medications. During history taking, she becomes annoyed and agitated, saying, "Stop being so nosy! There's nothing wrong with me! I feel fine and I just want to go home." She appears frail but alert. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows mildly dry mucous membranes. There is no evidence of trauma. She is oriented to person but not to place or time. She is able to provide her home address. Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the physician?

options.A: Arrange for transportation to take the patient home
options.B: Arrange for the patient to be transferred to a skilled nursing care facility
options.C: Admit the patient to a psychiatric inpatient facility

explanation: Correct: She is disoriented with limited history; next step is to obtain collateral information (from family/caregivers) to assess baseline and safety. Incorrect: Sending her home risks harm; psychiatric/skilled nursing transfers are premature without evaluation.
educational_objective: In acutely confused patients, obtain collateral history from family/caregivers to guide safe disposition.

question: A 73-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of localized mid- back pain. He has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is in mild discomfort but is able to walk without problems. There is pain with percussion over the lower thoracic spine. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. Serum studies show: Ca²⁺, Phosphorus, Total bilirubin, Alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT, v-Glutamyltransferase (GGT). X-rays of the spine show vertebral cortical thickening of the end-plates, creating "picture frame" vertebrae. Technetium 99m scan shows increased areas of uptake in the skull, thoracic spine, lumbar spine, and right proximal femur. Which of the following best describes the primary underlying pathophysiologic mechanism of this condition?

options.B: Decreased synthesis and secretion of intact parathyroid hormone
options.D: Increased osteoclast activity with disorganized bone remodeling.

explanation: Correct: Paget disease of bone is driven initially by increased osteoclast activity, often associated with increased osteoclastogenic cytokines (eg, IL-6, RANKL). None of the listed options captures the hallmark increased osteoclast activity; decreased IL-6/PTH is incorrect; IL-12 is not primary.
educational_objective: Paget disease features increased osteoclast activity followed by disorganized osteoblast response, causing thickened, fragile bone.

question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of progressive clumsiness and fatigue during the past 6 months. He says that his legs are tired. He was delivered at term after an uncomplicated pregnancy. He has met all developmental milestones, although there was some delay compared with other children his age. He is alert. He has difficulty rising from the chair, he uses his arms to push himself into a standing position. He is unable to jump with both feet together. Physical examination shows hypertrophy of the calf muscles. This patient most likely has weak hip adduction as a result of dysfunction of the muscle inserting onto the femur from which of the following locations?
explanation: Correct: Duchenne muscular dystrophy presents with Gowers' sign and calf pseudohypertrophy. Weak hip adduction involves adductor muscles (origins on pubis/ischium) inserting on femur; none of the listed origins (anterior sacrum, iliac crest/spine, lateral ilium) correspond to primary adductors.
educational_objective: In DMD, proximal weakness affects hip adductors (pubis/ischium origins), which are not among the provided options.

question: Investigators are evaluating oxygen consumption by different segments of the renal tubules in experimental animals. Arterial oxygen saturation is decreased in blood delivered to isolated perfused pig kidneys. Results show that as oxygen delivery declines, urine output decreases. A biopsy specimen of the ischemic model is obtained. Tubular cell death is most likely to be observed in which of the following areas?
explanation: Correct: The PCT (and thick ascending limb) have high ATP demand and are most sensitive to ischemia → acute tubular necrosis. Incorrect: CCD and DCT are less metabolically active; "loop of Henle" is nonspecific (the TAL portion is sensitive, but PCT is classic).
educational_objective: Ischemic acute tubular necrosis primarily injures PCT (and medullary TAL).

question: A 33-year-old man comes to the physician for a physical examination prior to starting a new job. He feels well and recently became engaged to be married. Physical examination shows a 1.5-cm fixed, nontender mass on the right side of the neck. During the examination, he appears anxious and says, "You seem to be spending a lot of time examining my neck. Is there something wrong? Do I have cancer?" After informing the patient about the discovery of the suspected mass, which of the following is the most appropriate initial statement by the physician? fiancée to come in with you when you return for a biopsy next week." to schedule a time as soon as possible to get a sample of the mass for further examination." Please take this referral to the front desk so that they can schedule the procedure and a follow-up visit with me." we have the results of the biopsy, I don't think you should worry about it." support of your fiancée."

options.A: "It's understandable that you're worried, so I'll walk you through each step. We'll need to schedule a time as soon as possible to get a sample of the mass for further examination."
options.B: "The only way to know if the mass in your neck is malignant or benign is to do a biopsy.
options.C: "Whatever this mass turns out to be, it'll be easier to face because you'll have the

explanation: Correct: Start with empathy, provide clear plan and next step (biopsy) without premature reassurance or delegating logistics. Incorrect: Minimizing worry, deflecting to front desk, or bringing in family first isn't patient-centered initial communication.
educational_objective: Combine empathy with a clear, stepwise diagnostic plan (eg, biopsy) when discussing concerning findings.

question: An investigator is studying the regulation of pulmonary lymphatic flow using an animal model. Catheters are implanted in the femoral vein, pulmonary artery, and main lymphatic vessel draining the lungs in anesthetized, intubated, mechanically ventilated animals. Drugs may be injected directly into the pulmonary artery catheter and inspired gas mixtures altered at the ventilator; timed collection of lymph from the catheters is used to calculate lymphatic flow. Which of the following interventions will most likely increase the flow of pulmonary lymph in these animals?

options.A: Administration of phenylephrine into the pulmonary artery
options.B: Decreasing the inspired oxygen concentration from 21% to 10%
options.C: Intravenous infusion of 0.9% saline for 5 minutes
options.D: Intravenous infusion of 20% albumin solution (20 g/100 ml saline) for 5 minutes

explanation: Correct: Expanding intravascular volume raises pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure and filtration, increasing interstitial fluid and lymph flow. Incorrect: Albumin raises oncotic pressure and reduces filtration; endothelin/phenylephrine effects are complex; hypoxia-induced vasoconstriction may reduce perfusion/flow depending on conditions.
educational_objective: Increased pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure (eg, volume loading) increases lymph formation and flow.

question: An investigator is studying the thyroid hormone receptor. It is found that the receptor binds chromatin in both the presence and absence of triiodothyronine (T₃). Results show that this binding inhibits transcription in the absence of the hormone and activates transcription in the presence of the hormone. It is theorized that binding of the hormone causes an allosteric conformational change that decreases affinity for complex 1 and increases affinity for complex 2. Complex 1 and complex 2 most likely contain which of the following enzyme activities?
explanation: Correct: Unliganded nuclear receptors recruit HDACs (repression); hormone binding switches to HAT coactivators (activation). Incorrect: Deiodinase/TPO act in hormone synthesis/metabolism, not chromatin regulation; endonucleases/ligases and ubiquitin pathways are unrelated here.
educational_objective: Thyroid receptor switches from HDAC (repression) to HAT (activation) complexes upon T₃ binding.

question: A 78-year-old man who is a Vietnam War veteran comes to the physician because of a 3- month history of low back pain that has become increasingly severe during the past 2 weeks, and has caused difficulty walking because of pain radiating down his left leg. He has a 3-week history of night sweats and an intermittent low-grade fever. He also has had a 9-kg (20-lb) weight loss during the past 3 months. He appears ill. He is 173 cm (5 ft 8 in) tall and weighs 55 kg (121 lb); BMI is 18 kg/m². His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), and pulse is 85/min. Physical examination shows pallor, right convex lumbar scoliosis, and tenderness over the L2-3 area. He has difficulty climbing onto the examination table. Coronal and axial views of a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast are shown. Which of the following active motions of the left hip is likely to be the most painful for this patient?
explanation: Correct: Psoas abscess from vertebral osteomyelitis (eg, TB) causes pain with hip extension (psoas stretch) and relief with flexion. Incorrect: Abduction/adduction/internal rotation are less provocative for psoas irritation; flexion typically relieves pain.
educational_objective: Iliopsoas inflammation (eg, psoas abscess) causes pain with hip extension due to muscle stretch.

question: An investigator is studying the mechanisms of nerve regeneration after injury. A repetition injury is induced in a peripheral nerve in an experimental animal. It is found that sensory and motor axons are lost by Wallerian degeneration beyond the site of the injury. Further study is most likely to show which of the following cell structures acting as a path-finding guide for the regeneration of the damaged axons?
explanation: Correct: Schwann cells and their endoneurial tubes (Bands of Büngner) formed by the myelin sheath/endoneurium guide regenerating PNS axons. Incorrect: Axon hillock initiates impulses; dendritic spines receive synapses; terminal boutons are presynaptic endings.
educational_objective: Schwann cell–derived myelin/endoneurial tubes guide regenerating peripheral axons.

question: A 40-year-old woman at 5 months' gestation comes to the physician for amniocentesis. Results show a normal 46,XY karyotype of the fetus. Four months later, the newborn is delivered and examination shows a female phenotype with mild clitoral enlargement. Ultrasonography shows the presence of male but not female genital ducts. This newborn most likely has a mutation of the gene of which of the following factors?

options.C: Zinc finger transcription factor Wilms tumor 1

explanation: Correct: 46,XY with Wolffian ducts (testosterone present) but female external phenotype at birth implies impaired DHT formation (5α-reductase deficiency). MIS is intact (no Mullerian ducts). Incorrect: AMH deficiency would leave Mullerian ducts; SRY/WT1 defects disrupt testis formation/Wolffian maintenance.
educational_objective: 5α-Reductase deficiency → under-virilized external genitalia at birth with intact Wolffian ducts in 46,XY.

question: A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of progressive shortness of breath while climbing stairs and constant fatigue. She is 163 cm (5 ft 4 in) tall and weighs 107 kg (235 lb); BMI is 40 kg/m². Her blood pressure is 170/110 mm Hg on three separate readings. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 45%. There are no regional wall motion or valvular abnormalities. An ECG shows that the sum of the magnitudes of the S wave in lead V2 and the R wave in lead V5 is 45 mm (scale=10 mm/mV). Which of the following cellular changes is most likely in this patient's left ventricle compared with normal?

options.A: Increased sarcomeres in an array in parallel with each other
options.B: Increased sarcomeres in an array in series with each other

explanation: Correct: Chronic pressure overload (hypertension) → concentric hypertrophy with sarcomeres added in parallel. Incorrect: Series addition occurs in volume overload (dilation); neutrophil infiltration suggests acute MI; decreased sarcomeres doesn't occur in hypertrophy.
educational_objective: Hypertension causes concentric LV hypertrophy via parallel addition of sarcomeres.

question: A 60-year-old woman comes to the physician because of vaginal bleeding for 6 weeks. Menarche occurred at the age of 12 years, and menses had occurred at regular 30-day intervals. She had three term pregnancies by the age of 25 years. She has been receiving conjugated equine estrogen therapy since menopause 10 years ago. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. She drinks alcoholic beverages five times weekly. Physical examination and laboratory studies show no abnormalities. An endometrial biopsy specimen shows endometrial adenocarcinoma. Which of the following is the strongest predisposing risk factor for the biopsy findings?
explanation: Correct: Unopposed estrogen is the major driver of endometrial carcinoma risk; early menarche increases lifetime estrogen exposure. Incorrect: Multiparity is protective; smoking is not a risk (may be modestly protective); alcohol's relationship is weaker than estrogen exposure patterns.
educational_objective: Increased lifetime estrogen exposure (eg, early menarche) raises endometrial cancer risk.

question: A 73-year-old woman has a 3-month history of increasing fatigue, weakness, and a 9.0-kg (20-lb) weight loss. Examination shows hepatosplenomegaly. An M-protein spike is observed on serum electrophoresis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Correct: An M-protein spike indicates a monoclonal immunoglobulin, produced by a malignant B-cell/plasma cell clone. Incorrect: AML/CML are myeloid; T-cell neoplasms do not produce an Ig spike.
educational_objective: A monoclonal M spike reflects a clonal B-cell/plasma cell process.

question: An investigator is studying a new hormone: Hormone X. To determine its cell target, a purified, radioactively labeled form of Hormone X is added to tissue cultures. Subsequent analysis shows that the radioactivity is detected only around the region of the plasma membrane. Hormone X is most similar to which of the following hormones?

options.D: Hormone X binds at plasma membrane

explanation: Correct: Localization only at the plasma membrane suggests a peptide/catecholamine hormone acting via a cell-surface receptor; none of the listed steroid/thyroid hormones (which use intracellular/nuclear receptors) fits.
educational_objective: Peptide/catecholamine hormones act via plasma membrane receptors, unlike steroid/thyroid hormones.

question: A 34-year-old man who is seropositive for HIV has a neoplasm manifested as violaceous raised cutaneous plaques (erythematous cutaneous plaques). Examination of tissue obtained on biopsy of the neoplasm is most likely to show which of the following?

options.A: Large polygonal and giant cells with myofibrils
options.C: Proliferating spindle cells forming slit-like spaces filled with blood

explanation: Correct: Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8) shows spindle cell proliferation with irregular blood-filled vascular spaces. Incorrect: The other options describe scar, muscle, or adenocarcinoma histology.
educational_objective: Kaposi sarcoma in HIV shows spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces.

question: A 31-year-old man who works as a chef comes to the emergency department 30 minutes after accidentally cutting his right thumb with a knife. Examination of the right hand shows a 3-cm-long, 0.5-cm-deep laceration of the thumb. The wound is cleaned, sutured, and heals normally, leaving a faint scar by 1 year after the injury. The remodeling of the scar that occurred during the first year after injury is primarily mediated by which of the following?
explanation: Correct: Scar remodeling over months is driven by MMPs (eg, collagenases) that degrade and reorganize extracellular matrix. Incorrect: Chemokines/IL-1/TNF are key in early inflammation, not long-term remodeling.
educational_objective: Matrix metalloproteinases mediate late scar remodeling by controlled ECM degradation.

question: A 60-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of progressive shortness of breath with exertion. Examination of the chest shows: Right Lung Base: decreased breath sounds, dullness on percussion, decreased tactile fremitus, no adventitious sounds Left Lung Base: normal breath sounds, normal percussion, normal tactile fremitus, crackles Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Correct: Decreased breath sounds, dullness, and decreased fremitus indicate fluid in the pleural space at the right base. Left-sided crackles suggest parenchymal process but the right findings are classic for effusion. Incorrect: Pneumonia increases fremitus; pneumothorax is hyperresonant with absent fremitus; others have different patterns.
educational_objective: Dullness to percussion with ↓breath sounds and ↓fremitus indicates pleural effusion.

question: A 70-year-old woman with osteoporosis comes to the physician for her scheduled injection of ibandronate. She is accompanied by her 75-year-old husband. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. The husband asks the physician, "Why don't I have osteoporosis? For the past 50 years we have done everything together, including eating the same foods and exercising. I even used to smoke and drink. Yet she has osteoporosis, and I don't." Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.A: "Exercising is good for both of you, but it is more protective for men."
options.B: "Men start out with a higher peak bone mass compared with women."

explanation: Correct: Men have higher peak bone mass and a slower rate of loss, which reduces osteoporosis risk compared with women. Incorrect: Alcohol increases risk; exercise helps both sexes similarly; low testosterone would increase, not decrease, his risk.
educational_objective: Higher peak bone mass in men reduces their lifetime osteoporosis risk versus women.

question: A 49-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a persistent and painful erection since he took a drug for erectile dysfunction 4 hours ago. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), and blood pressure is 110/65 mm Hg. Physical examination shows flushing of the skin and priapism. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a lack of input from which of the following neural pathways?

options.A: Parasympathetic fibers from the pelvic plexus
options.B: Somatic motor fibers from the pudendal nerve
options.C: Visceral afferent fibers to the pelvic plexus

explanation: Correct: Detumescence requires sympathetic (hypogastric) vasoconstrictor outflow; lack of sympathetic input (not listed) promotes persistent erection/priapism. The listed options do not represent the sympathetic pathway.
educational_objective: Priapism reflects persistent parasympathetic tone/inadequate sympathetic outflow (hypogastric).

question: A 70-year-old man comes to the physician because of a rash for 7 days. Physical examination shows multiple 4- to 6-cm tense bullae filled with clear fluid over the inner aspects of the forearms, lower abdomen, groin, and thighs. Examination of a skin biopsy specimen shows a non-acantholytic blister with separation of the epidermis from the basement membrane. Serologic studies are most likely to show an autoantibody directed against which of the following?
explanation: Correct: Bullous pemphigoid has autoantibodies to hemidesmosomal proteins (eg, BP180/type XVII collagen) that are part of anchoring filaments at the dermal–epidermal junction → tense, subepidermal blisters. Incorrect: Desmosomes (pemphigus vulgaris) are intraepidermal; type IV collagen is in the lamina densa; ICAM-1 is endothelial.
educational_objective: Bullous pemphigoid targets hemidesmosomal anchoring structures at the basement membrane.

question: An investigator is testing the hypothesis that advanced glycosylation end products (AGEs) lead to an increased synthesis of extracellular matrix by human renal mesangial cells. The cells are plated on two media: type I collagen treated extensively with glucose 6-phosphate to produce AGEs (first medium), and a control medium of untreated type I collagen. To confirm this hypothesis, mRNA that encodes for which of the following is most likely to be increased in cells incubated in the first medium compared with cells in the control medium?
explanation: Correct: AGEs stimulate mesangial matrix production (eg, collagen, fibronectin). Incorrect: eNOS and VEGF relate to endothelium/angiogenesis; NADPH oxidase promotes ROS but is not a matrix protein.
educational_objective: AGEs upregulate mesangial extracellular matrix components such as fibronectin.

question: An autopsy is done on a 50-year-old man who died of pneumonia despite 5 days of antibiotic therapy in the intensive care unit. He had a 15-year history of alcoholism. A photograph of a sagittal section of the brain is shown. Based on this pathology, which of the following findings was most likely present on neurologic examination of the patient prior to his death?
explanation: Correct: Alcoholic cerebellar degeneration (vermis, and possibly hemispheres) leads to cerebellar signs such as intention tremor and dysmetria. Incorrect: Essential tremor is a different disorder; Romberg tests proprioception (dorsal columns), not cerebellum.
educational_objective: Cerebellar degeneration from alcoholism causes dysmetria and other cerebellar signs.

question: A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of a 2-day history of dizziness and headache. She is intelligent and does well in school. Her mother had a cerebellar tumor removed during childhood and is concerned that her daughter might have a similar condition. A normal reaction to which of the following physical examination maneuvers is most likely to rule out a cerebellar tumor in this patient?
explanation: Correct: Cerebellar function is not assessed by the listed maneuvers (which test corticospinal tract, brainstem/vestibulo-ocular reflex, frontal release, and peripheral nerve irritability, respectively). Heel-to-shin or finger-to-nose would be appropriate.
educational_objective: Use coordination tests (eg, finger-to-nose) to evaluate cerebellar function; the listed maneuvers do not.

question: A 40-year-old man comes to the physician for a routine examination. He has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 20 years. Which of the following initial statements by the physician is likely to be most effective in encouraging this patient to stop smoking?

options.A: "Let me show you a picture of what lungs look like after a lifetime of smoking."
options.B: "Please tell me how I can help you to stop smoking."
options.C: "What thoughts have you had about quitting smoking?"
options.D: "Why do you continue to smoke when it is so unhealthy?"

explanation: Correct: Open-ended, nonjudgmental question aligns with motivational interviewing to assess readiness to change. Incorrect: Confrontational, fear-based, or overly directive statements are less effective initially.
educational_objective: Motivational interviewing starts with open-ended questions that explore readiness and ambivalence.

question: A 65-year-old right-handed man has a thrombotic stroke. A CT scan of the head is shown. Which of the following is the most likely neurologic finding in this patient?

options.C: Weakness of the lower two thirds of the face on the left

explanation: Correct: In a typical dominant (left) MCA stroke for a right-handed person, global aphasia can result (both Broca and Wernicke areas). (Image not provided; this is the most likely dominant-hemisphere deficit.) Incorrect: Left hemiparesis/spatial neglect/isolated facial weakness suggest different vascular territories or nondominant lesions.
educational_objective: Left MCA strokes in right-handed patients commonly cause aphasia.

question: A 33-year-old African American woman comes to the physician because of dry eyes for 3 weeks. Physical examination shows decreased lacrimation and uveitis. There is mild hepatosplenomegaly. A chest x-ray shows prominent bilateral hilar adenopathy. Microscopic examination of a hilar lymph node is most likely to show which of the following pathologic conditions?
explanation: Correct: Sarcoidosis presents with uveitis, dry eyes (lacrimal gland involvement), hepatosplenomegaly, and bilateral hilar adenopathy; nodes show noncaseating granulomas. Incorrect: The neoplasms/abscess listed do not match the clinical picture.
educational_objective: Sarcoidosis causes noncaseating granulomas in affected tissues and lymph nodes.

question: A study is conducted to assess the effects of aging on cognitive and physiologic function. Participants are recruited via advertisements in the local and regional news media, and all persons who answer the advertisement are selected for study. Which of the following best describes this sampling technique?
explanation: Correct: This is a volunteer (self-selected) convenience sample, which is prone to volunteer bias; none of the listed categories applies.
educational_objective: Recruiting all respondents to an ad yields a volunteer sample (selection bias), not a population-based or randomized sample.

question: During an experiment, investigators use an in vitro cell culture system to study leukocyte function. As part of the study, a new drug that prevents polymerization of actin filaments is tested. Which of the following leukocyte functions is most likely to be inhibited by this new drug?
explanation: Correct: Engulfment requires actin-dependent pseudopod formation. Incorrect: Receptor binding and clathrin-mediated internalization need not directly rely on actin polymerization.
educational_objective: Actin polymerization is essential for phagocytic engulfment.

question: A 1-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of developmental delay. Physical examination shows a coarse facial appearance, clouded corneas in both eyes, hepatosplenomegaly, stiff joints, and developmental delay. Urine studies show an increased concentration of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. Which of the following enzymes is most likely impaired in this patient?
explanation: Correct: Hurler syndrome (MPS I) with corneal clouding, coarse facies, HSM, and ↑dermatan/heparan sulfate results from α-iduronidase deficiency. Incorrect: The other enzymes correspond to different lysosomal or metabolic disorders.
educational_objective: Hurler syndrome is due to α-iduronidase deficiency, causing GAG accumulation.

question: A 30-year-old man is brought to the physician by his wife because of a 1-day history of irrational behavior and severe abdominal pain. He began treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection 3 days ago. His urine turned a light burgundy color during a similar episode 1 year ago. His mother and his maternal grandfather have had similar symptoms. He appears anxious and restless. His pulse is 96/min. Physical examination shows diaphoresis. Serum studies show increased concentrations of 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) and porphobilinogen. The physician suspects that a mutant allele is causing decreased activity of an enzyme involved in heme biosynthesis. This enzyme is most likely which of the following?
explanation: Correct: Acute intermittent porphyria is due to porphobilinogen deaminase (hydroxymethylbilane synthase) deficiency; this enzyme is not among the options listed.
educational_objective: Acute attacks with ↑ALA and ↑PBG indicate porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency (AIP).

question: A 7-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because of increasingly severe left knee pain during the past 12 hours. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), pulse is 115/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 110/60 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a tender, swollen left knee that is unable to be flexed because of pain. Hematologic studies show a leukocyte count of 35,000/mm³ and erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 120 mm/h. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Correct: The acute, febrile, very painful, swollen joint with marked leukocytosis/ESR is most consistent with septic arthritis, which is not among the choices.
educational_objective: Acute monoarticular arthritis with fever and very high inflammatory markers suggests septic arthritis.

question: A group of men between the ages of 25 and 30 years and a group of men between the ages of 75 and 80 years were deprived of water for 24 hours. Renal function measurements for both groups are shown: 25-30 Years: Urine specific gravity 1.030, Urine osmolality (mOsmol/kg) 1100 75-80 Years: Urine specific gravity 1.020, Urine osmolality (mOsmol/kg) 350 Which of the following changes associated with aging is the most likely cause of the difference in urine concentrating ability between the two groups?

options.A: Decreased renal tubule responsiveness to ADH (vasopressin)
options.C: Increased sodium transport in the thick ascending loop of Henle

explanation: Correct: Elderly have impaired urinary concentrating ability largely due to decreased responsiveness to ADH and reduced medullary gradient. Incorrect: The other changes do not specifically explain the reduced concentrating response after dehydration.
educational_objective: Aging reduces renal concentrating capacity, partly via decreased tubular response to ADH.

question: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother 6 hours after she noticed that his urine was red. He is otherwise feeling well. Fifteen days ago, the patient had a sore throat, fever and cough. His mother thought he had the flu and treated him symptomatically with rest and analgesics, and his status improved until now. His temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 100/50 mm Hg. Physical examination shows normal breath and cardiac sounds, no organomegaly, and 1+ lower extremity edema, bilaterally. Laboratory studies show: Serum: Urea nitrogen 40 mg/dL, Creatinine 2 mg/dL, Albumin 3.0 g/dL Urine: Color red-brown, Blood 3+, Protein 2+, Ketones negative, RBC 30-50/hpf, RBC casts few Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Correct: This presentation is classic for poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis (acute nephritic syndrome), which is not among the options listed.
educational_objective: Poststreptococcal GN causes hematuria with RBC casts, mild edema, and renal dysfunction after pharyngitis.

question: A 9-year-old girl is brought to the clinic by her mother because of areas of hair loss on her scalp that the mother first noticed 1 week ago. The patient otherwise has been well. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. She receives no medications. The patient transferred from her neighborhood elementary school to a private school for gifted children 3 months ago. The mother says that no one in the house has used new shampoos, soaps, or detergents recently. The patient's growth and development have been normal. The child appears healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the scalp shows two irregularly shaped, quarter-sized areas of alopecia on the right side of the head. Short, broken hairs are noted within these areas, but there is no scaling or erythema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Trichotillomania presents with irregular patches of hair loss with broken hairs of varying length and no inflammation. Alopecia areata shows smooth patches without broken hairs. Hypothyroidism causes diffuse hair thinning, not patchy alopecia. Menkes disease causes brittle, kinky hair due to copper metabolism defects, not localized alopecia.
educational_objective: Trichotillomania causes patchy alopecia with broken hairs and no inflammation.

question: A75-year-old woman is brought to the physician because of a 1-day history of fever and back pain. Her temperature is 39.5DC (1G3.1T), pulse is 111/min; respirations are 32/min. and blood pressure is 115/79 mm Hg. Physical examination shows left-sided costovertebral angle tenderness. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 17.0DG/mm3(with 9% bands) and pyuria. Urine cultures grow Escherichia coil, it is determined that the patient's fever is partially due to interleukin-G (IL-6), which was induced by the IL-1 produced during the immune response. Which of the following best describes the role of IKB in the nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-KB) signal transduction pathway from IL-1 binding to IL-S induction in this patient? Medical Exam Questions

options.A: Facilitates proteolytic cleavage of NF-KB dimers
options.C: Translocates to the nucleus after undergoing phosphorylation

explanation: NF-κB is sequestered in the cytoplasm by IκB. Upon phosphorylation and degradation of IκB, NF-κB translocates to the nucleus to induce cytokine genes. IκB does not phosphorylate NF-κB, undergo cleavage of NF-κB dimers, or translocate itself.
educational_objective: IκB binds and inhibits NF-κB until released, regulating inflammatory gene transcription.

question: A female newborn delivered at 26 weeks' gestation is found to have hyaline membrane disease. She is intubated and mechanically ventilated. Her vital signs are continuously monitored, and inspired oxygen is maintained at a level that will sustain an oxygen saturation between 92% and 95%. The primary goal of this treatment is protection of which of the following structures?
explanation: Supplemental oxygen in preterm infants can cause retinopathy of prematurity due to VEGF dysregulation and retinal neovascularization . The basal ganglia, choroid plexus, and cochlea are not directly affected by oxygen therapy.
educational_objective: Excess oxygen in preemies damages the retina, causing retinopathy of prematurity.

question: A 20-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her roommate 30 minutes after she ingested a large quantity of acetaminophen tablets during a suicide attempt. The physician asks her why she tried to kill herself. She replies tearfully, "My boyfriend told me that he doesn't want to see me again, and he won't return any of my phone calls. I loved him more than I've loved anyone else in my entire life. I was going to marry him! Now I hate his guts for what he's done to me. I just wanted to die." On further questioning, the physician learns that she had only two dates with this man. She tells the physician, "I just can't bear being alone. But I can tell that you understand. You're the only doctor who's ever understood how I feel." This patient most likely has which of the following types of personality disorders?
explanation: Borderline PD is characterized by unstable relationships, impulsivity, fear of abandonment, and suicidal behavior. Dependent PD is excessive need for care but without suicidality. Histrionic PD is attention-seeking, not intense anger/idealization. OCPD involves perfectionism and rigidity.
educational_objective: Borderline personality disorder causes instability, fear of abandonment, and self-harm.

question: A 54-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of fatigue and a persistent cough productive of colorless mucoid sputum. She also has had a 14-kg (30-lb) weight loss during this period. She has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes daily for 25 years. She is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and now weighs 52 kg (115 lb); BMI is 19 kg/m². Percussion of the chest shows hyperresonance. Her serum calcium concentration is 12.8 mg/dL. A chest x-ray shows a mass in the right middle lobe of the lung near the hilum. Examination of aspirate from the mass shows malignant cells. The neoplasm in this patient is most likely which of the following?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is strongly linked to smoking and produces PTHrP → hypercalcemia . Adenocarcinoma is more peripheral and does not typically secrete PTHrP. Large cell carcinoma is undifferentiated but less commonly hypercalcemic. Giant cell carcinoma is rare.
educational_objective: Squamous cell lung carcinoma causes PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia.

question: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his father because of bleeding from a cut on his left arm after he fell off his tricycle 1 hour ago. Physical examination shows a 2-cm shallow laceration on the left upper extremity. The laceration has stopped bleeding and is covered with a clot. This finding results from hepatic synthesis of which of the following?

options.C: Proteins that result in the production of fibrin strands

explanation: Coagulation factors synthesized in the liver form fibrin strands to stabilize clots. Platelet production is from bone marrow, not the liver. Plasmin promotes clot breakdown, not formation. Inhibitors of anticoagulants do not directly form fibrin.
educational_objective: The liver produces clotting factors that generate fibrin to stabilize hemostatic plugs.

question: A 70-year-old man comes to the office because of a 6-day history of abdominal pain. He has no history of major medical illness and takes no medications. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows epigastric tenderness. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a mass in the liver. As part of a study, electron microscopy of a biopsy specimen of the mass is done. Results show nuclear chromatin margination under the nuclear membrane, intact cell membranes, and cells that are smaller in size than normal cells in the tissue. The mechanism causing the cell size anomaly in this patient was most likely triggered by the release of which of the following substances into the cytoplasm?
explanation: Cytochrome c release from mitochondria activates caspases and intrinsic apoptosis. BAX promotes cytochrome c release but is not the final trigger. BCL2 prevents apoptosis. Procaspase-9 is downstream of cytochrome c release.
educational_objective: Cytochrome c release from mitochondria activates caspases and initiates apoptosis.

question: A 20-year-old man with sickle cell disease has chronic hemolytic anemia and has frequent painful crises that require transfusions. Hydroxyurea treatment significantly decreases the painful crises and transfusion requirements. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of the beneficial effects of this treatment?

options.B: Increased affinity of hemoglobin S for oxygen

explanation: Hydroxyurea increases HbF, which interferes with HbS polymerization. It does not alter oxygen affinity, HbS concentration, or dehydration directly.
educational_objective: Hydroxyurea reduces sickle crises by increasing HbF production.

question: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of developmental delay. He has a history of a cleft palate that was repaired surgically at the age of 1 year. He did not walk until the age of 18 months and did not speak any words until the age of 20 months. His height and weight are at the 5th percentile; his head circumference is below the 5th percentile. Examination shows ptosis and a smooth philtrum. Maternal use of which of the following substances during pregnancy is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Fetal alcohol syndrome causes growth restriction, microcephaly, smooth philtrum, midface hypoplasia, and neurodevelopmental delay. Cocaine causes placental abruption, heroin causes withdrawal, nicotine causes low birth weight.
educational_objective: Fetal alcohol exposure causes facial dysmorphisms and developmental delay.

question: A study is conducted to assess body mass index (BMI) in a group of 100 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Results show a mean (± standard error of the mean) BMI of 31 kg/m² (± 4 kg/m²). The 99% confidence intervals for this measurement are 20.7 to 41.3. The 95% confidence intervals are 23.3 to 38.8. Based on this information, which of the following best represents the number of individuals who have a BMI between 38.3 kg/m² and 41.3 kg/m²?
explanation: SEM = 4, CI width corresponds to 2.58×SEM for 99% CI. Distribution implies ~4% of patients lie in each tail at 95% CI, about 4 individuals between 38.3–41.3.
educational_objective: Confidence intervals estimate population spread; ~4% of sample falls in extreme tails.

question: A 44-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination 1 month after receiving a cadaveric kidney transplant. He says he feels well. Current medications include mycophenolate and prednisone. Physical examination shows an arteriovenous fistula in the left upper extremity and a well-healing surgical wound over the right lower quadrant of the abdomen. Serum studies show a urea nitrogen concentration of 44 mg/dL and creatinine concentration of 2.6 mg/dL compared with 21 mg/dL and 1.8 mg/dL, respectively, 2 weeks ago. Examination of a biopsy specimen of the transplanted kidney shows an inflammatory infiltrate affecting the small arterioles. These changes are most likely caused by which of the following mechanisms? cells

options.A: Donor CD4+-T lymphocytes recognize class II MHC molecules on host lymphocytes
options.B: Donor CD8+-T lymphocytes recognize class I MHC molecules on host dendritic cells
options.C: Host CD8+ T lymphocytes recognize class I MHC molecules on renal allograft cells

explanation: Acute cellular rejection is mediated by host T cells attacking donor MHC. Donor lymphocytes mediate graft-vs-host disease, not kidney rejection.
educational_objective: Acute rejection occurs when host T cells recognize donor MHC antigens.

question: A 25-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 6-week history of daytime fatigue, irritability, and emotional lability; he has had a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss during this period. He says that he is sleep-deprived, but he is unable to fall asleep readily. He is a medical student and has recently finished an intensive care unit rotation where he often worked days and nights. He is currently on an outpatient rotation and will be starting vacation next week. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following recommendations by the physician is most appropriate to improve this patient's sleep hygiene?

options.A: "Make sure you sleep late whenever you can to catch up on your sleep."
options.B: "Stay in bed even if you can't fall asleep."
options.C: "Try getting up the same time every day, even if you didn't get much sleep."

explanation: Consistent wake times entrain circadian rhythm. Alcohol disrupts sleep. Staying in bed awake worsens insomnia. Catching up late disrupts rhythm further.
educational_objective: Consistent wake time is key for restoring circadian sleep patterns.

question: A 45-year-old man is undergoing a surgical procedure. Which of the following maneuvers by the anesthesiologist would result in an increase in intracranial pressure?
explanation: Lower RR → ↑ CO₂ (hypercapnia) → cerebral vasodilation → ↑ ICP. Increasing FiO₂ or RR lowers ICP. Lowering airway pressure decreases ICP.
educational_objective: Hypercapnia increases intracranial pressure via cerebral vasodilation.

question: A 5-year-old boy who had intrauterine growth restriction has continued to grow slowly. Psychomotor development is normal. His parents are of average stature. Genetic studies show that he has uniparental maternal heterodisomy for chromosome 7. Which of the following mechanisms best explains his slow growth?

options.A: Expression of an autosomal dominant disorder
options.B: Expression of an autosomal recessive disorder

explanation: Uniparental disomy can unmask recessive mutations if both copies are inherited from one parent. It is not trinucleotide repeat, AD expression, or mosaicism.
educational_objective: Uniparental disomy can unmask autosomal recessive diseases.

question: A 66-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of swelling of his right elbow that began after he struck it against the edge of a file cabinet earlier that day. On physical examination the tip of the olecranon is obscured by a golf ball-sized fluctuant mass with well-defined borders. The mass is swollen, mildly tender and smooth. Range of motion of the elbow is normal. Which of the following structures was most likely injured in this patient?
explanation: Localized fluctuant swelling at olecranon indicates olecranon bursitis. Tendon, cartilage, capsule, and synovium are deeper or cause restricted motion.
educational_objective: Olecranon bursitis is inflammation of the bursa from trauma or pressure.

question: Which of the following abnormalities is most likely to result from occlusion of the vessel indicated by the arrow in the vertebral angiogram shown?
explanation: Occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) causes lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome, which classically involves the spinal trigeminal nucleus/tract, producing loss of pain and temperature sensation from the ipsilateral face【turn13file0†First Aid USMLE Step 1 2024.pdf†L9-L16】. Contralateral facial weakness and contralateral visual field deficits are cortical/brainstem motor or occipital lobe phenomena, not typical of PICA lesions. Ipsilateral lateral gaze palsy (abducens/PPRF lesion) is more consistent with pontine (e.g., AICA/basilar) involvement rather than lateral medulla.
educational_objective: PICA (lateral medullary) infarcts cause ipsilateral facial pain/temperature loss due to spinal trigeminal nucleus/tract involvement.

question: A full-term female newborn is evaluated shortly after birth. Pregnancy and delivery were uncomplicated. During the first 5 minutes after delivery, which of the following is most likely to be increased in this newborn?

options.C: Venous return when the umbilical cord is ligated

explanation: At birth, the first breaths drop pulmonary vascular resistance, which increases pulmonary blood flow; rising O₂ and loss of placental prostaglandins also promote ductus arteriosus closure【turn16file4†First Aid USMLE Step 1 2024.pdf†L20-L26】. Flow from PA→aorta via the ductus falls, pulmonary artery pressure falls, and venous return from the umbilical vein decreases after cord ligation.
educational_objective: Immediately after birth, decreased PVR increases pulmonary blood flow and functionally closes fetal shunts.

question: A 30-year-old woman comes to the physician for a health maintenance examination. She is training for a marathon and has been running up to 20 miles daily. She states that as long as she has adequate caloric intake, she feels well on long-distance runs of up to 20 miles. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Her fasting serum glucose concentration is 60 mg/dL. After her glucose stores have been depleted, which of the following organs, in addition to the liver, is most likely to release newly produced glucose in this patient?
explanation: Gluconeogenesis enzymes (including glucose-6-phosphatase) are present primarily in liver but also in kidney and intestinal epithelium; these tissues can generate and release free glucose during fasting【turn17file0†First Aid USMLE Step 1 2024.pdf†L81-L88】. Pancreas and thyroid do not release appreciable glucose; adrenals produce steroids, not net glucose.
educational_objective: Besides the liver, the kidney performs gluconeogenesis and can release glucose via glucose-6-phosphatase.

question: A 10-year-old girl is referred to a cardiologist because of a 6-year history of a murmur. She is asymptomatic. Physical examination shows a grade 2/6, systolic ejection murmur heard over the left sternal border. An ECG shows right axis deviation and right ventricular hypertrophy. She undergoes cardiac catheterization. Oxygen saturation findings are shown in the block diagram. This patient most likely has which of the following congenital heart defects?
explanation: ASD produces a left-to-right shunt with increased O₂ saturation ("step-up") in RA, RV, and pulmonary artery and a systolic ejection murmur with wide fixed split S2【turn16file12†First Aid USMLE Step 1 2024 (1).pdf†L23-L36】【turn16file12†First Aid USMLE Step 1 2024 (1).pdf†L32-L36】. Abnormal pulmonary venous return causes different physiology; membranous VSD shows step-up at RV/PA only【turn16file12†First Aid USMLE Step 1 2024 (1).pdf†L17-L18】.
educational_objective: ASD causes step-ups in O₂ saturation in RA, RV, and PA with wide fixed split S2.

question: A 65-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of substernal chest pain that occurs after eating. Physical examination shows no abnormalities except for systolic hypertension. Results of an exercise stress test are positive. The table shown depicts the results of an exercise stress test in 1000 patients at similar risk compared with the presence or absence of coronary artery disease (CAD). Based on these data, which of the following is the pretest probability of CAD in this patient?
explanation: Why correct: Pretest probability equals the disease prevalence in a comparable population before the test is performed. If 520 of 1000 similar-risk patients truly have CAD, the pretest probability is 520/1000 = 52%. First Aid emphasizes that post-test metrics depend on the pretest probability (prevalence) and that PPV/NPV vary with prevalence. Why others are wrong: 35% and 48% do not match the disease prevalence implied by the 1000-patient table; pretest probability is not derived from sensitivity/specificity alone.
educational_objective: Pretest probability is the disease prevalence in a comparable population prior to testing; it anchors how to interpret a positive or negative result.

question: A 57-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasingly severe joint pain and weakness during the past 2 months. Physical examination shows pallor. Laboratory studies show specific values and Philadelphia (Ph¹) chromosome present. A chimeric growth-promoting protein with which of the following activities is most likely encoded in this patient due to the presence of this chromosome?
explanation: Why correct: The Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) creates BCR-ABL, a constitutively active tyrosine kinase driving CML. Why others are wrong: cAMP is a second messenger, not the chimeric protein's activity; DHFR and MAP kinase are not the hallmark activity of BCR-ABL.
educational_objective: The Philadelphia chromosome creates BCR-ABL, a constitutively active tyrosine kinase that drives CML.

question: A 70-year-old woman comes to the physician for advice after her husband of 45 years suddenly dies of cardiac arrest. She wants to donate $1,000,000 to a small city's department of public health to decrease the number of sudden cardiac deaths. She asks the physician to recommend the most effective way to put this money to use. She says, "I want to see the results of my donation over the next 1 to 2 years." The patient is most likely to accomplish her goal if she contributes to which of the following? city age of 50 years

options.A: Creation of a citywide aerobic exercise program
options.B: Fortification of the water supply with aspirin
options.C: Provision of free HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor drugs to everyone in town over the
options.D: Provision of free relaxation and stress-management programs for all adults

explanation: Why correct: Statins reduce LDL and reduce mortality in patients with CAD and are foundational for primary prevention in higher-risk older adults. Broad, immediate pharmacologic primary prevention in those ≥50 (higher baseline risk) is most likely to reduce near-term fatal coronary events compared with lifestyle programs that yield benefits more slowly. Why others are wrong: Anti-smoking and exercise programs are highly valuable but tend to show population mortality effects over longer horizons. Aspirin water fortification is unsafe/implausible; stress-reduction programs do not meaningfully reduce sudden cardiac death at the population level.
educational_objective: In higher-risk populations, statin deployment produces meaningful near-term reductions in fatal coronary events; population lifestyle programs typically need longer to shift mortality.

question: A 45-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of a 6-hour history of constant right flank pain, fever, pain with urination, and blood in the urine. Antibiotic treatment was initiated 2 weeks ago for a urinary tract infection caused by Proteus mirabilis. She is writhing on the hospital bed, unable to find a comfortable position. Her temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 30/min, and blood pressure is 160/80 mm Hg. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities except for tenderness of the right flank to palpation. Urinalysis shows 1+ blood and a pH of 7.5. A spiral CT scan of the abdomen shows a staghorn right renal calculus. This renal calculus is most likely composed of which of the following?
explanation: Why "best of given options": Urease-positive organisms (e.g., Proteus) alkalinize urine and classically form struvite (ammonium magnesium phosphate) staghorn calculi. Struvite is not listed; among the choices, calcium phosphate preferentially forms in alkaline urine, making it the closest available answer. Why others are wrong: Calcium oxalate forms in any pH (often normoacidic), uric acid stones form in acidic urine and are radiolucent; cystine stones are due to cystinuria and classically in younger patients.
educational_objective: Proteus (urease+) infections create alkaline urine and classically cause struvite staghorn stones; if struvite isn't an option, calcium phosphate (alkaline-favored) is the closest choice.

question: A 64-year-old homeless man with alcoholism is brought to the emergency department by police after he was found wandering aimlessly in a city park. He has weakness, fatigue, and hunger. He appears disheveled and cachectic. His temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 134/82 mm Hg. Physical examination shows mild scleral icterus, numerous skin abrasions, and 1+ edema of the lower extremities. He is oriented to person but not to place or time. Laboratory studies show specific values. A photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear is shown. A deficiency of which of the following best accounts for the hematologic findings in this patient?
explanation: Alcoholics are prone to folate deficiency due to poor intake; smear shows macrocytic megaloblastic changes. Iron deficiency causes microcytosis; B6 deficiency causes sideroblastic anemia; copper deficiency causes microcytic anemia/neuropathy.
educational_objective: Chronic alcoholism causes folate deficiency leading to megaloblastic anemia.

question: A 37-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after her husband found her unconscious. Her temperature is 36°C (96.8°F), pulse is 128/min. and blood pressure is 70/40 mm Hg. Physical examination shows cool pale extremities, jugular venous distention, faint peripheral pulses; and crackles over the bottom two thirds of both lung fields. Heart sounds are normal and there are no murmurs. She withdraws to painful stimuli in at! four extremities. This patient is most likely experiencing which of the fallowing types of shock?
explanation: Findings: hypotension, JVD, pulmonary edema → pump failure (cardiogenic). Hypovolemic shock has flat neck veins; septic/anaphylactic are distributive with warm extremities, not JVD.
educational_objective: Cardiogenic shock presents with low BP, high JVP, pulmonary edema.

question: A 16-year-old boy with intellectual disability is admitted to the hospital because of severe respiratory distress. Physical examination shows dislocation of the ocular lenses bilaterally, dyspnea, and tenderness and edema of the left lower extremity. Serum concentrations of methionine and homocysteine are increased and serum cystine concentration is decreased. This patient most likely has a defect of which of the following enzymes? NBME Comprehensive Basic Science Self-Assessment Questions
explanation: Homocystinuria due to cystathionine β-synthase deficiency causes ↑homocysteine and methionine, ectopia lentis, thrombosis, and developmental delay. γ-Cystathionase deficiency would cause low cystathionine; fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency causes tyrosinemia I; methylmalonyl-CoA mutase deficiency causes methylmalonic acidemia.
educational_objective: Cystathionine β-synthase deficiency causes classic homocystinuria with elevated homocysteine/methionine, lens dislocation, and hypercoagulability.

question: A previously healthy 32-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of heavy menstrual bleeding, intermittent nosebleeds, and blood in her urine and stools. She says, "I've had to stop flossing because my gums bleed for an hour afterwards." Physical examination shows numerous ecchymoses and petechiae over the lower extremities. A test result for circulating antiplatelet antibodies is positive. Which of the following is the most likely pathogenesis of this patient's disease?
explanation: Immune thrombocytopenia is due to autoantibodies against platelet glycoproteins causing peripheral destruction and impaired function; patients bleed from mucosal surfaces with petechiae. "Inability of platelets to be released," "megakaryocyte dysfunction," and "monosomy 7" refer to production/marrow disorders (eg, myelodysplasia), not antibody-mediated disease.
educational_objective: Autoantibodies against platelet surface glycoproteins cause immune-mediated platelet dysfunction and destruction, leading to mucocutaneous bleeding.

question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because of a 5-month history of behavioral problems. Treatment with valproic acid, which inhibits histone deacetylase, is started. This drug is most likely to affect which of the following processes in this patient?
explanation: Histone deacetylase inhibition increases histone acetylation, opens chromatin, and increases transcription, which ultimately increases mRNA available for translation; among the choices, the downstream process most directly increased is translation. mRNA splicing and polyadenylation are post-transcriptional processing steps; post-translational processing occurs after protein synthesis.
educational_objective: HDAC inhibition increases gene expression by opening chromatin; the net effect is more mRNA and increased translation.

question: A 30-year-old woman has excessive gingival bleeding 3 hours after a tooth extraction. Laboratory studies show normal platelet count and morphology, but moderately increased bleeding time and moderately suppressed Factor VIII activity and Ristocetin cofactor activity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? disease
explanation: vWD causes increased bleeding time (platelet adhesion defect), decreased ristocetin cofactor activity, and can lower FVIII (vWF stabilizes FVIII). Hemophilia A/B cause normal bleeding time with markedly low FVIII or FIX; end-stage liver disease reduces multiple factors but not isolated ristocetin activity.
educational_objective: vWF deficiency impairs platelet adhesion and decreases FVIII stability, causing mucocutaneous bleeding with abnormal ristocetin testing.

question: In some inherited disorders of collagen, lysyl oxidase activity is deficient. This enzyme forms a reactive aldehyde that interacts with which of the following amino acid residues of another collagen molecule to cause cross-linking?
explanation: Lysyl oxidase (copper-dependent) oxidatively deaminates lysine to allysine, enabling covalent lysine–hydroxylysine cross-linking that stabilizes collagen fibrils. Other residues listed are not the principal cross-linking targets.
educational_objective: Collagen cross-linking requires lysyl oxidase-mediated covalent bonds between lysine residues.

question: A 75-year-old man has painless lesions that are rough to the touch. He worked outside for 30 years maintaining golf course grounds. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Chronic sun exposure causes premalignant, rough, scaly erythematous/brown papules (actinic keratoses) with risk of progression to SCC. Angiomas and xanthelasma are smooth vascular/lipid lesions; seborrheic keratoses are "stuck-on" waxy plaques.
educational_objective: Actinic keratoses are sun-induced, rough, scaly premalignant lesions that can progress to SCC.

question: A 79-year-old woman with severe dementia is brought to the ED with chest pain and agitation. ECG shows ST-segment elevation in anterolateral leads. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: ST-segment elevation localized to anterolateral leads indicates transmural myocardial infarction (STEMI), a form of ACS. Acute pericarditis typically shows diffuse ST elevation and PR depressions; pneumonia/PE do not cause focal ST-elevation patterns.
educational_objective: ST-segment elevation in regional leads indicates transmural MI (STEMI), an acute coronary syndrome.

question: A 70-year-old man has coronary artery bypass grafting. Post-operatively, his creatinine rises from 1 to 4.5 mg/dL with urine output of 15 mL/h. Which of the following best explains these findings?

options.B: Atheromatous emboli dislodged by balloon pump
options.C: Toxic acute tubular necrosis induced by hemolysis

explanation: Post-operative ischemia commonly causes ATN with oliguria and rising creatinine; path shows granular "muddy brown" casts. AIN is typically drug-induced with eosinophils; atheroemboli often show livedo; hemolysis-induced toxic ATN would have evidence of hemolysis.
educational_objective: Ischemic injury after surgery commonly causes ATN with oliguria and granular casts.

question: A 45-year-old man with Li-Fraumeni syndrome has a p53 mutation (R243P) that alters hydrogen bonding with DNA. Which of the following is the most likely result of this mutation on transcription of genes that inhibit cell division?
explanation: p53 is a transcription factor; loss of DNA binding impairs recruitment of the transcriptional machinery to promoters, reducing transcription of cell-cycle inhibitors (eg, p21). It does not directly change DNA or RNA polymerase binding capacity in the absence of TF recruitment and certainly does not increase TF/DNA polymerase binding.
educational_objective: p53 loss reduces transcriptional activation of cell-cycle inhibitors due to impaired DNA binding by a transcription factor.

question: A 50-year-old woman is on mechanical ventilation after motor vehicle collision. The most effective way to decrease arterial PCO2 in this patient is to increase which of the following?
explanation: PaCO₂ ∝ CO₂ production / alveolar ventilation; raising minute ventilation (RR×VT) lowers PaCO₂. Increasing respiratory frequency (at same VT) increases minute ventilation. Changes in inspiratory/expiratory time, PEEP, or tube size don't reliably lower PaCO₂.
educational_objective: Increase minute ventilation (eg, raise respiratory rate) to reduce PaCO₂ on mechanical ventilation.

question: A 47-year-old woman has acute asthma-like breathing difficulty, diarrhea and flushing for 4 months. Chest x-ray shows a 2.3-cm lung mass. Urine 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid is increased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Bronchial carcinoid secretes serotonin → flushing, diarrhea, wheezing; ↑urine 5-HIAA. Adenocarcinoma and SCC are not associated with carcinoid syndrome; lymphoma does not cause 5-HIAA elevation.
educational_objective: Bronchial carcinoid tumors can secrete serotonin, producing carcinoid syndrome with ↑5-HIAA.

question: A 2-month-old boy has hypotonia, poor feeding, large fontanels, midface hypoplasia, hepatomegaly, and cryptorchidism. Serum shows increased very-long-chain fatty acids, phytanic acid, and pipecolic acid. Electron microscopy would most likely show absence of which organelles?
explanation: Zellweger spectrum disorders (peroxisome biogenesis defects) cause accumulation of VLCFAs, phytanic acid, and pipecolic acid with hypotonia and dysmorphism; mitochondria, ER, and lysosomes are intact.
educational_objective: Peroxisomal biogenesis defects cause accumulation of VLCFAs and characteristic neonatal hypotonia/dysmorphism.

question: An animal study assesses effects of smoking on pulmonary defense mechanisms. Rats are exposed to cigarette smoke for 1 week. Which of the following sets of changes is most likely to be observed?

options.A: ↑ Mucus production, ↑ Macrophage function, ↓ Ciliary activity
options.B: ↑ Mucus production, ↓ Macrophage function, ↓ Ciliary activity
options.C: ↓ Mucus production, ↓ Macrophage function, ↑ Ciliary activity
options.D: ↓ Mucus production, ↓ Macrophage function, ↓ Ciliary activity

explanation: Cigarette smoke increases mucus production, impairs mucociliary clearance (↓ ciliary beating), and decreases alveolar macrophage function, predisposing to infection.
educational_objective: Smoking increases mucus, impairs cilia, and suppresses macrophages, weakening pulmonary defenses.

question: A 70-year-old man has difficulty sleeping since his wife died 5 months ago. He sometimes wakes early, cries when thinking of his wife, and once followed a woman who resembled her. He enjoys visits with grandchildren and remains active in bowling. Which is the most appropriate initial action?
explanation: This is normal bereavement (grief) within 12 months of the loss with preserved function and intermittent yearning; reassure and monitor. Neuropsych testing, sleep studies, or sedating antihistamines are unnecessary and potentially harmful.
educational_objective: Normal grief is managed with empathy and follow-up; pharmacotherapy is not routinely indicated.

question: A 38-year-old woman with asthma has nasal congestion, cough, and shortness of breath. Lab shows peripheral eosinophilia. Chest x-ray shows peripheral infiltrates with pleural effusion. Lung biopsy shows necrotizing vasculitis, granulomas, and eosinophilic necrosis. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: EGPA presents with adult-onset asthma, eosinophilia, and necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis with eosinophils. Goodpasture causes anti-GBM alveolar hemorrhage/glomerulonephritis; sarcoidosis has noncaseating granulomas without necrotizing vasculitis; GPA (Wegener) lacks eosinophilia and asthma.
educational_objective: EGPA combines asthma, eosinophilia, and necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis.

question: A 65-year-old man dies in motor vehicle collision. Autopsy shows left kidney and distal left ureter lesions. Right kidney is normal. Which was the most likely predisposing factor for the ureteral lesion?
explanation: Multifocal urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma can involve renal pelvis, ureter, and bladder. The strongest, most common risk is tobacco smoke (others include aromatic amines and cyclophosphamide). Unilateral left kidney/ureter involvement is consistent with urothelial carcinoma risk from smoking. Vinyl chloride → hepatic angiosarcoma; schistosomiasis → squamous bladder cancer; alcoholism is unrelated.
educational_objective: Tobacco use is the leading modifiable risk factor for urothelial carcinoma along the collecting system.

question: A 25-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 20 weeks' gestation has routine prenatal visit. Her respirations increased from 16/min pre-pregnancy to 22/min now. Which best explains the increased respirations?

options.A: Metabolic adjustment for fetal lung immaturity
options.C: Respiratory compensation for fetal metabolic CO2 production

explanation: Pregnancy produces a mild respiratory alkalosis due to progesterone-driven hyperventilation to excrete the increased CO₂ load (maternal plus fetal), increasing minute ventilation even without lung disease.
educational_objective: Progesterone in pregnancy increases minute ventilation, producing a mild respiratory alkalosis to handle maternal–fetal CO₂.

question: An investigator studies human immune response to tumor cell antigens. Which cancer type and tumor antigen combination is most likely to produce the highest antibody titer?
explanation: Highly overexpressed, surface growth factor receptors (HER2/neu) can be strongly immunogenic and elicit higher antibody titers than differentiation antigens shared with normal cells (eg, CD19 on B cells) or intracellular enzymes (eg, tyrosinase, PAP). (Conceptual; no patient care hinges on this nuance.)
educational_objective: Overexpressed, accessible tumor antigens (eg, HER2) tend to elicit stronger humoral responses than self-lineage markers.

question: An investigator studies Wernicke encephalopathy. Thiamine deficiency causes downregulation of glial high-affinity glutamate transporter before neuron loss. Which cells are most likely initially affected?
explanation: High-affinity glutamate transporters clearing synaptic glutamate are on astrocytes; thiamine deficiency (Wernicke) initially impairs astrocytic functions before neuronal death.
educational_objective: Astrocytes regulate extracellular glutamate; their dysfunction precedes neuron injury in thiamine deficiency.

question: A 13-year-old girl has facial and back blemishes for 8 months. Physical exam shows scattered comedones and papules. Treatment with a medication that decreases epidermal cell cohesion and increases cell turnover is initiated. Which drug was most likely prescribed?
explanation: Topical retinoids (tretinoin) normalize desquamation, decrease keratinocyte cohesion in the follicular infundibulum, and increase cell turnover—key in comedonal acne. Benzoyl peroxide is antimicrobial/comedolytic; clindamycin is antibacterial; metronidazole is for rosacea.
educational_objective: Retinoids reduce keratinocyte cohesion and increase turnover to treat comedonal acne.

question: An investigator wants to determine if coffee drinking is associated with pancreatic cancer. Coffee drinking histories of persons with cancer were compared with those of healthy persons. Which best describes this type of study?
explanation: Case-control studies compare prior exposures (here, coffee) in people with disease (cases) versus those without (controls). Cohorts follow exposure forward; RCTs randomize interventions; ecologic studies use group-level data; case series lack controls.
educational_objective: In case-control studies, you look back to compare exposures in cases vs controls.

question: An investigator studying gastric acid secretion observes that energy needed to secrete 1.0 nmol of H⁺ is 7 × 10⁻⁹ kcal. How many ATP molecules must be hydrolyzed during secretion of one H⁺ ion?
explanation: Gastric H⁺ secretion uses the H⁺/K⁺ ATPase; one ATP hydrolysis powers the export of one H⁺ (conceptual energy accounting). Thus ~1 ATP per H⁺ ion.
educational_objective: H⁺/K⁺ ATPase couples one ATP to pump H⁺ against its gradient across the parietal cell membrane.

question: A 41-year-old man has 6-week history of numbness of his right hand. He works in construction. Sensation to pinprick is decreased in the thumb and anterior forearm. The physician suspects compression of C5 and C6 spinal nerves. Weakness of which movement on the right is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?
explanation: C5–C6 innervate deltoid (axillary n.) and supraspinatus (suprascapular n.)—key for arm abduction. Adduction of index finger (ulnar; C8–T1), wrist flexion (C7), and shoulder elevation (CN XI) don't match C5–6 radiculopathy.
educational_objective: C5–C6 radiculopathy impairs deltoid/supraspinatus function → weak shoulder abduction.

question: A 20-year-old man has 2-day history of profuse watery diarrhea after returning from Central America. He appears alert but dehydrated with BP 90/60. Compared with a healthy individual, laboratory studies are most likely to show which findings?
explanation: Profuse secretory diarrhea causes non–anion gap metabolic acidosis (↓HCO₃⁻) with respiratory compensation (↓PCO₂) and total body K⁺ loss (↓K⁺).
educational_objective: Diarrhea → metabolic acidosis with low HCO₃⁻ and compensatory hyperventilation; K⁺ is lost.

question: A feature of host response to malaria in experimental animals is activation of CD8⁺ T lymphocytes with specificity for malaria antigens. Which is the best explanation for this response? molecules

options.A: Invasion of malaria parasite into cell cytoplasm leads to processing and presentation by class I MHC
options.B: Malaria genome encodes glycoproteins that mimic class I MHC molecules
options.C: Malaria parasite plasma membrane contains superantigen specific for CD8⁺ T lymphocytes

explanation: Dendritic cells can cross-present exogenous antigens on MHC I to activate CD8⁺ T cells, explaining cytotoxic responses to noncytosolic parasites.
educational_objective: Cross-presentation allows exogenous parasite antigens to be presented on MHC I, activating CD8⁺ T cells.

question: A 52-year-old man develops shortness of breath and near-fainting while exercising. He has 6-month history of similar episodes becoming increasingly severe, and 2-month history of exertional chest pain. Cardiac exam shows systolic murmur best heard at upper right sternal border. Which is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Symptomatic aortic stenosis in a relatively young adult often reflects calcification of a congenital bicuspid aortic valve; degenerative trileaflet calcific AS predominates at older ages.
educational_objective: Early-onset calcific AS is commonly due to a congenital bicuspid aortic valve.

question: A 22-year-old woman steps on glass while jogging on beach. After wound cleaning and suturing, she has numbness around sutures for 3 days, then normal sensation returns in 3 weeks. Which cell type most likely facilitated reinnervation of the skin?
explanation: Peripheral axon regrowth is guided by Schwann cells (bands of Büngner) that remyelinate and direct regenerating axons. Astrocytes and satellite cells are CNS/PNS glial not involved in axon elongation in skin; fibroblasts/keratinocytes repair tissue, not axons.
educational_objective: Schwann cells guide and remyelinate regenerating peripheral axons.

question: During an experiment, a knockout mouse strain is developed with isolated deficiency of carbonic anhydrase in erythrocytes only. Compared with normal mice, venous blood in the knockout mouse will most likely have higher concentration of which substance?
explanation: Without RBC carbonic anhydrase, less tissue CO₂ is converted to HCO₃⁻ inside RBCs, so less HCO₃⁻ exits in exchange for Cl⁻; consequently, venous plasma retains more Cl⁻ (less "chloride shift" into RBCs).
educational_objective: RBC carbonic anhydrase drives the chloride shift; its loss leads to relatively higher venous plasma Cl⁻.

question: An 82-year-old woman has 1-week history of light-headedness and fainting. She takes propranolol for hypertension. Pulse is 45/min, BP 90/50. ECG shows normal P waves and QRS complexes. Physician decreases propranolol dose. Five days later pulse is 80/min and symptoms resolve. Which best explains the low pulse while taking higher dose propranolol?

options.B: Increased calcium influx during late phase of slow depolarization
options.C: Increased potassium influx during rapid depolarization
options.D: Increased sodium efflux during early repolarization

explanation: β-blockade reduces cAMP, decreasing funny current (If) and L-type Ca²⁺ current in SA/AV nodal cells → slower phase-4 depolarization and bradycardia. None of the listed answer choices matches this mechanism.
educational_objective: β-blockers slow nodal phase-4 depolarization by reducing If/ICaL, lowering heart rate.

question: A 58-year-old woman has 3-month history of mild urine leakage when washing hands or hearing water running. No leakage with coughing or sneezing. No nocturia, hesitancy, or straining. Which is the most likely cause of this patient's incontinence? contractions E) Urinary tract infection

options.C: Detrusor overactivity (urge incontinence triggered by conditioned stimuli)

explanation: Leakage with running water suggests urge incontinence from involuntary detrusor contractions (conditioned reflex). Stress incontinence presents with cough/sneeze; overflow causes dribbling with incomplete emptying; UTI can worsen urgency but is not the mechanism here.
educational_objective: Urge incontinence = involuntary detrusor contractions; stress = ↑intra-abdominal pressure; overflow = incomplete emptying.

question: A clinical trial is conducted to compare the efficacy of a surgical procedure versus medical management of gastroesophageal reflux disease. In the study, 300 patients are randomly assigned to either the surgical procedure group or the medical management group; each group consists of 400 patients. Of the patients assigned to the surgical procedure group, 75 do not undergo the operation during the study period. Of the patients assigned to the medical management group, 50 undergo the operation during the study period. In an intention-to-treat analysis, which of the following most accurately represents how many patients would be analyzed in the surgical procedure and medical management groups, respectively? Surgical Procedure Group | Medical Management Group
educational_objective: Intention-to-treat analyzes patients in the groups to which they were randomized, regardless of adherence or crossover; group sizes remain as randomized (400

question: A 34-year-old man with AIDS comes to the physician because of muscle aches and reddish brown urine for 12 hours. He began treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 day ago as prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii (formerly P. carinii) infection. A sample of blood after centrifugation shows red serum. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these changes?

options.B: Precipitation of sulfamethoxazole leads to cystitis
options.C: Trimethoprim imparts a red color to body fluids

explanation: Sulfonamides precipitate oxidative hemolysis in G6PD deficiency → intravascular hemolysis and hemoglobinemia (red serum). AIN causes hematuria, not hemoglobinemia; TMP doesn't color fluids red; cystitis from crystalluria doesn't explain hemoglobinemia.
