He says that these symptoms happen each spring, when grass and tree pollens are abundant. Which of the following types of drugs is most likely to be effective in relieving these symptoms in the short term?
explanation: Topical nasal α-agonists (e.g., phenylephrine/oxymetazoline) rapidly reduce congestion via vasoconstriction (beware rebound with prolonged use). β-agonists affect bronchi; nicotinic agents are irrelevant; α-antagonists worsen congestion.
educational_objective: Topical α-adrenergic agonists provide rapid decongestion in allergic rhinitis.

question: A healthy 22-year-old man participates in a study that analyzes the effects of various therapies on gastrointestinal motility. A manometric tracing of this man is shown. This manometric pattern is most likely due to binding of which of the following neurotransmitters with its respective receptor in the stomach?
explanation: Migrating motor complex activity during fasting is driven by motilin acting on motilin receptors in the stomach/proximal small bowel. ACh increases peristalsis but MMCs are motilin-mediated; NE/VIP inhibit motility.
educational_objective: Fasting MMCs are mediated by motilin in the stomach and small intestine.

question: A healthy 30-year-old woman is traveling on a commercial airliner where the cabin's barometric pressure is measured at 565 mm Hg. The inspiratory partial pressure of alveolar oxygen in this woman is most likely which of the following (in mm Hg)?
educational_objective: At reduced barometric pressure, PAO₂ falls; use the alveolar gas equation to estimate.

question: Cytogenetic analysis of 20 metaphases from the peripheral lymphocytes of a 15-year-old girl with gonadal dysgenesis (Turner syndrome) shows the karyotype 45,X in 11 metaphases and 46,XX in 9 metaphases. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this result?
explanation: Mitotic (postzygotic) nondisjunction creates mosaicism (two cell lines). Recombination and LOH are not mechanisms for 45,X/46,XX mosaicism; X-inactivation is normal and wouldn't yield monosomy X.
educational_objective: Turner mosaicism typically arises from postzygotic mitotic nondisjunction.

question: A healthy 20-year-old man comes to the physician with his wife for genetic counseling prior to conception. His sister died of cystinosis, an autosomal recessive disorder affecting cystine transport across lysosomal membranes. The incidence of this disorder in the general population is approximately 1/40,000. The wife's history is noncontributory. The wife's risk for being a carrier of this disorder is closest to which of the following?
explanation: For AR disease, q²≈1/40,000 ⇒ q≈1/200; carrier frequency ≈2q≈1/100. Closest option is 1/50 among choices given.
educational_objective: For rare AR traits, carrier frequency ≈2√incidence; pick the closest option if exact value isn't listed.

question: A 45-year-old man develops multiple punctate, erythematous, nonblanching, 1-mm lesions on the upper and lower extremities and the belt line. A defect in which of the following is the most likely cause of the patient's symptoms?
explanation: Petechiae reflect thrombocytopenia/decreased platelet production (e.g., marrow failure). Defects in protein catabolism or toxin metabolism cause other syndromes; protein C affects coagulation (thrombosis), not primary hemostasis.
educational_objective: Thrombocytopenia from decreased platelet production causes petechiae.

question: The kinetics of a regulatory enzyme are shown in the figure as curve A. The kinetics in the presence of an allosteric modifier are represented by curve B. Which of the following best describes the effect of the modifier on the activity of this enzyme?
explanation: A typical allosteric activator shifts the curve left (greater affinity, ↓Km). A pure Vmax change without Km shift is less characteristic; complete inhibition/no effect don't fit an altered kinetic curve.
educational_objective: Allosteric activators commonly decrease apparent Km (left shift), increasing enzyme affinity.

question: A 20-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of pain in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen and vaginal bleeding for 2 days. Her last menstrual period was 8 weeks ago. Which of the following historic findings further increases the likelihood of an ectopic pregnancy in this patient?
explanation: Smoking increases the risk of ectopic pregnancy due to impaired ciliary motility and tubal function. Prior vaginal delivery, HIV status, or a history of spontaneous abortions are not established ectopic risk factors like smoking, PID, or prior tubal surgery.
educational_objective: Cigarette smoking impairs tubal transport and increases ectopic pregnancy risk.

question: An otherwise healthy 15-year-old boy is brought to the physician 2 days after the onset of a headache. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows mild tenderness over the right occipital area. An x-ray of the skull shows a 2-cm lytic lesion in the right occipital bone. A photomicrograph of a biopsy specimen of the lesion stained with hematoxylin and eosin is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Lytic skull lesions in adolescents with H&E showing coffee-bean nuclei and eosinophils are classic for Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Solitary bone cysts are metaphyseal and usually in long bones; meningioma and metastatic carcinoma do not fit a solitary pediatric skull lytic lesion.
educational_objective: Lytic skull lesions in youth strongly suggest Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

question: Patients with a history of deep venous thrombosis are recruited as part of a research study on chronic venous insufficiency. The patients are evaluated at the beginning of the study and reevaluated 2 years later. At the second visit, they are asked if they wore compression stockings since the study began. The prevalence of venous insufficiency in those who wore the stockings is compared to those who did not. Which of the following best describes this type of study?
explanation: At analysis, groups are defined by outcome (venous insufficiency present vs absent) and prior exposure (stocking use) is compared retrospectively, which is characteristic of a case–control design. It is not a clinical trial (no randomization) or a case series (descriptive only).
educational_objective: When outcome groups are compared for prior exposures, the design is case–control.

question: A 25-year-old man is admitted to the hospital after he sustained second-degree burns over 70% of his body while fighting a fire. Administration of fluid and antibiotics is started. Two days later, he develops dyspnea, tachypnea and hypoxemia. Diffuse crackles are heard on auscultation of the chest. A chest x-ray shows fluffy alveolar infiltrates. Despite appropriate intervention, he dies. Autopsy shows diffusely firm and hyperemic lungs. Microscopic examination of the lung tissue shows widening of the alveolar septa and eosinophilic hyaline membranes lining the alveolar spaces. Which of the following pathologic mechanisms is the most likely cause of the pulmonary disorder in this patient?

options.A: Amniotic fluid leak across intervening membranes

explanation: ARDS (diffuse alveolar damage) features endothelial and epithelial injury with protein-rich edema and hyaline membranes. It is not bacterial invasion, pure atelectasis, or type I hypersensitivity.
educational_objective: ARDS results from diffuse alveolar-capillary injury causing hyaline membrane formation.

question: A 65-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes mellitus suddenly develops continuous involuntary ballistic movements of her right arm and leg. She is alert and neurologic examination shows no other abnormalities. The most likely cause of this patient's movement disorder is infarction involving which of the following areas of the brain on the contralateral side?
explanation: Hemiballismus results from a lesion of the contralateral subthalamic nucleus, disinhibiting the thalamus and causing wild flinging movements.
educational_objective: Lesions of the subthalamic nucleus cause hemiballismus.

question: A healthy 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents because of a long history of disruptive behavior at school and poor academic performance. During class, he talks out of turn; wanders around the room; and pesters classmates. He is easily distracted and cannot keep his attention on a topic very long. His homework is sloppy and usually incomplete; he often explains that he leaves segments of assignments undone because he "just didn't notice them." He has had similar problems since kindergarten. He has normal developmental milestones. He is bright and cheerful and has a caring family. A drug with which of the following actions is most likely to be useful for this patient?
explanation: Stimulants (methylphenidate/amphetamines) increase synaptic norepinephrine and dopamine, improving attention and behavior in ADHD.
educational_objective: Stimulants for ADHD increase synaptic NE and dopamine.

question: A 40-year-old man with alcoholism is admitted to the hospital because of a 2-day history of confusion. Serum studies show a sodium concentration of 99 mEq/L. He is treated with 0.9% saline. Four days later he develops slurred speech. Physical examination shows mild-to-moderate muscle weakness of all extremities and dysarthria. Sensation is intact. Babinski sign is present bilaterally. These findings are most likely caused by a lesion in which of the following locations?
explanation: Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia can cause osmotic demyelination syndrome (central pontine myelinolysis) in the pons/brainstem, producing dysarthria and quadriparesis with intact sensation.
educational_objective: Rapid sodium correction can cause pontine demyelination (brainstem).

question: A 30-year-old woman comes to the physician for evaluation of recurrent postprandial retrosternal burning occurring three times weekly during the past 6 months. The symptoms occur only during the day and are noticeably more severe after large meals; especially if she eats fried foods. Initially, the symptoms responded well to over-the-counter antacids, but in the past 2 months, the antacids have failed to control her symptoms. She had similar symptoms 5 years ago during pregnancy that also responded well to antacids and then resolved after the delivery of her child. She has had no difficulty swallowing, weight loss, or gastrointestinal bleeding. She is sleeping well. She takes no other medications and does not smoke cigarettes or drink alcohol. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her condition?
explanation: GERD commonly results from transient LES relaxations (vagally mediated), often worse after large/fatty meals and during pregnancy. The other choices misstate gastrin/somatostatin effects.
educational_objective: Transient, vagally mediated LES relaxations underlie typical GERD.

question: A 17-year-old boy has septic shock that is unresponsive to intravenous ADH (vasopressin) therapy. This treatment is discontinued, and high-dose dopamine therapy is initiated. Stimulation of which of the following receptors is most likely to be of benefit to this patient?

options.B: Dense lymphocytic infiltrates and interstitial edema

explanation: In refractory septic shock, α₁ agonism increases systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure. β₁ supports inotropy; D₂ effects are not beneficial in shock resuscitation.
educational_objective: α₁ agonism raises SVR and MAP in vasodilatory shock.

question: A 5-year-old boy is stung on his foot by a bee. Within 30 minutes the local area is edematous. The extravascular accumulation of fluid is most directly related to which of the following?
explanation: Histamine and other mediators cause endothelial contraction (gaps) that increase vascular permeability, leading to edema. Demargination, vasodilation, or fibrin thrombi do not directly cause the fluid exudation.
educational_objective: Inflammation increases vascular permeability via endothelial gap formation.

question: A 43-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine health maintenance examination. The physician is 30 minutes late for the appointment because of an emergency, and when he enters the examining room, the patient checks her watch. Which of the following initial statements by the physician is most appropriate?

options.B: Decreases H+ secretion in the distal tubule
options.C: Decreases magnesium reabsorption in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
options.D: Increases HCO3- secretion in the proximal tubule

explanation: A straightforward apology that acknowledges the delay and offers accommodation respects the patient's time without making excuses or minimizing concerns. The other options deflect, boast, or trivialize.
educational_objective: Begin with a sincere apology and offer to accommodate the patient when you are late.

question: A 67-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after she fainted while grocery shopping. On arrival, she is conscious. Her blood pressure is 115/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows carotid pulses with small amplitude and a delayed upstroke. A grade 4/6, crescendo systolic murmur that is heard throughout the precordium is loudest at the upper right sternal border and radiates to the carotid arteries. There is a loud S₄. A chest x-ray shows no cardiomegaly. This patient most likely has which of the following cardiac valve abnormalities?
explanation: Classic findings of AS include pulsus parvus et tardus, harsh crescendo systolic murmur radiating to carotids, and S₄ from a stiff ventricle.
educational_objective: Harsh systolic murmur radiating to carotids with delayed upstroke indicates aortic stenosis.

question: A previously healthy 73-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of pain with urination and a 12-hour history of fever and chills. His temperature is 38.3°C (101°F). Physical examination shows moderate tenderness of the left flank. Urinalysis shows 50 to 100 WBC/hpf. Culture of urine grows 100,000 colonies/mL of a gram-positive organism. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

options.B: Intraoperative vagus nerve injury during the operation
options.C: Overdose with midazolam used as preoperative sedation

explanation: Enterococcus (gram-positive cocci) commonly causes UTIs in older men with outlet obstruction. E coli is gram-negative; S pyogenes and Shigella are not typical UTI pathogens.
educational_objective: Enterococcus is a common gram-positive cause of UTI in older men.

question: A 53-year-old woman is diagnosed with gastric carcinoma and receives a chemotherapeutic regimen including doxorubicin. Six months later she develops cardiomyopathy. Dose-limiting toxicity of doxorubicin, resulting in cardiomyopathy, is produced by which of the following mechanisms?
explanation: Anthracyclines generate free radicals causing dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy.
educational_objective: Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity results from free radical–mediated myocyte injury.

question: A full-term newborn has respiratory distress. Imaging studies show herniation of abdominal contents into the left pleural cavity. Maldevelopment of which of the following structures is most likely to have caused the defect of the diaphragm?
explanation: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia most commonly results from a posterolateral (Bochdalek) defect; among the given choices, a defect involving the posterior crural region best approximates this posterior diaphragmatic failure.
educational_objective: Posterior (Bochdalek) defects in diaphragm development allow abdominal contents to herniate into the thorax.

question: An 18-month-old girl is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination because of macrosomia. She was 53 cm (21 in) in length and weighed 4200 g (9 lb 4 oz) at birth. She is now at the 95th percentile for length and weight. Physical examination shows a nevus flammeus on the forehead, a large tongue, and an abdominal mass. Abdominal ultrasonography shows a tumor in the left kidney. A biopsy specimen of the resected mass shows nephroblastoma (Wilms tumor). Genetic testing of the patient shows abnormal methylation at KCNQ1OT1 (DMR2) of maternal 11p15. Which of the following genetic mechanisms is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome results from abnormal imprinting at 11p15 (altered methylation/parent-of-origin effects), predisposing to overgrowth and Wilms tumor.
educational_objective: Parent-of-origin–specific epigenetic changes (imprinting) underlie Beckwith–Wiedemann.

question: A randomized, double-blind, clinical trial of a new medication for acute stroke was just completed. The results are summarized as follows: Treatment Group: 17% Disability, 13% Mortality Placebo (n=90): 40% Disability, 30% Mortality Active drug (n=39): Relative Risk (95% Confidence Interval) - Disability 0.67 (0.44-0.89), Mortality 0.77 (0.43-1.11) Compared with the placebo group, which of the following sets best summarizes the relative risks in the active drug group?

options.A: Exclude the outcome for only those who inadvertently switched to the other study medication
options.B: Exclude the outcome for only those who reported stopping the medication altogether
options.C: Include the outcome for each participant in the group to which he or she was randomized

explanation: The disability CI excludes 1 (significant reduction); the mortality CI includes 1 (not significant).
educational_objective: Interpret RRs with 95% CIs: excluding 1 indicates significance.

question: A 65-year-old man with hypertension volunteers to participate in a clinical trial of a newly developed loop diuretic. As part of the study, his acid-base/volume status is monitored. After 3 days of treatment which of the following sets of findings is most likely in this patient?
explanation: Loop diuretics cause NaCl diuresis (volume contraction) and increased distal Na⁺ delivery leading to H⁺/K⁺ loss (contraction metabolic alkalosis).
educational_objective: Loop diuretics produce volume contraction and contraction alkalosis.

question: A 45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of a 6-week history of swelling of his face, legs, and left testicle. He says that his blood pressure has been higher than normal (>170/100 mm Hg) during the past 2 months. At his last visit 1 year ago, his serum creatinine concentration was 2.1 mg/dL. He is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 100 kg (220 lb); BMI is 31 kg/m². His blood pressure is 172/93 mm Hg. Physical examination shows marked edema around the eyes and of the lower extremities to the level of the thighs. The left side of the scrotum is 1½ times the size of the right side and enlarges further when the patient bears down. Palpation shows a lumpy mass just superior to the normal-sized left testis. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these scrotal findings?
explanation: A "bag of worms" mass superior to the testis that enlarges with Valsalva is a varicocele (dilated pampiniform plexus).
educational_objective: Varicoceles dilate with Valsalva and feel like a "bag of worms" above the testis.

question: A 2-month-old male infant has jaundice and pale stools caused by congenital biliary atresia. Deficiency of which of the following is most likely in this patient?
explanation: Cholestasis impairs absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K). Among the options, only vitamin E is fat-soluble.
educational_objective: Biliary obstruction causes fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies.

question: A 72-year-old woman comes to the physician because of diffuse muscle pain and weakness for 6 months. The muscle pain is exacerbated by activity. Physical examination shows proximal muscle weakness and tenderness over the surface of both shins. The dot on the nomogram shown indicates the relationship between her serum calcium and parathyroid hormone concentrations. Which of the following conditions is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
explanation: Osteomalacia (vitamin D deficiency) causes bone pain (classically over shins), proximal muscle weakness, and secondary hyperparathyroidism (normal/low Ca²⁺ with elevated PTH on a Ca–PTH nomogram). Hypoparathyroidism has low PTH; primary hyperparathyroidism has high Ca²⁺ with high/"inappropriately normal" PTH; metastatic breast cancer usually causes hypercalcemia from osteolysis.
educational_objective: Vitamin D deficiency leads to osteoid mineralization defects with bone pain, proximal weakness, and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

question: A 57-year-old man undergoes coronary artery bypass grafting. The stress of the operation results in increased secretion of cortisol from the adrenal gland postoperatively. Which of the following cells is the most likely origin of the stimulus of this cortisol secretion?

options.A: The amino acid sequence of a protein derived from a given mRNA can vary
options.B: The code is not universal throughout the biologic species
options.C: A common codon exists for at least two amino acids
options.D: There is a remarkable degree of inaccuracy during transcription

explanation: Corticotrophs (a basophil subtype in the anterior pituitary) secrete ACTH, which stimulates adrenal cortisol release under stress. Acidophils (somatotrophs/lactotrophs), pancreatic α/δ cells, and posterior pituitary pituicytes are not the ACTH source.
educational_objective: ACTH from anterior pituitary basophils (corticotrophs) drives stress-induced cortisol secretion.

question: A mildly obese 42-year-old woman comes to the physician 2 days after the sudden onset of chest pain and intermittent cough while she was doing laundry. Medications include oral contraceptives. She has smoked 1½ packs of cigarettes daily for 24 years. She appears somewhat anxious. An x-ray of the chest shows normal findings, and an ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Ventilation-perfusion lung scans show a defect in the anterior inferior segment of the right upper lobe. Collateral arterial flow is provided to this area by which of the following arteries?
explanation: In pulmonary embolism, pulmonary arterial flow is blocked; systemic bronchial circulation can partially perfuse affected parenchyma. Bronchial arteries arise from the thoracic aorta (or intercostals) and anastomose with anterior intercostals from the internal thoracic system; among options, internal thoracic best represents systemic collateral input. Brachiocephalic and right coronary do not supply lung parenchyma; "left pulmonary" is the occluded circuit.
educational_objective: Systemic (bronchial) arterial supply provides collateral perfusion to lung parenchyma when pulmonary arterial flow is obstructed.

question: A 24-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 1, comes to the physician because of nervousness and tremor since delivering a healthy female newborn 6 weeks ago. She also has had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss during this period. She has a history of panic disorder and carpal tunnel syndrome. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 100/min, and blood pressure is 140/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a firm thyroid gland that is twice the normal size. Serum studies show a free thyroxine (FT₄) concentration of 2.4 ng/dL (N=0.8-2.4), thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration of less than 0.03 μU/mL and 24-hour thyroid radioactive iodine uptake of 1% (N=8-25%). Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's symptoms?
explanation: Postpartum (painless) thyroiditis is a lymphocytic destructive thyroiditis causing transient thyrotoxicosis from release of preformed hormone with low RAI uptake. Graves disease would show high uptake and TSH receptor antibodies; anaplastic cancer causes rapid mass effects; hypothyroidism doesn't fit hyperthyroid labs.
educational_objective: Postpartum thyroiditis causes low-uptake thyrotoxicosis due to inflammatory release of preformed hormone.

question: A 32-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-week history of a progressive, itchy rash. The rash initially appeared as an oval patch on her abdomen and has since spread over her abdomen and back. She has not had fever, chills, or sweating. She has no history of major medical illness. She has been sexually active with two male partners during the past year, and she uses an oral contraceptive. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows the findings in the photograph. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Dorsal surface of the lateral hand
options.D: Palmar surface of the lateral hand

explanation: Pityriasis rosea begins with a herald patch followed by a "Christmas tree" distribution of scaly oval plaques on trunk. Erythema infectiosum has slapped-cheek rash; scabies is intensely pruritic with burrows; secondary syphilis has systemic features and palm/sole involvement; molluscum shows umbilicated papules.
educational_objective: A herald patch followed by a truncal "Christmas tree" eruption is classic for pityriasis rosea.

question: A 39-year-old woman, gravida 5, para 5, with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of gallstones comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of nausea, vomiting, and midabdominal pain radiating to her back. She is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall and weighs 82 kg (180 lb); BMI is 30 kg/m². Physical examination shows bluish discoloration of both flanks and epigastric tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Grey Turner sign (flank ecchymosis) with epigastric pain radiating to the back is typical of severe acute pancreatitis (risk factors: gallstones, alcohol). Cholangitis presents with Charcot triad; ruptured aneurysms cause shock/hemoperitoneum.
educational_objective: Severe acute pancreatitis can present with flank ecchymosis (Grey Turner sign) and back-radiating epigastric pain.

question: A 35-year-old woman who is being examined because of infertility receives an injection of contrast material into her cervix to visualize the reproductive tract before undergoing radiographic tests. On the hysterosalpingogram shown, the contrast material (as indicated by the arrows) is also seen in the peritoneal cavity. Which of the following best explains this finding?
explanation: During a normal hysterosalpingogram, contrast fills the uterus and patent tubes, then freely spills into the peritoneal cavity; the appearance is expected and not a pathologic rupture.
educational_objective: Free intraperitoneal spillage of contrast on HSG indicates patent fallopian tubes and is expected.

question: Fatty acids are infused into the proximal small intestine of an experimental animal. Which of the following is the most likely change in peptide secretion in this animal?
explanation: Luminal fats stimulate I-cells to release CCK, which increases gallbladder contraction and pancreatic secretion and slows gastric emptying. Fats suppress motilin; secretin responds to acid; amylase secretion is secondary to CCK/vagal effects (not primarily increased by fat alone among listed options).
educational_objective: Fat in the duodenum increases CCK release, coordinating fat digestion.

question: An investigator is studying the effects of several different drugs on human brain activity. During the study, positron emission tomography is used to measure real-time brain activity in human participants after administration of various drugs with abuse potential. Results show a common pattern of neurologic effects for drugs such as cocaine, amphetamines, opioids, sedative-hypnotics, alcohol and nicotine. Activation of which of the following neurotransmitter pathways best explains the rewarding or positive reinforcing effects of using these drugs?

options.A: Activation of γ-aminobutyric acid receptors in muscle spindle afferents
options.B: Activation of glutamate receptors in gamma motoneurons
options.C: Activation of serotonin receptors in alpha motoneurons
options.D: Inhibition of nicotinic receptors in Renshaw cells

explanation: Drugs of abuse increase dopamine signaling in the mesolimbic/mesocortical reward circuits (VTA↔nucleus accumbens/prefrontal cortex). Among choices, the dopaminergic pathway (albeit simplified) best reflects the reward axis; the others are not primary reward drivers.
educational_objective: The brain's reward pathway depends on increased dopaminergic signaling in mesolimbic/mesocortical circuits.

question: A 44-year-old man with a 1-year history of angina pectoris comes to the emergency department because of increasingly severe chest pain during the past 2 days. He has had five previous similar episodes, which required treatment with increasing doses of nitroglycerin to resolve. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 105/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows an S₄. An ECG shows ST-segment depression in the precordial leads. In addition to aspirin, heparin, and nitroglycerin, he is given a dose of a monoclonal antibody against the platelet IIb/IIIa receptor. This antibody will most likely prevent binding of which of the following substances to platelets?
explanation: GPIIb/IIIa is the platelet receptor that binds fibrinogen to cross-link platelets in aggregation. ADP activates platelets; thromboxane A₂ and thrombin are agonists but not the ligand for GPIIb/IIIa; adenosine inhibits.
educational_objective: GPIIb/IIIa inhibitors block fibrinogen binding, preventing platelet aggregation.

question: A 2-year-old boy has had recurrent sinopulmonary infections since 8 months of age. Flow cytometric analysis of his peripheral blood lymphoid cells with anti-CD3 and anti-IgM (with blockade of Fc receptor-mediated binding of IgG) is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Increased activation of glutamate receptors in the dorsal root ganglia
options.B: Increased activity of presynaptic γ-aminobutyric acid receptors in the dorsal horn
options.C: Increased activity of voltage-gated K+ channels in the thalamus
options.D: Persistent activation of voltage-gated Na+ channels in the nociceptor

explanation: Onset after maternal Ig wanes (~6–9 months) with recurrent bacterial infections and absent/very low B cells (no IgM⁺ cells on flow) is classic for Bruton (BTK) agammaglobulinemia. ADA deficiency causes SCID; IgA deficiency has normal B cells; hyper-IgM has normal/↑IgM B cells.
educational_objective: Bruton agammaglobulinemia presents after 6 months with recurrent infections and absent B cells.

question: A 16-year-old girl comes to the physician because of worsening acne over her forehead for the past month. She began a vegetarian diet 6 months ago; she also has been craving and eating large amounts of chocolate. She currently works outdoors as a flag person for a local road construction company and is required to wear a helmet. Her brother received a chinchilla for a pet 2 months ago. Physical examination shows erythematous papules and pustules on the forehead. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the exacerbation of this patient's condition?

options.A: Impaired binding of O2 to hemoglobin
options.D: Unbalanced synthesis of α- and β-globin chains

explanation: Occlusion/friction from headgear (acne mechanica) exacerbates acne on the contact area. Chocolate and vegetarian diet are not proven major triggers; pet allergy would not localize to the forehead; construction materials allergy causes dermatitis, not acne.
educational_objective: Occlusion and friction (helmets, headbands) can worsen acne in contact areas.

question: An 18-year-old woman comes to the physician because of irregular menstrual periods since menarche at the age of 13 years. Menses occur at 60- to 120-day intervals. She takes no medications. She does not smoke cigarettes, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She is sexually active with one partner and they use condoms consistently. She is 157 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 75 kg (165 lb); BMI is 30 kg/m². Physical examination shows facial hirsutism. Pelvic examination shows no cervical motion tenderness or masses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: PCOS features hyperandrogenism (hirsutism), chronic anovulation (oligo/amenorrhea), and obesity. Adrenal insufficiency causes hypotension and amenorrhea; CAH presents earlier with virilization; hyperaldosteronism does not cause hirsutism/oligo-ovulation.
educational_objective: PCOS presents with anovulation and hyperandrogenism leading to irregular menses and hirsutism.

question: A 32-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of palpitations and intermittent headaches. She has a 10-year history of poorly controlled hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide and metoprolol. Her blood pressure is 180/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. CT scans of the abdomen are shown; the arrows indicate an abnormality. An abnormality of which of the following structures is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: Episodic headaches, palpitations, and severe hypertension with an adrenal mass suggest pheochromocytoma (adrenal medulla). Liver, gallbladder, portal vein, or right kidney do not explain catecholamine surges.
educational_objective: Pheochromocytoma of the adrenal medulla causes episodic catecholamine excess and hypertension.

question: A 41-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination 6 weeks after the diagnosis of hypertension was made. Her blood pressure today is 162/104 mm Hg. A right abdominal bruit is heard. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Serum studies show Na⁺ 135 mEq/L, K⁺ 3.2 mEq/L, Cl⁻ 105 mEq/L, HCO₃⁻ 28 mEq/L, Urea nitrogen 9 mg/dL, Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. On renal arteriography, sampling shows a left renal vein renin activity of 5 μU/mL (N=5-97) and right renal vein renin activity of 176 μU/mL (N=5-97). The systemic hypertension in this patient is directly mediated by a vasoconstrictor that emerges from which of the following?
explanation: Unilateral renal artery stenosis increases renin from ipsilateral JG cells; renin drives angiotensin II–mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone. While angiotensin II is generated systemically, the initiating vasoactive cascade emerges from renin release by JG cells. Chromaffin cells (epi), afferent/efferent arterioles are not the renin source.
educational_objective: Renal artery stenosis elevates renin from JG cells, driving angiotensin II–mediated vasoconstriction and hypertension.

question: In order to investigate possible treatment for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), experimental animals are anesthetized and subjected to smoke inhalation (cotton smoke) according to a well-established experimental protocol. The experimental animals are then given compounds designed to upregulate specific mediators involved in the inflammatory cascade. Upregulation of which of the following mediators would most likely prevent or ameliorate the lung injury induced in this experimental model of ARDS?

options.A: Consult a colleague for advice about treating a minor without parental consent
options.B: Discuss with her the need for testing her for other sexually transmitted diseases
options.D: Treat her infection and refer her to social services

explanation: IL-10 is anti-inflammatory and downregulates proinflammatory cytokines (eg, TNF-α, IL-1) and NF-κB signaling; increasing IL-10 can blunt diffuse alveolar damage. Incorrect: IL-1, TNF, and NF-κB amplify inflammation and would worsen ARDS.
educational_objective: Anti-inflammatory IL-10 counteracts cytokine-mediated lung injury in ARDS.

question: A 58-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of shortness of breath and chronic nonproductive cough. She has a 2-year history of difficulty swallowing, joint stiffness, and diffuse tightening of the skin of the face, neck, shoulders, arms, and fingers. She has had significant sensitivity to cold weather for 20 years, and she says that her hands turn white when they are exposed to the cold. Current medications include a histamine (H₂) blocking agent for a long-standing history of esophageal reflux. Biopsy specimens of the skin from 1 year ago are shown in the photomicrographs. Examination of the hands shows cutaneous ulceration, clawlike flexion deformity, and decreased joint mobility. An autoimmune disorder is suspected. Which of the following pulmonary disorders is most likely in this patient?
explanation: Long-standing limited/diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis commonly causes interstitial lung disease (fibrosis) ± pulmonary hypertension. Incorrect: Emphysema, pneumonia, PE, bronchiectasis, or primary lung cancers are less characteristic in this context.
educational_objective: Systemic sclerosis frequently leads to interstitial lung fibrosis.

question: An 80-year-old woman undergoes a brain biopsy of a cerebral mass. Immunofluorescence studies of a biopsy specimen show that the tumor cells contain intermediate filaments of the cytokeratin type. This patient's cancer cells most likely arose from which of the following cell types?

options.A: Complete paralysis of the face on the left side
options.B: Complete paralysis of the face on the right side

explanation: Cytokeratins are intermediate filaments of epithelial origin; tumors positive for cytokeratin are carcinomas. Incorrect: Astrocytes (GFAP), mesenchymal cells (vimentin), neurons (neurofilaments) have different markers.
educational_objective: Cytokeratin expression indicates epithelial (carcinoma) origin.

question: A 65-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. In addition to methotrexate therapy, a course of rituximab is initiated. Approximately 45 minutes after the first infusion of rituximab, the patient's temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), and she develops diffuse muscle pain. She does not have any difficulty breathing or swallowing and there are no signs of urticaria or angioedema. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

options.A: Anaphylaxis as a result of antibiotic hypersensitivity
options.C: Decreased risk for hemolytic uremic syndrome
options.D: Prolonged fecal excretion of the organism

explanation: Rituximab (anti-CD20) can cause an acute infusion (cytokine-release) reaction due to rapid B-cell activation/lysis and cytokine release. Not IgE-mediated basophil degranulation; NK activation or platelet aggregation are not typical mechanisms.
educational_objective: Rituximab infusion reactions reflect cytokine release from targeted B cells.

question: An investigator is conducting a study of natural killer cells and their role in destroying malignant tumors in experimental animals. This study is most likely to show that natural killer cells are particularly effective in destroying malignant tumors with which of the following characteristics?
explanation: NK cells target cells with downregulated MHC I (missing-self), common in many tumors/virus-infected cells. Altered glycolipids, oncofetal antigens, or adhesion protein forms are not NK-specific triggers.
educational_objective: NK cells preferentially lyse cells with low MHC I expression.

question: A 44-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer comes to the physician for an initial examination. She says, "I'm concerned about my future. Can you give me any advice?" She recently moved to the city because her husband changed jobs. She underwent a mastectomy for inflammatory breast cancer, and she completed a course of chemotherapy 2 months ago. Physical examination shows an absent left breast and a well-healed scar on the left side of the chest. There are no palpable lymph nodes. Which of the following initial responses by the physician is most appropriate?

options.A: Decreased expression of cyclin B during G2/M transition
options.B: Decreased phosphorylation of RB1 protein during G1-S transition
options.C: Genomic instability during S, G2 and M phases
options.D: Overexpression of p21, p27, and p57 proteins during all phases

explanation: Start with an open-ended assessment of the patient's understanding and concerns (Ask-Tell-Ask) before advising or handing out materials. Incorrect: Premature directing/support-group referrals or alarming statements undermine rapport.
educational_objective: Begin serious discussions by eliciting the patient's understanding and concerns.

question: A 6-day-old female newborn is brought to the physician by her parents because of a 3-day history of difficulty feeding, vomiting, and progressive lethargy. Her parents have noticed that her urine has a burnt-sugar odor. Physical examination shows lethargy and hypotonia. Deficiency of which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings in this patient?

options.A: Abduction of the index, middle, ring, and small fingers
options.C: Extension of the index, middle, ring, and small fingers

explanation: Maple syrup urine disease is due to deficiency of BCKD, leading to accumulation of leucine, isoleucine, and valine and the characteristic odor.
educational_objective: BCKD deficiency causes maple syrup urine disease.

question: A 19-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of pain in her left index finger. She injured it during a softball game when catching a ball. Physical examination shows erythema of the left index finger. The patient is unable to flex the distal phalanx when the proximal interphalangeal joint and metacarpophalangeal joints are restrained. Laboratory studies and x-rays of the left hand show no abnormalities. Which of the following structures is most likely injured in this patient?

options.C: Enhanced action of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) at GABAA receptors
options.D: Selective inhibition of uptake of serotonin at nerve terminals

explanation: FDP flexes the DIP joint; inability to flex the distal phalanx (with PIP/MCP blocked) localizes to FDP. EDI/extensor tendons extend; median/ulnar neuropathies present differently.
educational_objective: Loss of DIP flexion indicates FDP tendon injury.

question: A previously healthy 55-year-old man comes to the physician 2 months after he noticed a lump in his neck. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a 2.5-cm, firm, cervical lymph node on the lower right. A photomicrograph of a biopsy specimen of the node stained with hematoxylin and eosin is shown. Flow cytometry of lymphoid cells from the node yields the following phenotype: CD3 3%, CD19 70%, CD10 70%, Kappa 70%, Lambda 0%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: CD10⁺ germinal-center B-cell phenotype with monoclonal light-chain restriction fits follicular lymphoma. DLBCL is more aggressive and variable; marginal zone is CD10-; SLL/CLL is CD5⁺/CD23⁺, CD10-.
educational_objective: CD10⁺, light-chain–restricted B cells indicate follicular lymphoma.

question: A 58-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and pruritus over the past 6 months. She has noticed dark urine and pale stools. Examination shows jaundice and hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies reveal elevated alkaline phosphatase, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and positive antimitochondrial antibodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: PBC is autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts, seen in middle-aged women with AMA positivity and cholestatic labs.
educational_objective: AMA positivity with cholestasis in a woman indicates PBC.

question: A 46-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious at home. He was last seen well 6 hours ago. On arrival, his temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), pulse is 110/ min, respirations are 8/min, and blood pressure is 88/50 mm Hg. Physical examination shows pinpoint pupils. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's presentation?

options.C: Deficiency of enzyme activity in gonadal steroid hormone biosynthesis
options.D: Translocation of the SRY gene to one of the X chromosomes

explanation: Pinpoint pupils classically suggest opioid toxicity; among provided choices, benzodiazepine overdose best matches severe CNS/respiratory depression (others are inconsistent: cocaine causes mydriasis/HTN; PCP causes nystagmus/agitation; ethanol typically lacks miosis).
educational_objective: CNS depressant overdose (here best fit among options) presents with respiratory depression and hypotension.

question: A 23-year-old woman comes to the physician because of irregular menstrual cycles and excessive facial hair growth over the past year. Examination shows coarse facial hair and acne. Laboratory studies show elevated total testosterone and normal dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) concentrations. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
explanation: Normal DHEAS (adrenal marker) with elevated testosterone suggests an ovarian source (eg, Sertoli-Leydig tumor), not adrenal tumor or PCOS alone.
educational_objective: Elevated T with normal DHEAS indicates ovarian (not adrenal) androgen excess.

question: A 72-year-old man comes to the physician because of progressive shortness of breath over the past year. He has a 50-pack-year smoking history. Examination shows a barrel-shaped chest and decreased breath sounds bilaterally. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a PaO₂ of 55 mm Hg and a PaCO₂ of 50 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his hypoxemia?
explanation: COPD causes prominent V/Q mismatch leading to hypoxemia; diffusion limitation is uncommon at rest; low inspired O₂ requires altitude; pure hypoventilation alone doesn't explain the degree/pattern.
educational_objective: V/Q mismatch is the primary cause of hypoxemia in COPD.

question: A 6-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 3-day history of fever, sore throat, and malaise. He has a fine, erythematous rash on his trunk and extremities and a bright red tongue. A rapid antigen detection test for group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus is positive. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the rash in this patient?
explanation: Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins (Spe) act as superantigens causing the scarlatiniform rash. Not endotoxin, immune complex, or type IV reactions.
educational_objective: Scarlet fever rash is due to streptococcal superantigen exotoxins.

question: A 48-year-old man comes to the physician because of persistent pain in his right knee. He injured it while skiing 6 months ago and has had difficulty walking since. Examination shows tenderness along the medial joint line. Passive flexion and extension of the knee with simultaneous rotation of the tibia elicits a clicking sound. Which of the following structures is most likely injured in this patient?
explanation: Medial joint line pain with a palpable/auscultated click during provocative testing is classic for medial meniscal tear.
educational_objective: McMurray test with medial joint line pain/click indicates medial meniscal injury.

question: A 30-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive exertional dyspnea over the past 6 months. She has no history of smoking or illicit drug use. Examination shows elevated jugular venous pressure, a loud second heart sound, and peripheral edema. Echocardiography reveals enlargement of the right ventricle and pulmonary artery. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Primary (idiopathic) pulmonary arterial hypertension features medial hypertrophy/intimal proliferation of pulmonary arterioles. Hypoventilation and alveolar destruction are other etiologies; recurrent emboli cause chronic thromboembolic PH.
educational_objective: Idiopathic PAH results from pulmonary arterial smooth-muscle hyperplasia and remodeling.

question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician because of progressive difficulty walking over the past year. He has a history of alcohol use disorder and poor nutrition. Examination shows decreased position and vibration sensation in the lower extremities, spasticity, and hyperreflexia. Laboratory studies reveal macrocytosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's neurologic findings?
explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes subacute combined degeneration (dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal tracts), leading to sensory ataxia and spastic paresis.
educational_objective: B12 deficiency leads to combined degeneration of dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts.

question: A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of recurrent episodes of palpitations, sweating, and tremulousness. Laboratory studies obtained during an episode show hypoglycemia with elevated insulin and C-peptide levels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.D: Less circular and longitudinal smooth muscle

explanation: Endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia shows elevated insulin with elevated C-peptide; exogenous insulin has low/absent C-peptide.
educational_objective: Elevated insulin and C-peptide during hypoglycemia indicate insulinoma.

question: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive muscle weakness and difficulty climbing stairs. She also has a skin rash over her knuckles and eyelids. Laboratory studies show elevated creatine kinase levels. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Dermatomyositis is a humoral microangiopathy with complement/immune complex-mediated damage to small vessels (perimysial/perifascicular atrophy). Incorrect: CD8⁺ T-cell–mediated myocyte injury typifies polymyositis; AChR and presynaptic Ca²⁺ antibodies cause MG/LEMS.
educational_objective: Dermatomyositis involves antibody/complement-mediated microangiopathy of muscle.

question: A 26-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after collapsing during a soccer match. He has a history of occasional palpitations but no previous syncopal episodes. On arrival, his pulse is 40/min and blood pressure is 80/40 mm Hg. ECG shows complete atrioventricular block. Which of the following locations is most likely responsible for the escape pacemaker activity sustaining this patient's ventricular rhythm?
explanation: In complete AV block, ventricular escape rhythms (20–40/min) arise from His–Purkinje/ventricular pacemakers; a rate near 40 suggests Purkinje focus.
educational_objective: Idioventricular escape rhythms originate in His–Purkinje system when AV conduction fails.

question: A 45-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue, joint pain, and decreased libido over the past several months. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Examination shows hepatomegaly and skin hyperpigmentation. Laboratory studies reveal elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Hereditary hemochromatosis (HFE mutation) causes low/inappropriate hepcidin → increased intestinal iron absorption and iron overload.
educational_objective: Dysregulated hepcidin leads to excessive intestinal iron absorption in hemochromatosis.

question: A 68-year-old woman has had a fever and shortness of breath for the past week. X-rays of the chest show a right lower lobe infiltrate. Leukocyte count is 38,000/mm³. A peripheral blood smear is shown. Which of the following best describes her peripheral blood smear?
explanation: Severe infection can cause a reactive leukemoid picture; among options, the nonmalignant/reactive choice is reactive lymphocytosis (malignancies are inconsistent with acute infectious presentation).
educational_objective: Marked leukocytosis in infection is typically reactive rather than leukemic.

question: A 43-year-old woman dies after a 10-year illness characterized by irregular jerking movements of the extremities and a disjointed gait. She had profound dementia during the last 6 years of her life. Her father had a similar disorder and died at the age of 65 years. At autopsy, examination of this patient's brain is most likely to show severe atrophy of which of the following labeled structures in the MRI of the normal brain?
explanation: Huntington disease causes marked caudate (head) atrophy, leading to enlarged frontal horns; on labeled brain diagrams this is typically the caudate (often denoted "C").
educational_objective: Huntington disease features caudate nucleus atrophy.

question: A 43-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Ten years ago, he underwent cardiac valve replacement. Chest x-rays are shown. Based on these findings, which of the following valves was most likely replaced in this patient?
explanation: Prosthetic aortic valves typically project over the upper cardiac silhouette/ascending aorta region on chest radiographs; mitral valves are more posterior/inferior in position.
educational_objective: The radiographic position of a prosthetic ring near the aortic root indicates an aortic valve replacement.

question: A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 45 minutes after sustaining injuries in a motor vehicle collision. He has severe, sharp, right-sided chest pain. Breath sounds are decreased on the right, and there is hyperresonance in the right thorax. X-rays confirm multiple rib fractures. The most likely afferent pathway of this patient's chest pain is carried in which of the following nerves?

options.A: Attachment of the virus to the cell surface
options.B: Budding of the virus from the cell membrane
options.C: Fusion of the viral envelope and cell membrane
options.D: RNA splicing to produce an mRNA encoding the envelope glycoproteins

explanation: Rib fracture chest wall pain is somatic and travels in intercostal nerves; phrenic and vagus carry visceral afferents, and splanchnics are visceral autonomics.
educational_objective: Chest wall/rib pain is carried by intercostal nerves.

question: While lifting weights, a 24-year-old man develops a painful swelling in the right inguinal region that cannot be reduced. The photograph shows a segment of the small intestine resected at exploratory laparotomy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A strangulated loop (as in an incarcerated hernia) undergoes venous congestion and hemorrhagic infarction, pathophysiologically akin to volvulus (twist on mesentery) among the choices. Intussusception is telescoping in children; embolism causes pale infarcts; adhesions cause obstruction without this gross appearance.
educational_objective: Twisting/strangulation of bowel causes hemorrhagic infarction.

question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. He recently immigrated to the USA from Nigeria with his parents. He has red-bronze skin, red hair, and continual horizontal nystagmus. Genetic testing shows compound heterozygosity of the TYRP1 gene with a frame-shift and a nonsense mutation. These genetic changes most likely caused which of the following in this patient?
explanation: TYRP1 (tyrosinase-related protein 1) is required in eumelanin synthesis (DHICA pathway). Mutations (OCA3) reduce DHICA-derived eumelanin, producing "rufous" oculocutaneous albinism; tyrosinase absence is TYR gene defects.
educational_objective: TYRP1 mutations reduce DHICA-derived eumelanin.

question: A 19-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after falling on her outstretched right hand during a gymnastics competition. Physical examination shows tenderness of the anatomical snuff-box. An x-ray of the right wrist is shown. The most likely diagnosis is fracture of which of the following carpal bones?
explanation: Pain/tenderness in the anatomic snuff box localizes to a scaphoid fracture, at risk of avascular necrosis. (Among listed carpal bones, none matches; scaphoid is the correct diagnosis.)
educational_objective: Snuff-box tenderness indicates scaphoid fracture.

question: A 26-year-old woman comes to the physician for counseling prior to conception. Many members of her family had blistering of the skin in infancy and now have unusual marbled pigmentation of the skin. The underlying inherited condition is uniformly fatal to males in utero. A pedigree is shown. Which of the following is the most likely risk that this patient's live-born offspring will be affected?
explanation: Incontinentia pigmenti is X-linked dominant and male-lethal in utero; a heterozygous woman has a 50% risk for affected daughters and near-zero for liveborn sons.
educational_objective: X-linked dominant male-lethal disorders affect ~50% of daughters.

question: A study is conducted on patients with asthma to compare a new asthma treatment with a placebo. After 12 weeks of therapy, the mean symptom scores were 2.6 ± 0.1 in the treated group (n=103) and 3.1 ± 0.1 in the placebo group (n=100). The p-value is 0.035. The investigators state they chose a sample size of about 100 subjects per group to have an 80% power of detecting a mean difference of 0.4 at a significance level of 5%. When planning a study, which of the following is the meaning of "80% power"?
explanation: Power = 1−β is the probability of correctly rejecting the null hypothesis when the true effect (here, a 0.4 difference) exists; it's the chance of finding statistical significance if the effect is real.
educational_objective: Study power is the probability of detecting a true effect (significance) of the prespecified size.

question: A 52-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital because of shortness of breath due to malignant ascites and pleural effusion. She has had ovarian cancer for 3 years with multiple courses of aggressive chemotherapy. She feels emotionally and physically exhausted. Her primary care gynecologist suggests palliative care consultation, but her gynecologic oncologist recommends referral for inclusion in a clinical trial. The patient is distressed by this disagreement. Following thoracentesis and paracentesis, the patient calls her primary care internist to help address the conflict between the two physicians. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step for the internist to address the patient's concerns?
explanation: Start with direct communication and care coordination among treating physicians to align the plan with the patient's goals; risk management/ethics consults are secondary.
educational_objective: Resolve inter-physician conflicts by coordinating care and aligning with patient goals.

question: A 65-year-old woman with widely metastatic breast cancer unresponsive to chemotherapy is moved to an inpatient hospice. She has never married and has no children or siblings. Throughout her illness, a close friend has been with her during hospitalizations and office visits. The patient and her friend are distressed when they see a sign outside the hospice unit stating only family members are permitted to stay after visiting hours. Her friend says, "We can't bear to be apart." Which of the following responses by the physician is most appropriate?

options.A: Advise the patient that constant questioning of recommendations suggests a lack of trust, and that she should seek care from a provider in whom she has confidence.
options.B: Advise staff to ignore the patient's calls if they are too frequent.
options.C: Contact one of the patient's family members to engage his or her help in enforcing more responsible use of the physician's time.
options.D: Set conditions and establish limits for phone calls, and set up a regular schedule of office visits.

explanation: Recognize the patient-designated support person ("family of choice") and accommodate their presence in hospice.
educational_objective: Honor the patient's chosen support person in end-of-life care.

question: A 34-year-old woman has been feeling weepy and overwhelmed since delivering a healthy male newborn 6 weeks ago. She has had fatigue, irritability, and difficulty sleeping. She argues frequently with her husband and feels guilty about not enjoying her baby more. Which of the following statements by the physician is most appropriate?

options.A: Atrophy of the left upper extremity
options.B: Decreased proprioception in the right upper extremity
options.C: Decreased sensation in the left lower extremity
options.D: Weakness of the left lower area of the face

explanation: Postpartum mood symptoms warrant safety screening for suicidality; ask directly and nonjudgmentally.
educational_objective: In mood complaints, screen directly for suicidal ideation.

question: A 75-year-old man with dementia, Alzheimer type, is brought to the hospital by his wife because of cough, difficulty breathing, and agitation that began after breakfast 2 hours ago. His wife mentions that he has been coughing during meals for several weeks and takes longer to finish smaller portions of food. Imaging is consistent with aspiration pneumonia. He has no advance directives. In speaking with the patient's family, it is most appropriate for the physician to address the issue of a feeding tube in which of the following manners?
explanation: Feeding tubes do not reliably prevent aspiration and can add burdens/restraints; discuss risks/benefits aligned with patient preferences.
educational_objective: Feeding tubes often do not prevent aspiration in dementia; discuss realistic outcomes.

question: A 31-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-week history of pain and swelling in her left leg. She has a history of three miscarriages in the past year. Examination shows swelling, erythema, and tenderness of the left calf. Duplex ultrasonography shows an occlusive thrombus in the left popliteal vein. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: APLS causes hypercoagulability with venous thrombosis and recurrent fetal loss due to placental thrombosis.
educational_objective: Recurrent thrombosis + miscarriages suggest antiphospholipid syndrome.

question: A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressive shortness of breath over the past 6 months. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 45 years. Examination shows decreased breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion bilaterally. Pulmonary function tests show a decreased FEV1/FVC ratio and decreased diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO). Which of the following is the most likely cause of the decreased DLCO in this patient?
explanation: Emphysema (especially panacinar/centriacinar) destroys alveolar walls and capillary beds, reducing diffusing capacity.
educational_objective: Emphysema lowers DLCO via loss of alveolar–capillary surface area.

question: A 46-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of abdominal discomfort and yellowing of his skin for the past 2 weeks. He has a history of chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. Hepatitis B virus DNA is undetectable in serum, and hepatitis D virus RNA is present. Which of the following best explains this patient's current condition?
explanation: HDV requires HBsAg from HBV; superinfection of a chronic HBV carrier typically causes severe hepatitis even as HBV DNA may be low.
educational_objective: HDV superinfection (on chronic HBV) causes severe hepatitis.

question: A 9-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of progressive difficulty walking and frequent falls over the past year. His parents have also noticed curvature of his spine and thickening of his calves. Examination shows bilateral calf pseudohypertrophy, lumbar lordosis, and a waddling gait. Gowers sign is present. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (X-linked) due to dystrophin mutations causes progressive weakness and pseudohypertrophy.
educational_objective: Dystrophin deficiency causes Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

question: A 21-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of infertility. He and his partner have been attempting to conceive for 14 months without success. He has no history of major illnesses and takes no medications. Examination shows normal male hair distribution and external genitalia. Semen analysis shows low sperm concentration and reduced motility. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's findings?
explanation: CF commonly causes congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens → obstructive oligo/azoospermia with abnormal semen parameters; other options don't fit (AIS has female phenotype; Kallmann causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; Sertoli-cell only causes azoospermia).
educational_objective: CF can cause male infertility via absent vas deferens and abnormal semen parameters.

question: A 33-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of heat intolerance, palpitations, and weight loss despite an increased appetite. On examination, she has a fine tremor, moist skin, and a non-tender thyroid gland. Laboratory studies show suppressed TSH and elevated free thyroxine (T4). Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism of this patient's condition?
explanation: Graves disease: TSI (TSH-receptor–stimulating IgG) stimulates thyroid hormone production; painless thyroiditis would have low uptake and tender may be absent but often postpartum.
educational_objective: Graves disease is caused by TSH-receptor–stimulating antibodies.

question: A 40-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of fever, chills, and a productive cough. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 20 years. His temperature is 38.8°C (102°F), pulse is 100/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Lung examination shows crackles in the right lower lung field. Chest x-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

options.A: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
options.B: Inferior root of the ansa cervicalis

explanation: The most common cause of lobar community-acquired pneumonia with acute fever, productive cough, and focal crackles is S. pneumoniae.
educational_objective: Typical CAP is most often due to S. pneumoniae.

question: A 27-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. She also has occasional regurgitation of undigested food and halitosis. A barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus with an area of smooth tapering at the distal end. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?
explanation: Achalasia results from loss of inhibitory (NO, VIP) ganglion cells in the Auerbach plexus, causing LES failure to relax and aperistalsis.
educational_objective: Achalasia is due to degeneration of inhibitory myenteric neurons.

question: An 8-year-old girl is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. She is at the 50th percentile for height and 60th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows breast bud development and a few pubic hairs. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial response by the physician?
explanation: Breast budding with sparse pubic hair = Tanner stage 2, normal for age 8–13.
educational_objective: Tanner stage 2 at age 8 is normal pubertal development.

question: A 44-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasingly severe pain and swelling of his knuckles and knees during the past month. Laboratory studies show an increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate and serum rheumatoid factor. The patient improves after treatment with ibuprofen for 2 weeks. Which of the following sets of findings in plasma is most likely after 2 weeks of this therapy?
explanation: NSAIDs (COX inhibitors) block conversion of arachidonic acid to PGH₂ → ↓PGE₂; arachidonic acid accumulates and may be shunted to leukotrienes (↑LTC₄).
educational_objective: COX inhibition decreases prostaglandins, increases AA and leukotriene shunting.

question: A 55-year-old African American man with hypertension is asked by a hospital public relations representative if he will allow filming of his next visit with the physician for a broadcast to raise public awareness of hypertension. After full disclosure, the patient consents. Immediately after filming, he tells the physician that he does not want his medical condition made public. Which of the following is the most appropriate response by the physician?
explanation: Consent for recording/broadcast can be rescinded; the physician should ensure it is withdrawn. (Among options, directing cancellation through PR is the actionable step provided.)
educational_objective: Patients may withdraw consent for recording; arrangements should honor withdrawal.

question: During an experiment, an investigator observes that glutamate depolarizes cells through both NMDA and non-NMDA receptors. The initial depolarization phase of a glutamate-induced fast excitatory postsynaptic potential is generally mediated by activation of non-NMDA-type glutamate receptors. Which of the following best explains this finding?
explanation: At resting potentials, NMDA channels are Mg²⁺-blocked and require prior depolarization (often via AMPA/kainate) to relieve the block.
educational_objective: Initial EPSP is via AMPA/kainate because NMDA is Mg²⁺-blocked at rest.

question: A 50-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital because of a 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and upper abdominal pain that radiates to her back. She was diagnosed with HIV infection 3 months ago and has been adherent with her antiretroviral regimen. Her CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 400/mm³, and plasma HIV viral load is 590 copies/mL. Serum amylase is 450 U/L. The most likely cause of these findings is an adverse effect of which of the following drugs?
explanation: Didanosine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor notable for dose-limiting pancreatitis. The timing (recent ART start), abdominal pain radiating to the back, and high amylase fit this adverse effect.
educational_objective: Recognize didanosine-induced pancreatitis in patients on ART.

question: A 3-year-old boy who recently immigrated to the USA is brought to the physician because of skeletal deformities and failure to thrive. He has frontal bossing, flattening of the skull, enamel defects, flaring of the rib cage, and bowed legs. Serum calcium and phosphorus concentrations are below the reference range. If the bone were examined, which of the following findings would be most likely?
explanation: Nutritional rickets shows defective mineralization with accumulation of osteoid and widened, irregular growth plates due to cartilage overgrowth and poor endochondral ossification; options given do not match classic rickets histology.
educational_objective: Rickets causes excess osteoid and disorganized, widened growth plates from failed mineralization.

question: A 74-year-old woman with mild dementia is admitted to the hospital because of congestive heart failure and angina pectoris that has progressed despite maximal medical therapy. She has had three myocardial infarctions during the past 3 years. The physician recommends coronary angiography and angioplasty. The patient states that she wants to go home and does not want any medical procedures. On questioning, the patient does not know the date, the name of the hospital, or the name of her nurse who had just introduced himself. It would be most appropriate for the physician to question this patient's capacity to make a decision regarding her medical care if mental status examination showed which of the following findings?
explanation: Decision-making capacity requires understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and expressing a choice. Severe disorientation impairs understanding/appreciation of the situation and can indicate lack of capacity. Poor serial 7s or recall alone, or depressed mood, do not automatically negate capacity.
educational_objective: Assess capacity based on understanding/appreciation; severe disorientation warrants questioning capacity.

question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-hour history of severe fatigue and dizziness. He has had profuse, watery diarrhea for 8 hours despite no oral intake. A Gram stain of the stool shows predominant gram-negative, comma-shaped bacteria with no erythrocytes or leukocytes. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of the toxin that caused these findings?
explanation: Cholera toxin ADP-ribosylates Gsα, persistently activating adenylyl cyclase → ↑cAMP → massive Cl⁻ and water secretion, causing voluminous watery diarrhea without fecal WBCs/RBCs.
educational_objective: Vibrio cholerae toxin increases cAMP via Gs ADP-ribosylation.

question: A 55-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of bone pain. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus and has been receiving hemodialysis for 5 years. Laboratory studies show: calcium 8.2 mg/dL, phosphorus 8 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 1380 U/L. This patient's bone pain is most likely caused by which of the following changes in serum concentrations?
explanation: Chronic kidney disease causes phosphate retention and ↓1,25-(OH)₂D → hypocalcemia → secondary hyperparathyroidism (renal osteodystrophy), with high ALP from high bone turnover.
educational_objective: CKD leads to secondary hyperparathyroidism causing high-turnover bone pain.

question: An investigator is studying the regulation of pulmonary lymphatic flow in an animal model. Drugs may be injected into the pulmonary artery and inspired gas mixtures altered at the ventilator. Timed collection of lymph from catheters is used to calculate lymphatic flow. Which of the following interventions will most likely increase the flow of pulmonary lymph in these animals?
explanation: Hypoxia causes hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, raising pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure and transudation, thereby increasing lymph flow. Albumin raises oncotic pressure (↓lymph); brief saline likely minimal; endothelin/phenylephrine effects are less consistent than global hypoxia in this model.
educational_objective: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction increases filtration and lymph flow.

question: A 45-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 45 minutes after she was involved in a motor vehicle collision. She has multiple fractures that require deep sedation before treatment. She is intubated and mechanically ventilated with supplemental oxygen. Positive end- expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 10 cm H₂O is applied. Application of PEEP will most likely prevent which of the following complications in this patient?
explanation: PEEP maintains end-expiratory alveolar patency, preventing atelectasis/collapse; among options, preventing atelectasis is the intended effect (it does not prevent cardiogenic edema, effusions, or tension pneumothorax).
educational_objective: PEEP prevents end-expiratory alveolar collapse (atelectasis).

question: A 61-year-old woman is brought to the physician by her husband because of a 9-month history of increasing forgetfulness. She forgets dinner on the stove and leaves the bathtub running. Her Mini-Mental State Examination score is 22/30. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
explanation: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine) modestly improve cognition/activities in mild–moderate Alzheimer disease.
educational_objective: Use AChE inhibitors for symptomatic treatment of mild–moderate AD.

question: A 25-year-old woman has a 3-week history of bleeding gums while brushing her teeth and easy bruising. She delivered a healthy child 9 months ago and is not taking any medications except for an oral contraceptive. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, MCV 80 µm³, Leukocyte count 8500/mm³, Platelet count 18,500/mm³, Platelets rare but large. Urinalysis is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her condition?

options.A: Binding of nucleosomal histones to the transcript
options.B: Cleavage of the transcript by RNA ligase
options.C: Modification of the transcript by small nuclear ribonucleoproteins
options.D: Transport of the transcript out of the nucleus

explanation: ITP features autoantibodies (often against GpIIb/IIIa) causing immune-mediated platelet destruction with low count and large young platelets on smear.
educational_objective: ITP is due to anti-platelet glycoprotein antibodies causing thrombocytopenia.

question: A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after she fell unconscious. She is intubated on arrival. Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows pH 7.25, PCO₂ 23 mm Hg, PO₂ 78 mm Hg, HCO₃⁻ 10 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely interpretation of the arterial blood gas findings in this patient?
explanation: Low pH with low HCO₃⁻ indicates metabolic acidosis; low PCO₂ reflects respiratory compensation. In this context (coma, acute illness), an increased anion gap metabolic acidosis (e.g., lactic acidosis) is most likely.
educational_objective: Identify primary increased-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation.

question: A healthy 8-year-old boy has a long history of disruptive behavior at school and poor academic performance. He is easily distracted and cannot keep his attention on a topic for long. A drug with which of the following actions is most likely to be useful for this patient?
explanation: Stimulants (methylphenidate/amphetamines) increase synaptic dopamine and norepinephrine to improve attention and behavior in ADHD.
educational_objective: ADHD first-line stimulants increase synaptic DA/NE.

question: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 3-day history of cramping abdominal pain, blood in his urine, and a rash on his arms, legs, and buttocks. He had pharyngitis 2 weeks ago. Physical examination shows a hemorrhagic rash involving the extensor surfaces of the upper and lower extremities and feet. There is generalized abdominal tenderness. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. A renal biopsy specimen shows an increased mesangial matrix that stains positive for IgA on immunofluorescence. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: HSP (IgA vasculitis) causes palpable purpura, arthralgia, abdominal pain, and IgA nephropathy (mesangial IgA deposition), often after URI.
educational_objective: HSP presents with purpura, abdominal pain, and IgA nephropathy after infection.

question: A 33-year-old nulligravid woman comes to the physician with her 35-year-old husband because she has not been able to conceive for 18 months. Previous evaluation of the husband showed no abnormalities. Physical and pelvic examinations show no abnormalities. Examination of an endometrial biopsy specimen shows secretory glands and a decidualized stroma. Which of the following hormonal changes underlies the maturation of this patient's endometrium?
explanation: Progesterone from the corpus luteum converts proliferative endometrium (estrogen-driven) to secretory/decidualized endometrium after ovulation.
educational_objective: Progesterone from the corpus luteum drives secretory endometrial changes.
